IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r8.speaker: بعض أصحاب اللغة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r8.claim: They also read the keys as weighing down the strong group that carries them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r8.anchor: وكذلك قوله سبحانه: ما إن مفاتحه لتنوأ بالعصبة أولي القوة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.claim: He rejects imposing inversion on the Qur’an without sound grounds: poets may reverse wording by mistake, for rhyme or meter, or from poetic necessity.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p125/r11.anchor: وهذا ما لا يجوز لأحد أن يحكم به على كتاب الله عز وجل لو لم يجد له مذهبا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r14.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r14.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r14.claim: The keys weighed down a band means their weight made the band bend under them.

MAJAZ:v1p12/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p12/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p12/r4.claim: Although the keys are grammatically said to burden the band, the intended sense is that the band struggles under the keys’ weight.

BURHAN:v3p289/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p289/r1.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v3p289/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ and others say there is no inversion: the keys weigh down and incline the group carrying them toward collapse.
BURHAN:v3p289/r1.anchor: وقيل لا قلب فيه والمراد والله أعلم أن المفاتح تنوء بالعصبة أي تميلها من نقلها وقد ذكر هذا الفراء وغيره

BURHAN:v3p289/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p289/r2.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v3p289/r2.claim: Ibn Asfur endorses al-Farisi’s analysis: the intransitive ناء becomes transitive with باء, so the keys make the group lean under their weight; this regular construction is preferable to unlicensed inversion.
BURHAN:v3p289/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور والصحيح ما ذهب إليه الفارسي أنها بالنقل ولا قلب والفعل غير متعد فصار متعديا بالباء

ITQAN:v2p373/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p373/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p373/r3.claim: لتنوء بالعصبة means to weigh heavily; a line by Imruʾ al-Qays supports the sense.
ITQAN:v2p373/r3.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال لتثقل أما سمعت قول امرئ القيس

DAMGHANI:v1p350/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r15.claim: Farah can mean boastful exuberance and arrogance, which God dislikes; the cited passages gloss it as bطر.
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r15.anchor: الفرح والبطر والمرح قوله تعالى في سورة القصص انه لا يحب الفرحين

STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r13.claim: Moses' contemporary Korah exemplifies wickedness, worldly extravagance, and pride.
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r13.anchor: Moses’ contemporary Korah is presented as the epitome of wickedness and worldly extravagance and pride.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.claim: The fate of a wealthy Jewish capitalist shows that God grants favors, though the wretched attribute them to their own ability and idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.anchor: The fate of a capitalist Jew is mentioned.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r6.claim: Qārūn is a foreign proper name and is indeclinable for foreignness and proper-name status; “from his people” may mean one who believed in Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r6.anchor: وقارون أعجمي: منع الصرف للعجمة والعلمية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Qārūn was an Israelite by consensus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهو إسرائيلي بإجماع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r8.claim: Among conflicting genealogies, the strongest is Ibn ʿAbbās's report that Qārūn was Moses's cousin, son of Yishhar, son of Qāhith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r8.anchor: وأولاها: ما قاله ابن عباس أنه ابن عمه، وهو قارون ابن يصهر بن قاهث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r9.claim: Qārūn was called al-Munawwar for his handsome appearance, knew and recited the Torah best among the Israelites, then became a hypocrite like al-Sāmirī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r9.anchor: وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته، وكان أحفظ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r10.claim: His transgressions included unbelief, arrogance, envy of Moses's prophethood and Aaron's sacrificial role, oppression under Pharaoh, and arranging a woman's false accusation against Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r10.anchor: فبغى عليهم: ذكروا من أنواع بغيه الكفر والكبر، وحسده لموسى على النبوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r11.claim: Another reported sign of his arrogance was adding a handspan to his clothes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r11.anchor: ومن تكبره أن زاد في ثيابه شبرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r12.claim: One view says God gave him a treasure of Joseph; another says his wealth was called treasure because he withheld its zakāt, beginning his hostility toward Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r12.anchor: آتيناه من الكنوز، قيل: أظفره الله بكنز من كنوز يوسف عليه السلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p322#2/r13.claim: The relative mā is connected to inna and its complements; al-Naḥḥās cites al-Akhfash against the Kūfan restriction on such relative clauses.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r1.claim: The keys are variously glossed as treasury keys, the treasuries themselves, or their containers; al-Aʿmash reads “his keys.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r1.anchor: وقالوا هنا: مقاليد خزائنه. وقال السدي: هي الخزائن نفسها. وقال الضحاك: ظروفه وأوعيته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r2.claim: Reports of the number of keys were so extravagant that the author omits them as lies or near-lies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r2.anchor: وذكروا من كثرة مفاتحه ما هو كذب، أو يقارب الكذب، فلم أكتبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r3.claim: Abū Zayd defines nāʾa bi-l-ʿamal as rising while bearing it; cited poetry illustrates the verb's sense of bearing a heavy load.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r3.anchor:
قال أبو زيد:
نؤت بالعمل إذا نهضت به.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the syntax as inversion: the keys weigh down the group, as though the text said the group bears them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو مقلوب وأصله: لتنوء بها العصبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r5.claim: The bāʾ is causative: the keys make the group heavy, a construction also attributed to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Farrāʾ, and preferred by al-Naḥḥās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r5.anchor: والصحيح أن الباء للتعدية، أي لتنيء العصبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r6.claim: The causative sense is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and al-Suddī; Arabs say a load weighs down a camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r6.anchor: وروي معناه عن ابن عباس وأبي صالح والسدي، وتقول العرب: ناء الحمل بالبعير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows the keys to be the grammatical subject: they rise with effort when the carrier lifts them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويمكن أن يسند تنوء إلى المفاتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r8.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r8.claim: Budayl reads the verb in masculine singular, explained by an omitted masculine noun such as the load of the keys; al-Zamakhsharī offers a related attachment explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r8.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة: لينوء، بالياء، وتذكيره راعى المضاف المحذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī reports Budayl's singular “key,” which removes the need to explain the masculine verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r9.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو الداني إن بديل بن ميسرة قرأ: ما إن مفتاحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan are also cited for taking the keys to mean the wealth itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p323/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والحسن: أن المفاتح هي الأموال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that forty strong men carried Qārūn's treasuries, said here to number four hundred thousand, ten thousand per carrier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت خزائنه تحملها أربعون أقوياء، وكانت أربعمائة ألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r2.claim: Abū Muslim takes the keys as knowledge and exhaustive awareness, like God's “keys of the unseen”; guarding so many kinds of treasure burdens its keepers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r2.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: المراد من المفاتح: العلم والإحاطة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r3.claim: Qārūn's people condemn the arrogant, intoxicating joy of someone absorbed in worldly success and heedless of the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r3.anchor: إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح: نهوه عن الفرح المطغي الذي هو انهماك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r4.claim: Abū al-Ṭayyib's verse illustrates that joy in a passing fortune is grief because its owner knows it will depart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r4.anchor:
وقال أبو الطيب:
أشد الغم عندي في سرور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes id dependent on the burdening of the keys; the author rejects this because that burden is not confined to the time of the rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ومحل إذ منصوب بتنوء. انتهى، وهذا ضعيف جدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya links id to Qārūn's transgression, while al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ propose other links; the author finds these timing connections weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: متعلق بقوله: فبغى عليهم، وهو ضعيف أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r7.claim: The author supplies an omitted act of showing off: Qārūn displayed pride in his treasures when his people told him not to rejoice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r7.anchor: ويظهر أن يكون تقديره: فأظهر التفاخر والفرح بما أوتي من الكنوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r8.claim: The warning against rejoicing recalls 57:23; an Arab poem praises not exulting when fortune smiles or despairing when it turns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r8.anchor: وقال تعالى: ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم ، والعرب تمدح بترك الفرح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r9.speaker: عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r9.claim: ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥijāzī reports the reading al-fāriḥīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r9.anchor: وقرىء: الفارحين، حكاه عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r10.claim: “God does not love” describes an act, not an attribute of essence: here it means He does not extend blessing and mercy to the arrogant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r10.anchor: ولا يحب: صفة فعل، لا صفة ذات، بمعنى الإرادة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p567/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p567/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p567/r9.claim: The passage resumes the topic from verse 61 after the secondary discussion of polytheism concludes at verse 75; verses 76–84 continue the original theme.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p567/r9.anchor: The succeeding topic is connected to verse 61.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r1.claim: The verse says Qarun belonged to Moses' people, which may imply that he believed in Moses; it may instead indicate kinship.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r1.anchor: ظاهر ذلك يدل على أنه كان ممن قد أمن به

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Qarun was Moses' cousin, giving their shared ancestry through Yishar, Qohath, and Levi.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي : إنه كان ابن عم موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says Qarun was Moses' paternal uncle, based on their shared ancestry through Yishar and Qohath.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق إنه كان عم موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun was Moses' maternal cousin.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه كان ابن خالته

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r5.claim: Qarun was called al-Munawwar for his handsome appearance and was Israel's foremost reciter of the Torah, but he became a hypocrite like al-Samiri.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r5.anchor: ثم قيل إنه كان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته وكان أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r6.claim: One explanation is that Qarun's wealth made him despise the poor, disregard their right as fellow believers, and fail to honor them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r6.anchor: أنه استخف بالفقراء ولم يرع لهم حق الإيمان ولا عظمهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that Qarun acted unjustly; Pharaoh had appointed him over the Israelites, whom he then oppressed.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r7.anchor: أنه من الظلم ، قيل ملكه فرعون على

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r8.claim: Al-Qaffal explains that Qarun sought superiority over his people and wanted them subjected to him.

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says Qarun transgressed, overpowered his people, and did not deal fairly with them.

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that Qarun acted tyrannically and arrogantly toward his people and angered them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس : تجبر وتكبر عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r11.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r11.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says Qarun's transgression was to wear clothes a span longer than his people's, an act of arrogance.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r11.anchor: قال شهر بن حوشب : بغيه عليهم أنه زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r12.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi says Qarun envied Aaron's high-priestly office: Moses had prophecy and Aaron the priesthood, altar, and offerings, while Qarun felt he had no position.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r12.anchor: قال الكلبي : بغيه عليهم أنه حسد هرون على الحبورة

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r13.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r13.claim: In al-Kalbi's account, Moses tested the leaders' rods by God's command; Aaron's almond-wood rod sprouted green leaves overnight, but Qarun called the sign magic and withdrew with many followers.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r13.anchor: قال الكلبي : بغيه عليهم أنه حسد هرون على الحبورة

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r14.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r14.claim: Al-Kalbi's story continues that Aaron received the priesthood, altar, and offerings; Israelites brought him gifts, which a heavenly fire consumed, while wealthy Qarun separated with many Israelite followers.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r14.anchor: قال الكلبي : بغيه عليهم أنه حسد هرون على الحبورة

RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r15.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r15.claim: Abu Umama al-Bahili reports that the Prophet said Qarun was among the seventy chosen ones who heard God's speech; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v25p12#2/r15.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة الباهلي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r1.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r1.claim: Al-Kaʿbi objects that if God does not give illicit wealth, the phrase “We gave him” conflicts with that principle; al-Razi replies that the text does not establish Qarun's wealth was illicit, and it could have come from previous kings' treasure, inheritance, or trade.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r1.anchor: قال الكعبي : ألستم تقولون إن الله لا يعطي الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r2.claim: Mafātih is the plural of maftaḥ, with a kasra on the mīm, meaning keys; it is also said to mean stores, whose singular would be maftaḥ with a fatḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r2.anchor: المفاتح جمع مفتح بكسر الميم وهو ما يفتح به

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r3.claim: The idiom nāʾa bihi al-ḥiml means that a load became so heavy it made its bearer lean.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r3.anchor: ويقال ناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r4.claim: ʿUṣba means a large group and is synonymous with ʿiṣāba; the brothers of Joseph were ten, since Joseph and his brother were not with them.

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r5.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r5.claim: One interpretation takes the keys literally: each storehouse had a finger-sized key made of camel hide, and sixty camels carried the keys when Qarun rode.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r5.anchor: قالوا كانت مفاتيحه من جلود الإبل وكل مفتاح مثل إصبع

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r6.claim: Critics of the literal-key view object that one person's wealth would not require so many keys, and that buried treasure would have no keys.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من طعن في هذا القول

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r7.claim: Al-Razi answers that a great volume of goods rather than coin could require many keys; the report of sixty loads is not in the Quran and should not be accepted, while numerous distinct keys would be hard for a group to track.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r7.anchor: أن المال إذا كان من جنس العروض

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r8.claim: Although “treasures” conventionally means wealth stored underground, it can also denote collected wealth kept in places secured by locks.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r8.anchor: أن ظاهر الكنز وإن كان من جهة العرف ما قالوا فقد يقع على المال المجموع في المواضع التي عليها أغلاق

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan prefer taking the keys metaphorically as the wealth itself, which they consider clearer and farther from the objections; Ibn Abbas says forty strong men carried Qarun's treasuries, which numbered four hundred thousand, ten thousand per carrier.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r9.anchor: وهو اختيار ابن عباس والحسن أن تحمل المفاتح على نفس المال

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r10.claim: Abu Muslim takes mafātih to mean knowledge and comprehensive access, as in “with Him are the keys of the unseen”; Qarun's varied, abundant treasures burdened their keepers' ability to preserve and oversee them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r10.anchor: اختيار أبي مسلم : أن المراد من المفاتح

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r11.claim: Qarun's people tell him not to rejoice with such vanity and worldly attachment that it distracts him altogether from the Hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r11.anchor: والمراد لا يلحقه من البطر والتمسك بالدنيا ما يلهيه عن أمر الآخرة أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r12.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r12.claim: Some say only someone content with and settled in worldly life rejoices in it; one who knows he will soon leave does not, as al-Mutanabbi aptly observed.
RAZI-FULL:v25p13/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه لا يفرح بالدنيا إلا من رضي بها

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r1.claim: Razi calls the Qur'anic wording in 57:23 a more eloquent and concise expression than the preceding poetic line about worldly joy.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r1.anchor: لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما ءاتاكم

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun's joy was shirk because it came without fear of God's punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان فرحه ذلك شركا

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r1.claim: Every particle witnesses divine unity to the knower; attaining true witnessing and tawhid comes through the best remembrance, occupied with it through day and night.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r1.anchor: والوصول إلى هذا الشهود والتوحيد الحقيقي إنما هو بخير الأذكار أي بالاشتغال به

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r2.speaker: الشيخ المغربي
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r2.claim: The Moroccan shaykh counsels seeking with a longing eye, since the Beloved eventually manifests to the one who seeks to see.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r2.anchor:
قال الشيخ المغربي :
تخست ديده طلب كن س آنكهي ديدار

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r3.claim: Qarun is a non-Arabic name like Harun, so it is indeclinable.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r3.anchor: اسم أعجمي كهارون فلذلك لم ينصرف

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r4.claim: Qarun was Moses' cousin, believed in him, taught the Israelites the Torah, and was nicknamed the shining one for his beauty, but wealth turned him into a hypocrite like the Samaritan.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r4.anchor: كان ابن عمه يصهر بن قاهش بن لاوي بن يعقوب وموسى بن عمران ابن قاهش

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r5.claim: Qarun was among those who believed in Moses and taught the Israelites the Torah, then wealth changed his state and made him hypocritical like the Samaritan.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r5.anchor: وكان ممن آمن به وأقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته ثم تغير حاله بسبب الغنى

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r6.claim: Al-Raghib defines baghy as seeking to go beyond moderation, whether or not one succeeds, and associates it with arrogance and overstepping one's station.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : البغي طلب تجاوز الاقتصاد فيما يتحرى تجاوزه أو لم يتجاوزه

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r7.claim: Qarun sought superiority over his people and wanted them under his command; wealth's abundance led to arrogance, pride, conceit, rebellion, and rejection of advice.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r7.anchor: والمعنى فطلب الفضل عليهم وأن يكونوا تحت أمره وليس ببعيد فإن كثرة المال

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r8.claim: A hadith warns that God will not look on Judgment Day at someone who drags his robe out of pride.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لا ينظر الله يوم القيامة إلى من جر ثوبه خيلاء"

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r9.claim: A report urges people to show kindness to the poor before their own fortunes change, since the poor will have great standing in the afterlife and may lead their benefactors to Paradise.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : "اتخذوا الأيادي عند الفقراء قبل أن تجيء دولتهم"

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r10.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r10.claim: Reports say Qarun's first act of rebellion was refusing God's command for Israelites to attach four sky-colored threads to their garments, intended to remind them of revelation and obedience.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r10.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار : كان أول طغيانه وعصيانه أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى موسى عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r11.claim: God explains that a small command is not insignificant: those who disobey a small command will not obey a great one.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r11.anchor: فقال : يا موسى إن الصغير من أمري ليس بصغير

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r12.claim: Qarun refused the threads, saying masters use such things to distinguish themselves from servants; this began his transgression.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r12.anchor: وامتنع قارون وقال : إنما يفعل هذا الأرباب بعبيدهم لكي يتميزوا من غيرهم

BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r13.claim: After the sea crossing, the priestly office of the altar was given to Aaron, setting up Qarun's later jealousy.
BURSEVI:v6p311#3/r13.anchor: ولما عبروا البحر جعلت حبورة القربان وهي رياسة المذبح في هارون

BURSEVI:v6p312/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r1.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p312/r1.claim: Kashf al-Asrar explains that Israelites brought sacrificial offerings to Aaron, who placed them on the altar, where heavenly fire consumed them.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r1.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (در رياست مذبح آن بودكه بني إسرائيل قربان

BURSEVI:v6p312/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r2.claim: Qarun envied Aaron's priesthood and complained that Moses had prophecy, Aaron priesthood, and he himself had no office despite teaching Torah.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r2.anchor: فحسده قارون وقال : يا موسى لك الرسالة ولهارون الحبورة ولست في شيء

BURSEVI:v6p312/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r3.claim: Moses replied that God, not Moses, had bestowed Aaron's office; Qarun demanded proof and dismissed the miracle of Aaron's budding staff as magic.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r3.anchor: قال موسى : ما أنا جعلتها في هارون بل الله جعلها من فضله

BURSEVI:v6p312/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r4.claim: Moses had the Israelites leave their staffs overnight in the tent where revelation descended; Aaron's almond staff leafed green, but Qarun called it magic and withdrew with followers.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r4.anchor: فأمر موسى رؤساء بني إسرائيل بوضع عصيهم في القبة التي

BURSEVI:v6p312/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r5.claim: Moses tried to deal gently with Qarun because of kinship, but Qarun ignored him, harmed him, and grew more arrogant and rebellious.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r5.anchor: وجعل موسى يداريه لما بينهما من القرابة وهو لا يلتفت إليه بل يؤذيه ولا يزيد إلا تجبرا وبغيا

BURSEVI:v6p312/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p312/r6.claim: Al-Raghib defines kanz as collecting wealth in heaps and storing it, from the expression for heaping dates in a container.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : الكنز جمع المال بعضه فوق بعض وحفظه

BURSEVI:v6p312/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r7.claim: Rikaz is wealth embedded in earth, whether naturally formed or placed there; a mineral deposit is naturally formed, while a treasure is placed there.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r7.anchor: والفرق بين الركاز والمعدن والكنز أن الركاز هو المال المركوز في الأرض مخلوقا كان أو موضوعا

BURSEVI:v6p312/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r8.claim: Mafātiḥ is the plural of maftaḥ, with kasra, meaning the keys used to open chests.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r8.anchor: جمع مفتح بالكسر ما يفتح به أي مفاتح صناديقه

BURSEVI:v6p312/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r9.claim: The relative clause about the keys is the second object of āteynāhu.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r9.anchor: خبر أن والجملة صلة ما وهو ثاني مفعولي آتينا

BURSEVI:v6p312/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p312/r10.claim: To be burdened by a load means it weighs and bends its bearer; the bā is causative.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r10.anchor: وناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله فالباء للتعدية

BURSEVI:v6p312/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r11.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p312/r11.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that ʿuṣbah is a mutually supporting group.

BURSEVI:v6p312/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p312/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p312/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the group here consisted of forty men; Qarun's 400,000 keys were carried ten thousand to each man.
BURSEVI:v6p312/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : العصبة في هذا الموضع أربعون رجلا

BURSEVI:v6p313/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r1.claim: The keys' weight made their bearers bend and lean under the load.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r1.anchor: والمعنى لتثقلهم وتميل بهم إذا حملوها لثقلها

BURSEVI:v6p313/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p313/r2.claim: A report said to be found in the Gospel describes Qarun's keys as finger-sized, each opening a treasure; another account says he carried them everywhere and changed the material from iron to wood to cowhide as they grew too heavy.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتح خزائن قارون

BURSEVI:v6p313/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r3.claim: The phrase idh qāla is in the accusative, attached to tanūʾu.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r3.anchor: منصوب بتنوء يعني موسى وبني إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v6p313/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r4.claim: The speakers advising Qarun may be Moses and the Israelites collectively, or Moses alone offering counsel.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r4.anchor: يعني موسى وبني إسرائيل وقيل : قاله موسى وحده بطريق النصيحة

BURSEVI:v6p313/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r5.claim: The counsel means not to rejoice in worldly wealth; worldly joy is expansive delight in immediate pleasures, especially bodily pleasures.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r5.anchor: (شادي مكن بمال دنيا) والفرح انشراح الصدر بلذة عاجلة

BURSEVI:v6p313/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r6.claim: Worldly joy is blameworthy because it follows attachment and approval of the world and forgetfulness that its pleasures must pass; knowing their transience necessarily brings grief.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r6.anchor: والفرح في الدنيا مذموم مطلقا لأنه نتيجة حبها والرضى بها والذهول عن ذهابها

BURSEVI:v6p313/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r7.claim: The warning echoes the command not to grieve over what passed or rejoice over what was given.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r7.anchor: ولذا قال تعالى : {لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بمآ ءاتااكم}

BURSEVI:v6p313/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r8.claim: The only permitted rejoicing is in God's grace and mercy and the believers' victory by God's help.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r8.anchor: ولم يرخص في الفرح إلا في قوله : {قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذالك فليفرحوا}

BURSEVI:v6p313/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r9.claim: Here, those who rejoice are people exulting in worldly ornaments, which God dislikes.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r9.anchor: أي بزخارف الدنيا فإن الدنيا مبغوضة عند الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v6p313/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313/r10.claim: God loves those who rejoice in worship and seek afterlife happiness.
BURSEVI:v6p313/r10.anchor: وإنما يحب من يفرح بإقامة العبودية وطلب السعادة الأخروية

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r1.claim: The Bible tells of Korah, a prominent Israelite who rebelled against Moses; the source also refers to 29:39.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r1.anchor: In the Bible the story of Korah (Qārūn), a prominent Israelite who rebelled against Moses, is told in Numbers 16

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r2.claim: Korah’s worldly station illustrates that wealth and power cannot save one from God’s punishment, the lesson of verse 60.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r2.anchor: Korah’s station in life exemplifies the lesson of v. 60, namely, that wealth and power in the world will not save one

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r3.claim: Transgression may mean Korah’s disbelief in God.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r3.anchor: Transgressed renders baghā, which can refer to his disbelief in God (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r4.claim: Another gloss is Korah’s contempt for others, arising from his great wealth.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r4.anchor: or his contemptuous attitude toward others stemming from his great wealth (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r5.claim: Transgression may also refer to failing to give required charity, flaunting his wealth, or mistreating people.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r5.anchor: it may point to his failure to give charity in accordance with proper belief, flaunting his wealth, or mistreating people (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r6.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r6.claim: Some attribute Korah’s attitude and actions partly to jealousy of Moses and Aaron and the station God gave them.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r6.anchor: Some say that his attitude and actions stemmed partly from his jealousy of Moses and Aaron and the station that God had bestowed upon them.

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r7.claim: One interpretation warns Korah not to be wanton or miserly with his wealth, withholding what is due to others.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r7.anchor: he should not be wanton or miserly with this wealth, denying it from those who have a right to some of it (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r8.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r8.claim: Another interpretation warns against celebrating worldly things as though the Hereafter had no consequences.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r8.anchor: he should not celebrate the things of this world as if there were no consequences in the Hereafter (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r9.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r9.claim: The keys may be literal keys to so many treasures that one person could not carry them.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r9.anchor: keys to manifold treasures so numerous that a single man could not carry them

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r10.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r10.claim: Alternatively, the burden may be the knowledge required to manage so many different keys, which were difficult to count or track.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r10.anchor: the nature of the burden was one of knowledge—he had so many different keys for different treasures they were difficult to count or keep track of

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r11.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that the keys were carried together with the treasures.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r11.anchor: or that the keys were carried along with the treasures

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r12.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r12.claim: The keys may signify knowledge: Korah knew so many fields that the combined skills of a group could not equal his.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r12.anchor: these were keys of knowledge, meaning that Korah was proficient and knowledgeable in so many different areas

STUDYQURAN:28:76/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r13.claim: The image of keys for knowledge is linked to God’s keys of the Unseen in 6:59.
STUDYQURAN:28:76/r13.anchor: God’s Knowledge of the Unseen in 6:59

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives Qarun’s lineage through Yishhar and Qahith and identifies him as Moses’ cousin; he prefers Ibn Jurayj’s genealogy, which most scholars follow.
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r1.anchor: كان من عشيرة موسى بن عمران النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو ابن عمه لأبيه وأمه

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies Qarun as a cousin of Moses, descended from Qahith, and the report corrects the transmitted name “Yisfar” to “Yishhar” and “ʿUmar” to “ʿImran.”
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} [القصص: 76] قال: ابن عمه ابن أخي أبيه

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Yishhar fathered both ʿImran and Qarun, making Qarun Moses’ paternal uncle and full brother of his father.
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r3.anchor: وأما ابن إسحاق فإن ابن حميد حدثنا قال: ثنا سلمة، عنه أن يصهر بن قاهث

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that Qarun was Moses’ cousin.
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} [القصص: 76] قال: كان ابن عم موسى

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r5.claim: Qatāda says Qarun was Moses’ cousin, was called al-Munawwar for his beautiful Torah recitation, but hypocritically opposed Moses like al-Samiri and was destroyed by arrogance.
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} [القصص: 76] : كنا نحدث أنه كان ابن عمه أخي أبيه

TAB-FULL:v18p309/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that Qarun was Moses’ cousin and then transgressed against him.
TAB-FULL:v18p309/r6.anchor: عن سفيان، عن سماك، عن إبراهيم، " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} [القصص: 76] قال: كان ابن عمه فبغى عليه

TAB-FULL:v18p311/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm again identifies Qarun as Moses’ cousin.
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم، " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} [القصص: 76] قال: كان ابن عمه

TAB-FULL:v18p311/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r2.speaker: مالك بن دينار
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r2.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār says he had heard that Moses was Qarun’s cousin.
TAB-FULL:v18p311/r2.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار، قال: «بلغني أن موسى بن عمران كان ابن عم قارون»

TAB-FULL:v18p312/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r1.claim: Qarun exceeded proper bounds against his people through pride and tyranny.
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r1.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب، " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم} [القصص: 76] قال: زاد عليهم في الثياب

TAB-FULL:v18p312/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r2.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r2.claim: One explanation is that Qarun’s transgression was adding a handspan to the length of his clothes.
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r2.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب، " {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم} [القصص: 76] قال: زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا

TAB-FULL:v18p312/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r3.claim: Qatāda says Qarun transgressed through the abundance of his wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p312/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «إنما بغى عليهم بكثرة ماله»

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r1.claim: The “mafātiḥ” are keys, the plural of “maftaḥ,” used to open doors; another view takes them to mean storehouses.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r1.anchor: ذكر من قال ما قلنا في معنى مفاتح

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r2.claim: Some exegetes take “mafātiḥ” here to mean storehouses that weigh down the band.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قوله: " {ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: كانت خزائنه تحمل على أربعين بغلا

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r3.speaker: خيثمة
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r3.claim: Khathīma reports that Qarun’s leather keys, each finger-sized and for a separate treasure, were carried on sixty mules.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r3.anchor: عن خيثمة، قال: «كانت مفاتح قارون تحمل على ستين بغلا

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r4.speaker: منصور
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r4.claim: Manṣūr reports that the Gospel described Qarun’s keys as weighing sixty white, marked mules, with each finger-sized key opening a separate treasure.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r4.anchor: عن منصور، عن خيثمة، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the keys were made of camel hide.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «كانت المفاتح من جلود الإبل»

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid describes the leather keys as resembling the keys of stringed instruments.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، " {وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: مفاتح من جلود كمفاتح العيدان

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r7.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ takes the “keys” to mean storehouses, which he says were carried on forty mules.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قوله: " {ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: كانت خزائنه تحمل على أربعين بغلا

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the keys as Qarun’s containers.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي حجير، عن الضحاك، " {ما إن مفاتحه} [القصص: 76] قال: أوعيته

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “tanūʾu” as “weighs down”; al-Ṭabarī explains “ʿuṣbah” as a group.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: لتثقل بالعصبة

TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r10.claim: Some exegetes say the keys weighed down a band of forty men.
TAB-FULL:v18p312#2/r10.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كانت مفاتحه تنوء بعصبة مبلغ عددها أربعون رجلا

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the band consisted of forty men.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح، قوله: " {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: أربعون رجلا

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r2.claim: Qatāda says the band could number anywhere from ten to forty.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: ذكر لنا أن العصبة ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that people say forty men moved the keys because there were so many of them.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة} [القصص: 76] : يزعمون أن العصبة أربعون رجلا

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the band as forty men.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة} [القصص: 76] قال: أربعون رجلا

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r5.speaker: خيثمة
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r5.claim: A further report gives sixty as the band’s number and says the keys were transported on sixty mules.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: ستون، وقال: كانت مفاتحه تحمل على ستين بغلا. حدثنا كذلك ابن وكيع، قال: ثنا أبي، عن الأعمش، عن خيثمة

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r6.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives the band as three people.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، " {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: العصبة: ثلاثة

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās defines a band as three to ten people.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، " {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] قال: العصبة: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

TAB-FULL:v18p315/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r8.claim: Mujāhid gives the band as ten to fifteen people in one report and fifteen men in another.
TAB-FULL:v18p315/r8.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {أولي القوة} [القصص: 76] قال: خمسة عشر

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r2.claim: Mujāhid interprets the phrase as fifteen men.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {أولي القوة} [القصص: 76] قال: خمسة عشر

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r3.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r3.claim: Some Basran grammarians treat the wording as a reversal: it means the strong band is burdened by the keys, a construction also illustrated by the cited poetry.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r3.anchor: مجاز ذلك: ما إن العصبة ذوي القوة لتنوء بمفاتح نعمه

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r4.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r4.claim: A Basran example says a woman’s rump “weighs her down,” though she in fact bears its weight; the apparent direction is reversed.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r4.anchor: ويقال في الكلام: إنها لتنوء بها عجيزتها، وإنما هو: تنوء بعجيزتها

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r5.speaker: شاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r5.claim: An anonymous line illustrates the reversed construction: one says “I ransomed him with his own self and wealth,” meaning with my own life and wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: [البحر الوافر] فديت بنفسه نفسي ومالي … وما آلوك إلا ما أطيق

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r6.speaker: شاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r6.claim: An anonymous verse says the lances suffer from the red warriors, while its intended sense is that the warriors suffer from lances; “horses” here means men.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r6.anchor: وقال آخر: [البحر الطويل] وتركب خيلا لا هوادة بينها … وتشقى الرماح بالضياطرة الحمر

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r7.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r7.claim: A Basran notes that beginning “inna” after “mā” is unusual, though 62:8 offers a parallel construction.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r7.anchor: وقال آخر منهم {ما إن مفاتحه} [القصص: 76] قال: وهذا موضع لا يكاد يبتدأ فيه «إن»

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r8.speaker: أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r8.claim: Kufan grammarians reject the Basran objection: beginning “inna” after “mā” is allowed, especially with “mā” or “man”; it is less natural with “alladhī,” which does not govern its relative clause.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r8.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من الكوفيين ينكر هذا الذي قاله هذا القائل، وابتداء إن بعد ما

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r9.speaker: رجل من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r9.claim: One grammarian takes the phrase to mean that the keys make the band heavy and lean; with the preposition “bā” the verb means “weigh down,” as in 18:96 and 19:23.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r9.anchor: وقال آخر منهم في قوله: {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] : نوءها بالعصبة: أن تثقلهم

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r10.speaker: شاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r10.claim: An anonymous line says a rump weighs women down, but the intended construction is that they bear the rump’s weight.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r10.anchor: وفي الشعر: [البحر الكامل] تنوء بها فتثقلها عجيزتها

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r11.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r11.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line is another poetic example cited in support of the Arab construction.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r11.anchor: وقال الأعشى: [البحر الكامل] ما كنت في الحرب العوان مغمرا … إذ شب حر وقودها أجذالها

TAB-FULL:v18p317/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r12.speaker: رجل من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r12.claim: Another grammarian says the band itself bears the keys; the expression shifts the verb onto the keys, as in the cited poetic construction.
TAB-FULL:v18p317/r12.anchor: رجل من أهل العربية: ما إن العصبة تنوء

TAB-FULL:v18p319/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r1.claim: An Arabic verse calls a prized object an adornment to the eye; al-Tabari says this proposed sense works only if supported by received usage, otherwise its proponent misunderstands it.
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r1.anchor: إن سراجا لكريم مفخره … تحلى به العين إذا ما تجهره وهو الذي يحلى بالعين

TAB-FULL:v18p319/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r2.claim: The people of strength are people of might; the expression describes the keys weighing down and inclining a strong band. An Arab verse about an archer leaning under a bow illustrates ناء.
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r2.anchor: حتى إذا ما التأمت مواصله … وناء في شق الشمال كاهله يعني: الرامي لما أخذ القوس، ونزع مال عليها.

TAB-FULL:v18p319/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r3.claim: In Arab usage ناءك means أناءك with its initial alif dropped by analogy after ساءك, as مرأني likewise drops the alif of أمرأني after هنأني.
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r3.anchor: ومعناه: ما ساءك وأناءك من ذلك، إلا أنه ألقى الألف لأنه متبع لساءك، كما قالت العرب: أكلت طعاما فهنأني ومرأني

TAB-FULL:v18p319/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the keys weigh down the band over the alternative that the band struggles to lift them: it fits the wording and early authorities, and signals the treasure’s great quantity.
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r4.anchor: وهذا القول الآخر في تأويل قوله: {لتنوء بالعصبة} [القصص: 76] : أولى بالصواب من الأقوال الأخر، لمعنيين

TAB-FULL:v18p319/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r5.claim: An alternative gloss makes the band lift the keys; al-Tabari says this fails to show the great abundance of Qarun’s treasure, since a band could lift few or many keys.
TAB-FULL:v18p319/r5.anchor: قول من قال: معنى ذلك: ما إن العصبة لتنوء بمفاتحه، إنما هو توجيه منهم إلى أن معناه: ما إن العصبة لتنهض بمفاتحه

TAB-FULL:v18p321/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the rejected ‘joyful’ as people who are exuberant or merry.
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله " {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} [القصص: 76] يقول: المرحين

TAB-FULL:v18p321/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r2.claim: Mujahid describes them as ostentatious, boastful and ungrateful for what God gave them.
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} [القصص: 76] قال: المتبذخين الأشرين البطرين، الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم

TAB-FULL:v18p321/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r3.claim: Mujahid also explains the prohibited joy as joy arising from oppression or arrogance.
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r3.anchor: إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} [القصص: 76] قال: هو فرح البغي

TAB-FULL:v18p321/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r4.claim: Qatadah glosses لا تفرح as ‘do not frolic’ and الفرحين as ‘those who frolic.’
TAB-FULL:v18p321/r4.anchor: أي لا تمرح {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} [القصص: 76]

TABATABAI:28:76/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r1.claim: The Qarun narrative follows the polytheists’ fear that following guidance would get them driven from their land: his fate warns them that rejecting God leads to ruin and could befall them too.
TABATABAI:28:76/r1.anchor: بيان قصة قارون من بني إسرائيل ذكرها الله سبحانه بعدما حكى قول المشركين { إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا }

TABATABAI:28:76/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r2.claim: Qarun trusted his own skill, preferred worldly life, and pursued corruption; God sank him and his house, and no group could help or save him.
TABATABAI:28:76/r2.anchor: فأمن العذاب الإلهي وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وبغى الفساد في الأرض فخسف الله به وبداره الأرض

TABATABAI:28:76/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r3.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:76/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines baghy as seeking unjust transgression or domination.
TABATABAI:28:76/r3.anchor: قال في المجمع البغي طلب العتو بغير حق

TABATABAI:28:76/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r4.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:76/r4.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says mafātiḥ and mafātīḥ are plural forms with the same meaning: tools used to unlock things.
TABATABAI:28:76/r4.anchor: قال والمفاتح جمع مفتح والمفاتيح جمع مفتاح ومعناهما واحد وهو عبارة عما يفتح به الأغلاق

TABATABAI:28:76/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r5.claim: Some exegetes take the keys to mean Qarun’s treasure stores, but Tabataba’i rejects that interpretation.
TABATABAI:28:76/r5.anchor: وذكر جمع من المفسرين أن المراد بالمفاتح الخزائن، وليس بذاك

TABATABAI:28:76/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r6.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:76/r6.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines nāʾa bi-ḥimlih as rising under a heavy burden.
TABATABAI:28:76/r6.anchor: قال وناء بحمله ينوء نوءا إذا نهض به مع ثقله عليه

TABATABAI:28:76/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r7.claim: Another lexicographer says the load weighed its bearer down until it tilted him, which Tabataba’i finds more apt here.
TABATABAI:28:76/r7.anchor: وقال غيره ناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله وهو الأوفق للآية

TABATABAI:28:76/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r8.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:76/r8.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines ʿuṣba as a group whose members are closely bound together.
TABATABAI:28:76/r8.anchor: وقال في المجمع أيضا العصبة الجماعة الملتف بعضها ببعض

TABATABAI:28:76/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABATABAI:28:76/r9.claim: Mujāhid says ʿuṣba is a group of ten to fifteen people.
TABATABAI:28:76/r9.anchor: فقيل ما بين عشرة إلى خمسة عشر عن مجاهد

TABATABAI:28:76/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:28:76/r10.claim: Qatāda says ʿuṣba is a group of ten to forty people.
TABATABAI:28:76/r10.anchor: وقيل ما بين عشرة إلى أربعين عن قتادة

TABATABAI:28:76/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r11.speaker: أبو صالح
TABATABAI:28:76/r11.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says ʿuṣba means forty men.
TABATABAI:28:76/r11.anchor: وقيل أربعون رجلا عن أبي صالح

TABATABAI:28:76/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:28:76/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿuṣba means a group of three to ten people.
TABATABAI:28:76/r12.anchor: وقيل ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:28:76/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:76/r13.claim: An unattributed view defines ʿuṣba as a group whose members support one another.
TABATABAI:28:76/r13.anchor: وقيل إنهم الجماعة يتعصب بعضهم لبعض

TABATABAI:28:76/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r14.claim: Joseph’s nine brothers call themselves ʿuṣba, undercutting the earlier estimates of ten to fifteen, ten to forty, or forty people.
TABATABAI:28:76/r14.anchor: ويزيف غير القولين الأخيرين قول إخوة يوسف

TABATABAI:28:76/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76/r15.claim: Rejoicing means excessive worldly delight amounting to arrogant insolence; attachment to worldly pleasure distracts from the afterlife and breeds pride, which is why God does not love such people.
TABATABAI:28:76/r15.anchor: فسر الفرح بالبطر وهو لازم الفرح والسرور المفرط بمتاع الدنيا فإنه لا يخلو من تعلق شديد بالدنيا ينسى الآخرة

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r1.claim: The prohibition on rejoicing is reinforced by the instruction not to exult over what God gave and that God loves no arrogant boaster.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r1.anchor: ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم والله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.claim: The Ibn Abbas story centers on Qarun's wrongdoing against Moses, whereas the Qur'anic account says he wronged the Israelites; the verse also points to learned, acquired know-how, apparently the means of making wealth.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.anchor: على أن رواية ابن عباس تقصص بغيه على موسى عليه السلام والذي تقصه الآيات بغيه على بنى إسرائيل

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.claim: The present Torah recounts the rebellion differently, naming Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and On with 250 leaders who oppose Moses; the cited account is Numbers chapter 16.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.anchor: ففي الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد وأخذ قورح بن بصهار بن نهات بن لاوي وداثان وأبيرام

TABRISI:28:76-82/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82/r10.claim: Baghy is unjustly seeking rebellion; unjust rulers are consequently called bughāt.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r10.anchor: البغي طلب العتو بغير حق ومنه قيل لولاة الجور بغاة

TABRISI:28:76-82/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82/r11.claim: Kanz is accumulated wealth, conventionally hidden underground; legally only wealth on which zakāt is unpaid is called a treasure, given the warning about it.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r11.anchor: والكنز جمع المال بعضه على بعض وصار بالعرف عبارة عما يخبأ تحت الأرض

TABRISI:28:76-82/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82/r12.claim: Mafātiḥ and mafātīḥ are plural forms with the same meaning: what opens a lock.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r12.anchor: والمفاتح جمع مفتح والمفاتيح جمع مفتاح ومعناهما واحد

TABRISI:28:76-82/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82/r13.claim: Nāʾa bi-ḥimlihi means to rise under its weight; anʾāʾ is also used. An ʿuṣba is a tightly joined group.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r13.anchor: وناء بحمله ينوء نوءا إذا نهض به مع ثقله عليه

TABRISI:28:76-82/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r14.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:28:76-82/r14.claim: Abū Zayd says nāʾanī al-ḥiml means ‘the load weighed me down.’
TABRISI:28:76-82/r14.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: ناءني الحمل إذا أثقلني

TABRISI:28:76-82/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82/r15.claim: Bāʾ and hamza can alternate in transitive forms; Arabic says the keys weigh down a group or, in the inverse form, the group bears them.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r15.anchor: فالباء والهمز يتعاقبان في تعدي الفعل قال سبحانه

TABRISI:28:76/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:28:76/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets the phrase as inverted order, meaning the group is weighed down by the keys; the author rejects this as incorrect and unsuitable for Qurʾānic language.
TABRISI:28:76/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هذا من المقلوب ومعنى قوله لتنوء بالعصبة تنوء العصبة بها

TABRISI:28:76/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76/r2.claim: The author rejects using alleged poetic inversions to explain Qurʾānic wording, since examples may be Arab poetic errors; he cites the lamp and Imruʾ al-Qays lines as such cases.
TABRISI:28:76/r2.anchor: وهذا غير صحيح ولا يجوز أن يحمل القرآن عليه لأنه يجري مجرى الغلط من العرب

TABRISI:28:76/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76/r3.claim: The anonymous lamp poem is offered as an inversion example: ‘the eye shines by it’ is taken to mean ‘it makes the eye shine.’
TABRISI:28:76/r3.anchor: إن سراجا لكريم مفخره تجلى به العين إذا ما تجهره

TABRISI:28:76/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76/r4.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line about an oil lamp in lamp-wicks is another alleged inversion example.
TABRISI:28:76/r4.anchor: يضيء الظلام وجهها لضجيعها كمصباح زيت

TABRISI:28:76/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76/r5.claim: The cited line about a thrust by Ḥuṣayn is treated as an example in which an object is expressed as the agent.
TABRISI:28:76/r5.anchor: غداة أحلت لابن صرمة طعنة حصين غبيطات

TABRISI:28:76/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76/r6.claim: A rājiz’s verse mistakenly treats pistachios as vegetables, further showing that poetry can contain errors.
TABRISI:28:76/r6.anchor: جارية لم تعلم المرققا ولم تذق من البقول الفستقا

TABRISI:28:76/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r7.speaker: خداش بن زهير
TABRISI:28:76/r7.claim: Although many read Khidāsh’s line as saying men suffer from spears, the author says the spears suffer because they are too noble to be used against such thugs.
TABRISI:28:76/r7.anchor: وتركت خيلا لا هوادة بينها وتشقى الرماح بالضياطرة الحمر

TABRISI:28:76/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r8.speaker: زهير
TABRISI:28:76/r8.claim: Zuhayr’s ‘red one of ʿĀd’ is no mistake for Thamūd: Thamūd was called the later ʿĀd, descended from survivors of the first ʿĀd; their name evokes scant water and smaller numbers.
TABRISI:28:76/r8.anchor: فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم كأحمر عاد ثم تنتج فتتئم

TABRISI:28:76/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r9.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:76/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says Qarun was an Israelite from Moses’ tribe and his maternal cousin; a report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh agrees.
TABRISI:28:76/r9.anchor: أي كان من بني إسرائيل ثم من سبط موسى وهو ابن خالته عن عطاء عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:28:76/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:28:76/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj instead makes Qarun Moses’ paternal cousin based on their descent from Qāhath.
TABRISI:28:76/r10.anchor: وقيل: كان ابن عم موسى لحا لأنه كان قارون بن يصهر بن قاهث وموسى بن عمران بن قاهث عن ابن جريج

TABRISI:28:76/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r11.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TABRISI:28:76/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says Moses was Qarun’s nephew and Qarun his uncle.
TABRISI:28:76/r11.anchor: وقيل: كل موسى ابن أخيه وقارون عمه عن محمد بن إسحاق

TABRISI:28:76/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r12.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:76/r12.claim: Qatāda says Qarun lorded his treasures over the Israelites; he was called al-Munawwar for his beauty and, despite being a foremost Torah reciter, hypocritically rebelled like al-Sāmirī.
TABRISI:28:76/r12.anchor: عن قتادة قال وكان يسمي المنور لحسن صورته

TABRISI:28:76/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r13.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وابن عباس
TABRISI:28:76/r13.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Ibn ʿAbbās say Qarun was Pharaoh’s agent over the Israelites in Egypt and oppressed them.
TABRISI:28:76/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب وابن عباس

TABRISI:28:76/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r14.speaker: عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب
TABRISI:28:76/r14.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab say Qarun added a span to his clothes.
TABRISI:28:76/r14.anchor: وقيل: إنه زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا عن عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب

TABRISI:28:76/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76/r15.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:28:76/r15.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Qarun found one of Joseph’s hidden treasures.
TABRISI:28:76/r15.anchor: قال عطاء أصاب كنزا من كنوز يوسف

TABRISI:28:76#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:76#2/r1.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn ʿAbbās, take the keys as Qarun’s treasuries; al-Zajjāj prefers this view, comparing the phrase with 6:59.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r1.anchor: فيكون المراد بمفاتحه خزائن ماله وهو قول ابن عباس

TABRISI:28:76#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
TABRISI:28:76#2/r2.claim: Qatāda and Mujāhid instead understand the keys as implements for opening doors.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r2.anchor: هي المفاتح التي تفتح بها الأبواب عن قتادة ومجاهد

TABRISI:28:76#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r3.speaker: الأعمش عن خيثمة
TABRISI:28:76#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash transmits from Khaythama that Qarun’s leather keys were each as large as a finger.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r3.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن خيثمة قال: كانت مفاتيح قارون من جلود كل مفتاح مثل الإصبع

TABRISI:28:76#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:28:76#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid defines an ʿuṣba as ten to fifteen people.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r4.anchor: ما بين عشرة إلى خمسة عشرة عن مجاهد

TABRISI:28:76#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:28:76#2/r5.claim: Qatāda defines an ʿuṣba as ten to forty people.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r5.anchor: ما بين عشرة إلى أربعين عن قتادة

TABRISI:28:76#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
TABRISI:28:76#2/r6.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says an ʿuṣba is forty men.

TABRISI:28:76#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:76#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines an ʿuṣba as three to ten people.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r7.anchor: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:28:76#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is any group whose members support one another.

TABRISI:28:76#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76#2/r9.claim: Qarun’s people tell him not to exult boastfully, swagger, or act arrogantly over his treasures; God does not love that disposition.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r9.anchor: أي لا تأشر ولا تمرح ولا تتكبر بسبب كنوزك

TABRISI:28:76#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76#2/r10.claim: The anonymous poems show farḥ can mean insolent boasting rather than ordinary happiness.
TABRISI:28:76#2/r10.anchor: ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني ولا جازع من صرفه المتقلب

TABRISI:28:81-82/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:81-82/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:81-82/r12.claim: Qarun’s story continues the promised account of Moses: it is another episode from Moses’ story.
TABRISI:28:81-82/r12.anchor: إنما اتصلت قصة قارون بما قبلها من قوله نتلو عليك

TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r1.claim: The author says Qarun’s story reinforces that worldly goods are temporary and what is with God is better and more enduring, as stated in 42:36.
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r1.anchor: فأكد سبحانه ذلك بحديث قارون وحاله

TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r2.claim: Another connection is that, after describing unbelievers’ disgrace on Judgment Day, the commentary identifies Qarun as one of them, to be disgraced then as he was in this life.
TABRISI:28:76-82#2/r2.anchor: ذكر عقيبة أن قارون من جملتهم

THALABI:v7p259/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p259/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v7p259/r1.claim: Most commentators say Qarun was Moses's cousin: Qarun's father and Moses's father shared Fāhith, son of Levi, son of Jacob.
THALABI:v7p259/r1.anchor: هذا قول أكثر المفسرين، وقال ابن إسحاق

THALABI:v7p259/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p259/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v7p259/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives another genealogy: Yashhar fathered both Imran and Qarun; Imran's son Moses was therefore Qarun's brother's son, and Qarun his paternal uncle.
THALABI:v7p259/r2.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: تزوج يصهر ابن فاهث شميت بنت تباويت

THALABI:v7p260/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p260/r1.claim: Qatada says Qarun was called al-Munawwar for his handsome appearance and was the Israelites' finest reader of Torah, but hypocritical like the Samaritan.
THALABI:v7p260/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته ولم يكن في بني إسرائيل أقرأ للتوراة منه،

THALABI:v7p260/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r2.speaker: المسيب
THALABI:v7p260/r2.claim: Al-Musayyib says Qarun served Pharaoh as governor over the Israelites and oppressed them.
THALABI:v7p260/r2.anchor: عن المسيب إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم قال: كان عاملا لفرعون على بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v7p260/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p260/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh appointed Qarun over the Israelites while Pharaoh was in Egypt.
THALABI:v7p260/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان فرعون قد ملكه على بني إسرائيل حين كان بمصر

THALABI:v7p260/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p260/r4.claim: Qatada explains Qarun's aggression as stemming from his great wealth and many children.
THALABI:v7p260/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: فبغى عليهم بكثرة ماله وولده،

THALABI:v7p260/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r5.speaker: سفيان
THALABI:v7p260/r5.claim: Sufyan, transmitting from Qatada, says Qarun oppressed people through arrogance and ostentation.
THALABI:v7p260/r5.anchor: سفيان عنه: بالكبر والبذخ، عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب

THALABI:v7p260/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r6.speaker: عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب
THALABI:v7p260/r6.claim: ʿAta al-Khurasani and Shahr ibn Hawshab say Qarun extended his garments by a handspan beyond others.
THALABI:v7p260/r6.anchor: عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب: زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا

THALABI:v7p260/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p260/r7.claim: Mafātiḥ is the plural of miftah, the tool used to open a door.
THALABI:v7p260/r7.anchor: وهي جمع المفتح، وهو الذي يفتح به الباب

THALABI:v7p260/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p260/r8.claim: The keys weighed down their carriers because of their heaviness; nāʾa yanūʾu describes rising under a heavy load, as an anonymous poem illustrates.
THALABI:v7p260/r8.anchor: أي لتثقل بهم إذا حملوها لثقلها

THALABI:v7p260/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p260/r9.claim: Mujahid defines the group carrying the keys as ten to fifteen people.
THALABI:v7p260/r9.anchor: فقال مجاهد: ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر، قتادة:

THALABI:v7p260/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r10.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p260/r10.claim: Qatada gives the group as between ten and forty people.
THALABI:v7p260/r10.anchor: قتادة: ما بين العشرة إلى أربعين، أبو صالح:

THALABI:v7p260/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r11.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v7p260/r11.claim: Abu Salih says the group numbered forty men.
THALABI:v7p260/r11.anchor: أبو صالح: أربعون رجلا، عكرمة منهم من يقول:

THALABI:v7p260/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r12.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v7p260/r12.claim: Ikrima reports two estimates: forty or seventy people.
THALABI:v7p260/r12.anchor: عكرمة منهم من يقول: أربعون، ومنهم من يقول: سبعون،

THALABI:v7p260/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r13.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p260/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, says the group numbered three to ten.
THALABI:v7p260/r13.anchor: الضحاك عن ابن عباس: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة،

THALABI:v7p260/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r14.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p260/r14.claim: Another estimate puts the group at sixty.
THALABI:v7p260/r14.anchor: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة، وقيل: ستون.

THALABI:v7p260/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r15.speaker: خيثمة
THALABI:v7p260/r15.claim: Khaythama says he found in the Gospel that Qarun's keys loaded sixty marked white mules, each key no larger than a finger and each corresponding to a treasure.
THALABI:v7p260/r15.anchor: عن خيثمة، قال: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون توقر ستين بغلا

THALABI:v7p260/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r16.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p260/r16.claim: Mujahid says the keys were made from camel hides.
THALABI:v7p260/r16.anchor: مجاهد: كانت المفاتيح من جلود الإبل

THALABI:v7p260/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r17.speaker: يقال
THALABI:v7p260/r17.claim: One account says Qarun carried keys everywhere: first iron, then wood when iron was too heavy, then finger-length cowhide keys; forty mules carried them when he rode.
THALABI:v7p260/r17.anchor: ويقال: كان قارون [أينما] ذهب يحمل معه مفاتيح كنوزه،

THALABI:v7p260/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r18.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v7p260/r18.claim: Some interpret the keys as guards; Abu Salih adopts this interpretation.
THALABI:v7p260/r18.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أراد بالمفاتيح الحراس وإليه ذهب أبو صالح

THALABI:v7p260/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p260/r19.speaker: أبو زرين
THALABI:v7p260/r19.claim: Abu Zarrin argues that one key would suffice for the people of Kufa, so the verse means Qarun's treasures rather than literal keys.
THALABI:v7p260/r19.anchor: عن أبي زرين قال: لو كان مفتاح واحد لأهل الكوفة كان كافيا إنما يعني كنوزه،

THALABI:v7p261/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r1.claim: On one construction, the keys lean on and weigh down the group carrying them.

THALABI:v7p261/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r2.speaker: أهل البصرة
THALABI:v7p261/r2.claim: The Basrans say Arabic reverses the apparent relation, as when one says a woman's rear burdens her although she bears it, like a camel bears its load.
THALABI:v7p261/r2.anchor: والآخر قال أهل البصرة: قد يفعل العرب هذا، تقول للمرأة: إنها لتنوء بها عجيزتها

THALABI:v7p261/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r3.claim: He glosses the first poem as saying, I ransomed him with my life and wealth, illustrating the shifted construction.
THALABI:v7p261/r3.anchor: والمعنى فديت بنفسي ومالي نفسه، وقال آخر

THALABI:v7p261/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r4.claim: The second poem means the corpulent men are pierced by spears, and الخيل here means men.
THALABI:v7p261/r4.anchor: وإنما يشقي الضياطرة بالرماح، والخيل هاهنا: الرجال

THALABI:v7p261/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r5.claim: Here do not rejoice means do not act insolently or arrogantly; ordinary happiness is not blameworthy.
THALABI:v7p261/r5.anchor: لا تفرح لا تأشر ولا تمرح، ومنه قول الله سبحانه: إنه لفرح فخور

THALABI:v7p261/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r6.claim: The condemned rejoicers are insolent, ungrateful, arrogant people who fail to thank God for what He gave them.
THALABI:v7p261/r6.anchor: إن الله لا يحب الفرحين الأشرين البطرين المتكبرين الذين لا يشكرون الله سبحانه على ما أعطاهم

THALABI:v7p261/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r7.speaker: مبشر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v7p261/r7.claim: Mubashir glosses the prohibition as do not cause corruption, and explains that God does not love corruptors.
THALABI:v7p261/r7.anchor: مبشر بن عبد الله في قول الله سبحانه وتعالى: لا تفرح قال: لا تفسد إن الله لا يحب الفرحين المفسدين

THALABI:v7p261/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p261/r8.claim: A poem uses أفرحتك to mean that the deposits corrupted you.

THALABI:v7p262/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r7.speaker: المسيب بن شريك
THALABI:v7p262/r7.claim: Al-Musayyib ibn Sharik glosses the keys as Qarun's containers and reports that they numbered four hundred million, carried in forty bags.
THALABI:v7p262/r7.anchor: عن المسيب بن شريك ما إن مفاتحه قال: أوعيته وكانت أربعمائة ألف ألف

THALABI:v7p262#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p262#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh had appointed Qarun ruler over the Israelites while they were in Egypt.
