THALABI:v7p262#2/r13.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كان فرعون قد ملك قارون على بني إسرائيل حين كان بمصر

THALABI:v7p262#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r14.speaker: المسيب بن شريك
THALABI:v7p262#2/r14.claim: Al-Musayyib ibn Sharik says Qarun was an official over the Israelites who oppressed them.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r14.anchor: وعن المسيب بن شريك: أنه كان عاملا على بني إسرائيل وكان يظلمهم

THALABI:v7p262#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r15.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p262#2/r15.claim: One view says Qarun transgressed by adding a handspan to the people's clothing.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا

THALABI:v7p262#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r16.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p262#2/r16.claim: Other explanations say Qarun's transgression was arrogance or his great wealth.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: بغى عليهم بالكبر، وقيل: بكثرة ماله

THALABI:v7p262#2/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r17.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p262#2/r17.claim: Mujahid estimates the group carrying the keys at ten to fifteen people.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r17.anchor: فقال مجاهد: ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر

THALABI:v7p262#2/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r18.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p262#2/r18.claim: Qatada estimates the group at ten to forty people.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r18.anchor: وقال قتادة: ما بين العشرة إلى أربعين

THALABI:v7p262#2/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r19.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v7p262#2/r19.claim: Ikrima transmits estimates of forty or seventy people.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r19.anchor: وقال عكرمة: منهم من يقول أربعون ومنهم من يقول سبعون

THALABI:v7p262#2/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r20.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v7p262#2/r20.claim: Al-Dahhak estimates the group at three to ten people.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r20.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

THALABI:v7p262#2/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r21.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p262#2/r21.claim: Another estimate places the group at sixty people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun was from the Israelites, in Moses’ tribe, and was his maternal cousin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: من بني إسرائيل، ثم في سبط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r2.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل وإبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r2.claim: They call Qarun Moses’ cousin and give their lineages as Qarun son of Yashar son of Qahat and Moses son of Imran son of Qahat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل وإبراهيم: كان ابن عمه لخالته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead says Moses was Qarun’s nephew and Qarun was Moses’ full uncle, since both Qarun and Imran were sons of Yashar son of Qahat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r3.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان موسى ابن أخي قارون، وقارون كان عم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r4.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r4.claim: Qatada and Muqatil say Qarun transgressed through his abundant wealth and children, becoming arrogant and extravagant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r4.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة؛ قال: بغى عليهم بكثرة ماله وولده بالكبر والبذخ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r5.speaker: المسيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r5.claim: Al-Musayyab says Qarun was Pharaoh’s official over the Israelites and oppressed them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r5.anchor: وقال المسيب (¬4): كان قارون عاملا لفرعون على بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r6.speaker: الفراء والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r6.claim: They say Qarun resented that Moses had prophethood and Aaron held the altar and offerings, while he had no such distinction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: بغيه عليهم: أنه قال: إذا كانت النبوة لموسى، وكان المذبح والقربان في يد هارون، فمالي (¬6)؟ وهذا قول الكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r7.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r7.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says Qarun exceeded others by a handspan in his clothing; al-Wahidi treats this as a sign of arrogance and self-exaltation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p446/r7.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب في تفسير قوله: {فبغى عليهم}: زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r1.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash reads ما as “that which”: the إن clause belongs to the relative construction, so one pauses after ما despite إن usually beginning a clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش: يريد: الذي إن مفاتحه، وهذا موضع لا يكاد يبتدأ فيه ب: إن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r2.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك وأبو صالح وأبو رزين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r2.claim: They understand the mafatih as Qarun’s treasure stores; the author says this is the preferred reading of al-Farra’ and al-Zajjaj.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وخيثمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r3.claim: They take the word as keys used to open doors, and say Qarun’s keys were made of camel hides.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: المفاتح هاهنا جمع: مفتاح، وهو ما يفتح به الباب. وهو قول قتادة ومجاهد وخيثمة؛ قالوا: كانت مفاتيحه من جلود الإبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r4.claim: Al-Farra’ prefers “treasure stores”: if the word meant keys, the normal plural would be مفاتيح, although مفاتح is permissible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: {مفاتحه} خزائنه (¬6). وأيضا فإن المفاتح لو كان جمع مفتاح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r5.claim: Al-Layth distinguishes the plurals: مفاتيح is the plural of the key that opens a lock, while مفاتح is the plural of a treasury.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p448/r5.anchor: قال الليث: وجمع المفتاح (¬7) الذي يفتح به المغلاق: مفاتيح، وجمع المفتح الخزانة: مفاتح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains النوء as rising with effort and difficulty; ناء بحمله describes laboring under a heavy load.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r1.anchor: معنى النوء في اللغة: النهوض بجهد ومشقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī cites al-Rumma’s nestling poem as evidence for rising with effort; ينوءن witnesses this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r2.anchor: قال ذو الرمة يصف الفراخ: ينوءن ولم يكسين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r3.claim: A second al-Rumma poem uses تنوء for a hind whose heavy rear makes her rise laboriously.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r3.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: تنوء بأخراها فلأيا قيامها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r4.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r4.claim: Al-Azharī says the root sense of النوء is leaning to one side.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r4.anchor: قال الأزهري: وأصل النوء: الميل في شق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a poem about an archer whose shoulder leans north after drawing a bow, illustrating الميل في شق.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r5.anchor: أنشد الفراء: حتى إذا ما التأمت مواصله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r6.claim: A person is called ناء بحمله because lifting a heavy burden makes the lifter lean.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r6.anchor: وقيل لمن نهض بحمله: ناء به؛ لأنه إذا نهض به وهو ثقيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r7.claim: The word also describes a star setting while slanting away from its place of disappearance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r7.anchor: وكذلك النجم إذا سقط مائلا عن مغيبه الذي يغيب فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r8.claim: He refers readers to his explanation of عصبة at Joseph 12:8 and 12:14.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r8.anchor: وذكرنا تفسير العصبة عند قوله: {ونحن عصبة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r9.claim: In the transmission of ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says forty of the strongest men carried Qarun’s keys.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: كان يحمل مفاتيحه أربعون رجلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r10.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r10.claim: Mujāhid defines the group as ten to fifteen people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: العصبة ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r11.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r11.claim: Muqātil gives the range for عصبة as ten to forty people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r11.anchor: وقال مقاتل: العصبة: عشرة نفر إلى أربعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r12.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r12.claim: Al-Kalbī defines the group as fifteen to forty people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r12.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ما بين الخمسة عشر إلى الأربعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r13.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r13.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says عصبة means forty people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r14.claim: Abū Isḥāq defines عصبة as a group united in one affair, following one another’s actions and supporting one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r14.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والعصبة في اللغة: الجماعة الذين أمرهم واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r15.speaker: خيثمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r15.claim: Al-Aʿmash transmits from Khaythama that sixty fine dappled mules carried the keys when Qarun rode.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r15.anchor: روى الأعمش عن خيثمة قال: كان إذا ركب قارون حملت المفاتيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r16.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r16.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the keys were carried on forty mules; another report says seventy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r16.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: كانت تحمل على أربعين بغلا، وقيل: سبعون بغلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r17.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r17.claim: Al-Wāḥidī questions interpreting عصبة as mules, since the word applies to men.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r17.anchor: ولست أدري كيف فسروا العصبة بالبغال، وهي في الرجال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r18.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r18.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r18.claim: Muqātil takes the heavy keys as those of Qarun’s treasuries.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r18.anchor: قال مقاتل في تفسير: {لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة} عن حمل خزائنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r19.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the wording as the load of the keys weighing down the group.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ليثقلهم حمل المفاتيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r20.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r20.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r20.claim: Abū Zayd contrasts نؤت بالحمل, I rise with the load, with ناءني الحمل, the load weighed me down; this matches Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r20.anchor: قال أبو زيد: يقال نؤت بالحمل أنوء به، إذا نهضت به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r21.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r21.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r21.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the bāʾ as causative: the keys make the group bend under their weight; dropping bāʾ requires an initial alif, as in 18:96.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p450/r21.anchor: وشرح ذلك الفراء والمبرد؛ قال الفراء: نوؤها بالعصبة أن تثقلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the wording really means the keys make the group bend under their burden, like قم بنا meaning make us stand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد: مجازه في الحقيقة: {ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r2.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad cites Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm’s poem as Arabic evidence for making someone alight: تحل بنا means تجعلنا نحلها.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r2.anchor: وأنشد لقيس بن الخطيم: ديار التي كادت ونحن على منى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq likewise glosses the phrase as making the group bear a heavy load.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r3.anchor: ونحو هذا قال أبو إسحاق: {لتنوء بالعصبة} لتثقل العصبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash call the construction inverted: the group bears the keys; they cite poetry and an idiom about foul deeds reaching Hajar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة ومن وافقه: هذا مقلوب، إنما العصبة تنوء بالمفاتيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites a war poem as evidence for the proposed inversion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r5.anchor: وأنشد: ما كنت في الحرب العوان مغمرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains أو بلغت سؤاتهم هجر as their foul deeds reached Hajar, another proposed inversion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r6.anchor: فجعل هذا مثل قولهم: أو بلغت سؤاتهم هجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ accepts the inversion only if its proponent heard a transmitted precedent; otherwise he says the man misunderstood the meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p453/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: فإن كان سمع بهذا أثرا فهو وجه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r1.claim: Muqātil identifies Qarun’s people who spoke to him as the Israelites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إذ قال له قومه} قال مقاتل: بنو إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the plural as referring to one person, like 3:173, and says the man was Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd of Ashjaʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: يعني موسى، وهو من الجمع الذي أريد به الواحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r3.claim: The commentators gloss لا تفرح as do not act arrogantly, revel insolently, behave boastfully, or exult with conceit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: لا تأشر ولا تمرح ولا تبطر ولا تفخر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r4.speaker: هدبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites Hudba’s poem using مفراح for someone who is not boastfully elated when fortune pleases him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r4.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة في الفرح بمعنى البطر قول هدبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r5.speaker: ابن أحمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r5.claim: Ibn Aḥmar’s poem uses الفرح for arrogance and insolence, glossed as البطر والأشر.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r5.anchor: وأنشد لابن أحمر: ولا ينسيني الحدثان عرضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba and others say the command targets insolent conceit, since ordinary happiness is not blameworthy; compare 11:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p455/r6.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة وغيره: أراد: لا تأشر؛ لأن السرور غير مكروه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r1.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil explain the condemned rejoicers as arrogant, ungrateful braggarts who fail to thank God for what He gave them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r1.anchor: يعني: الأشرين البطرين، الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم. قاله مجاهد ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses them as mockers; al-Wāḥidī says mockery is an implication of arrogance, not the actual interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد: المستهزئين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says Qarun was told not to exult in worldly wealth, since the person who rejoices in it spends it outside the cause of the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أراد لا تفرح بكثرة المال في الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل:} إن قارون كان من قوم موسى { [القصص: 76] كان ابن عمه أخي أبيه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r7.claim: Qārūn transgressed against the Israelites as Pharaoh’s official, oppressing them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r7.anchor: } فبغى عليهم { [القصص: 76] وكان عاملا لفرعون فتعدى عليهم وظلمهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r8.claim: “We gave him” refers to Qārūn and means “We bestowed on him.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r8.anchor: قال:} وآتيناه { [القصص: 76] ، يعني: قارون، أي: أعطيناه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r10.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r10.claim: Some explain Qārūn’s “keys” as his storehouses or wealth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r10.anchor: } ما إن مفاتحه { [القصص: 76] قال بعضهم: خزائنه، يعني: أمواله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r11.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r11.claim: Others understand the keys as keys to the storehouses.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r12.claim: His keys would weigh heavily on a company of strong men.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r13.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r13.claim: Al-Suddī explains “men of strength” as strong men and says this company comprised forty men.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r13.anchor: وقال السدي:} أولي القوة { [القصص: 76] ، يعني: أولي الشدة، والعصبة، الجماعة. وهم هاهنا أربعون رجلا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r14.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r14.claim: Those who advised Qārūn were Moses and the Israelite believers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r14.anchor: قال:} إذ قال له قومه { [القصص: 76] قال له موسى والمؤمنون بنو إسرائيل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r15.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r15.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r15.claim: “Do not rejoice” means “do not exult arrogantly.”

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r16.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r16.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r16.claim: Al-Suddī explains the condemned rejoicing as arrogant worldly exultation by polytheists who neither believe in nor hope for the hereafter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r16.anchor: وقال السدي:} لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين { [القصص: 76] ، يعني: لا تبطر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r17.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r17.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r17.claim: Those rejoicing in worldly life in another verse are identified as polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r17.anchor: وقال في آية أخرى:} وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا { [الرعد: 26] وهم المشركون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r18.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r18.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r18.claim: Ibn Mujāhid reports from his father that the phrase means insolent, arrogant people who do not thank God for what they receive; the terms are equivalent.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r18.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه: الأشرين، البطرين الذين لا يشكرون فيما أعطاهم وهو واحد.

QASHANI:28:76/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:76/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:76/r1.claim: Qarun is identified as a learned man like Bal'am ibn Ba'ura.
QASHANI:28:76/r1.anchor: { إن قارون كان من قوم موسى } عالما كبلعم بن باعوراء

QASHANI:28:76/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:76/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:76/r2.claim: Veiled by ego and knowledge, Qarun grows arrogant and overbearing; greed and love of worldly life delude him, make him admire his own adornment, and draw him downward until he is swallowed while veiled and detested.
QASHANI:28:76/r2.anchor: لاحتجابه بنفسه وعلمه بالتكبر والاستطالة عليهم

ELMALILI:28:76/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:76/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:76/r1.claim: Qarun, like Pharaoh for political despotism, epitomizes financial despotism and hoarding; his story depicts a monopolist capitalist.
ELMALILI:28:76/r1.anchor: Firavun, siyâsî zulm ü istibdadda alem olduğu gibi Kārûn da mâlî istibdad ve ihtikârda alemdir. Bu suretle Kārûn kıssası muhtekir bir kapitalist kıssasıdır.

ELMALILI:28:76/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:76/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:76/r2.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and a relative of Moses.
ELMALILI:28:76/r2.anchor: Mûsâ’nın kavminden idi yani Benî İsrâil’den ve Mûsâ’nın akrabasından idi

ELMALILI:28:76/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:76/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:76/r3.claim: Elmalılı explains Qarun's transgression as hoarding, withholding zakat, and rebelling against Moses.
ELMALILI:28:76/r3.anchor: derken onlara karşı bağyetti ihtikâr yaptı, zekâtını vermedi, Mûsâ’ya isyan etti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r1.speaker: Tefsirlerde
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r1.claim: Commentaries portray Qarun as Moses’s cousin and a high-ranking Pharaoh official who oppressed Israel; after first believing Moses, he opposed him from greed and envy, boasted of knowledge and wealth, and was destroyed by disbelief and arrogance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r1.anchor: Tefsirlerde Karun, Hz. Mûsâ’nın amcasının oğlu ve Firavun’un yüksek seviyede bir görevlisi olarak tanıtılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r2.claim: A report says Qarun had the broadest religious knowledge among the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r2.anchor: Rivayete göre İsrâiloğulları içinde dinî mâlûmatı en geniş olan kimseydi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r3.claim: Usba means a tightly united, powerful group of ten to forty people; the expression alludes to Qarun’s immense wealth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r3.anchor: on yahut daha çok (kırka kadar) kişiden oluşan, birbirine sıkı sıkıya bağlı güçlü bir cemaat” anlamına gelmektedir (İbn Âşûr, XII, 222)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.claim: Qarun’s story remains a warning to those who trust wealth and power, consider themselves privileged and great, disobey God, wrong others, and transgress.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.anchor: Karun kıssası, servet ve gücüne güvenerek, kendini imtiyazlı ve büyük görüp Allah’a isyan, insanlara karşı haksızlık eden

BAQILLANI:v1p105/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r1.claim: Istīṭrād is a digression in which a poet appears to describe a horse but turns the passage toward satire of ʿUthmān; the cited poets illustrate the device.
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r1.anchor: قال هذا المستطرد أو قال الاستطراد قلت وما معنى ذلك قال يرى أنه يصف الفرس ويريد هجاء عثمان

BAQILLANI:v1p105/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r2.claim: The Quranic example moves from the particular image of shadows to the broader report that every creature and the angels prostrate to God.
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r2.anchor: كأنه كان المراد أن يجري بالقول

BAQILLANI:v1p105/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r5.claim: Al-Bāqillānī names exception as another poetic figure and illustrates it with al-Nābigha's claim that his people have no fault except battle-worn swords.
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r5.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول

BAQILLANI:v1p229/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r1.claim: The first horse line uses familiar material about speed and is neither unprecedented nor beyond the conventional comparisons poets already used.
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r1.anchor: البيت الأول صالح وقد قاله الناس ولم يسبق إليه ولم يقل ما لم يقولوه

BAQILLANI:v1p229/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r2.claim: The horse's speed is compared to a hawk or eagle diving, but that is not truly a horse's characteristic and is not the fastest phase of their flight.
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r2.anchor: على أن الهوى يذكر عند الانقضاض خاصة وليس للفرس هذه الصفة في الحقيقة

BAQILLANI:v1p229/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r3.claim: Comparing the horse's ears to a leaf conveys their keen, rapid response to sound, like a leaf sensing the wind; that intended sense is not explicit in the wording.
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r3.anchor: وأما البيت الثاني فقوله إن الأذنين كأنهما من ورق موصل وإنما أراد بذلك حدتهما وسرعة حركتهما

BAQILLANI:v1p229/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r4.claim: The third line is an instance of istīṭrād, for which Abu Tammām's treatment is excellent, while al-Buḥturī's line is poor in both wording and meaning.
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r4.anchor: وأما البيت الثالث فقد ذكرنا فيما مضى من الكتاب انه من باب الاستطراد ونقلنا نظائر ذلك

BAQILLANI:v1p229/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r5.claim: Al-Buḥturī's praise of a horse that does not avoid a speck in water is an ugly blemish; Bashshār's bloody-water image or al-Mutanabbī's daring image would better praise its valor.
BAQILLANI:v1p229/r5.anchor: والذي وقع للبحتري في هذا البيت عندي ليس بجيد في لفظ ولا معنى وهو بيت وحش جدا

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r1.claim: Times themselves are alike as containers; their difference comes from the acts and states that occur in them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r1.anchor: الأوقات ظروف لما يحصل فيها من الأفعال والأحوال ؛ فالظروف من الزمان متجانسة

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r2.claim: For those close to God, nights and days pass briefly, while time drags for those separated from Him; three poems express how felt duration changes with nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r2.anchor: فأهل القرب لياليهم قصار وكذلك أيامهم ، وأرباب الفراق لياليهم طوال

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r3.claim: The people described in the preceding passage have no defense, excuse, merciful intercessor, or helper; their error is evident and everlasting punishment overtakes them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r3.anchor: لا حجة لهم ، ولا جواب يعذرهم ، ولا شفيع يرحمهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r4.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r4.claim: The story says Qarun was Moses' cousin and one of Israel's most devout worshippers, living apart from people in a hermitage.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r4.anchor: جاء في القصص أنه كان ابن عم موسى ، وكان من أعبد بني إسرائيل ، وكان قد اعتزل الناس

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r5.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r5.claim: Satan appeared to Qarun in human form and outwardly worshipped beside him until Qarun marveled at his devotion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r5.anchor: فتصور له إبليس في صورة بشر ، وأخذ في الظاهر يتعبد معه في صومعته حتى تعجب قارون

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r6.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r6.claim: Satan first persuaded Qarun that they must earn their necessities rather than rely on people's gifts, and Qarun agreed to work one day each week and spend the proceeds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r6.anchor: ندخل في الأسبوع يوما السوق ، ونكتسب ، وننفق ذلك القدر في الأسبوع ، فأجابه إليه

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r7.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r7.claim: Satan next proposed one market day for their living and another for charity, and Qarun agreed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r7.anchor: نكتسب في الأسبوع يوما لأنفسنا ، ويوما نكتسب ونتصدق به ، فأجابه إليه

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r8.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r8.claim: Satan then added a third workday for savings against illness or other interruptions, alongside days for expenses and charity; Qarun again agreed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r8.anchor: نكتسب في الأسبوع ثلاثة أيام ؛ يوما للنفقة ويوما للصدقة ويوما للإدخار

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r9.speaker: القصص
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r9.claim: Once Satan saw worldly love take root in Qarun's heart, he left him to continue; Qarun's wealth and conduct then developed as they did.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r9.anchor: فلما علم أن حب الدنيا استمكن من قلبه ودعه

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r10.claim: Love of the world drives hoarding, hoarding strengthens love, and love leads to transgression against others; abundant wealth became the cause of Qarun's destruction.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r10.anchor: وحمله حب الدنيا على جمعها ، وحمله جمعها على حبها ، وحمله حبها على البغي عليهم ، وصارت كثرة ماله سبب هلاكه

QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r11.claim: Although repeatedly admonished to forgo joy in worldly wealth and its enjoyment, Qarun persisted in error.
QUSHAYRI:v2p445/r11.anchor: وكم وعظ بترك الفرج بوجود الدنيا ، وبترك الاستمتاع بها

BURHAN:v2p114/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.claim: The section asks about Qur’anic phrases that coincide with metrical poetry, whether a full line, several lines, or a hemistich, while treating such coincidence as distinct from poetry.
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.anchor: فإن قيل فقد وجد فى القرآن ما وافق شعرا موزونا إما بيت تام أو أبيات أو مصراع

BURHAN:v2p114/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.claim: The author adds Qur’anic phrases as examples of metrical coincidence, including night worship, charity, disputing, the flood, Abu Lahab, victory, conversion, and Qarun.

BURHAN:v3p287/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p287/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p287/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says changing the order of paired expressions across passages varies eloquent style; either ordering can achieve the point, though the superior item is usually first.
BURHAN:v3p287/r1.anchor: علم بذلك أن كلا الطريقين داخل تحت الحسن وذلك لأن العطف في المختلفين كالتثنية في المتفقين فلا عليك أن تقدم أيهما شئت فإنه حسن مؤد إلى الغرض

BURHAN:v3p287/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p287/r3.speaker: حازم
BURHAN:v3p287/r3.claim: Hazim rejects inversion as a rhetorical figure in the Qur'an, arguing that when Arabs invert order it is frivolity, mockery, imitation, or necessity, none fitting God.
BURHAN:v3p287/r3.anchor: فأنكره جماعة منهم حازم في كتاب منهاج البلغاء وقال إنه مما يجب أن ينزه كتاب الله عنه

BURHAN:v3p287/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p287/r4.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v3p287/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad accepts inversion without qualification beyond requiring that it cause no ambiguity.
BURHAN:v3p287/r4.anchor: المبرد في كتاب ما اتفق لفظه واختلف معناه

BURHAN:v3p287/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p287/r5.speaker: آخرون
BURHAN:v3p287/r5.claim: Other scholars say inversion is eloquent when it conveys a subtle point, but otherwise is not; Ibn al-Da'i permits it in interpretation when the reading is near, while remote readings belong only in poetry.
BURHAN:v3p287/r5.anchor: وفصل آخرون بين أن يتضمن اعتبارا لطيفا فبليغ وإلا فلا ولهذا قال ابن الضائع يجوز القلب على التأويل ثم قد يقرب التأويل فيصح في فصيح الكلام

BURHAN:v3p287/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p287/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p287/r6.claim: In inversion of attribution, the keys are grammatically said to weigh down the group, while the intended sense is that the group strains under the keys; this dramatizes their weight as if they summon strong bearers.
BURHAN:v3p287/r6.anchor: إن لم تجعل الباء للتعدية لأن ظاهره أن المفاتح تنوء بالعصبة ومعناه أن العصبة تنوء بالمفاتح لثقلها

BURHAN:v1p382/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p382/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p382/r1.claim: The extra alif after the hamza in تبوء and لتنوء signals semantic detail: Cain returns with two sins from one deed, while Qarun’s keys weigh down and tilt the band, suggesting a move from material treasure to the weight of knowledge and the afterlife.
BURHAN:v1p382/r1.anchor: وكذلك زيدت الألف بعد الهمزة في حرفين

BURHAN:v1p385/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p385/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p385/r1.claim: The orthography adds alif after mīm in مائة and مائتين, but not فئة; among hamzas preceded by a silent letter, only تبوء and لتنوء have this written alif, and the sole medial case is موئلا.
BURHAN:v1p385/r1.anchor: ولا أعلم همزة متطرفة قبلها ساكن رسمت خطا في المصحف إلا في هذين الموضعين

BURHAN:v4p218/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p218/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p218/r1.claim: The passage lists analyses of إن: one prior reading is remote, Qutrub takes it as قد, and it may be an indefinite noun with a modifier.
BURHAN:v4p218/r1.anchor: وعن قطرب انها بمعنى قد حكاه ابن الشجري ويحتمل النكرة الموصوفة

BURHAN:v4p218/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.claim: Some deny a negative use of إن and reconstruct deleted ما in examples such as ما إن الكافرون إلا في غرور; a poetic line supports the omission.
BURHAN:v4p218/r2.anchor: واعلم إن بعضهم انكر مجئ النافية وقال في الايات السابقة إن ما محذوفة والتقدير ما إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

ITQAN:v4p449/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p449/r2.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v4p449/r2.claim: Al-Farra' exempts لتنوأ, أن تبوأ, and السوأى from the rule that a hamza preceded by a consonant with sukun is omitted.
ITQAN:v4p449/r2.anchor: فإن سكن ما قبله حذف هو نحو ( ملء الأرض ) دفء شيء الخبء ماء إلا ( لتنوأ )

ITQAN:v4p449/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p449/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p449/r3.claim: The author says these are not true exceptions because the alif after waw is an extra alif after the verb’s waw, not the hamza’s written seat.
ITQAN:v4p449/r3.anchor: قلت وعندي أن هذه الثلاثة لا تستثنى لأن الألف التي بعد الواو ليست صورة الهمزة

ITQAN:v3p102/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p102/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p102/r6.claim: In an inversion of attribution, the keys are said to weigh down the group (meaning the group bears them); similar constructions reverse the apparent roles of book and term, nursing women, or fire and disbelievers.

SULAMI:v2p109#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r1.claim: Al-Qāsim says Qarun’s conduct was rebellion and transgression in every condition, and what is rejoiced over may become a source of grief.
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : في جميع الأحوال : بغى وطغيان والمفروح به محل الحزن

SULAMI:v2p109#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r2.claim: Sahl warns that rejoicing in something unworthy of joy brings unending grief.
SULAMI:v2p109#4/r2.anchor: قال سهل : من فرح بغير مفروح به استجلب حزنا لا انقضاء له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r1.claim: Calling a praised person “night” is not idiomatic merely to express displeasure; the metaphor suits someone described through darkness or blackness, as in Ibn Tabataba’s verse about a dark-skinned man.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r1.anchor: العرف لم يجر بأن تجعل الممدوح ليلا هكذا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r2.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r2.claim: The Prophet gives explicit comparisons: people are like a hundred camels with no mount among them, and the believer is like a palm or a young shoot.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r2.anchor: قول النبي الناس كإبل مائة لا تجد فيها فيها راحلة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r3.claim: An explicit simile cannot always become a metaphor by deleting the subject: reading the Prophet’s camels as people or a palm as a believer would be a strained riddle, not ordinary speech.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r3.anchor: هل تقدر أن تقول رأيت إبلا مائة لا تجد فيها راحلة في معنى رأيت ناسا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r4.claim: With an explicit kāf-simile the comparison noun is normally definite, while an indefinite needs a qualifying adjective; as a predicate, however, both definite and indefinite forms are natural.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p213/r4.anchor: كان كلا الأمرين التعريف والتنكير فيه حسنا جميلا

TUSTARI:28:76/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:76/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:28:76/r1.claim: Rejoicing in something unworthy of joy brings unending grief; a believer has no rest before meeting God.
TUSTARI:28:76/r1.anchor: من فرح بغير مفروح استجلب حزنا لا انقطاع له، وليس للمؤمن راحة

TUSTARI:28:76/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:28:76/r2.speaker: الأعمش
TUSTARI:28:76/r2.claim: Al-A'mash recalls attending a funeral where everyone was so grieved that they did not know whom to console.
TUSTARI:28:76/r2.anchor: حكي عن الأعمش قال: كنا نشهد جنازة فلا ندري من نعزي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r1.claim: Fronting can preserve a word's grammatical role, as when a predicate or object is moved before its subject, or can transfer it into a new role.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r1.anchor: تقديم يقال إنه على نية التأخير ، وذلك في كل شيء أقررته مع التقديم على حكمه الذي كان عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r2.claim: In a second kind of fronting, word order changes grammatical roles: المنطلق زيد makes المنطلق the subject, while زيد ضربته makes زيدا a subject and the verb's object a pronoun.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r2.anchor: ولكن على أن تنقل الشيء عن حكم إلى حكم ، وتجعل له بابا غير بابه ، وإعرابا غير إعرابه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r3.speaker: صاحب الكتاب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r3.claim: The cited grammar authority says speakers put first what they most need to clarify and care about, although both participants matter.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r3.anchor: قال صاحب ' الكتاب ' ، وهو يذكر الفاعل والمفعول : ' كأنهم يقدمون الذي بيانه أهم لهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r4.speaker: النحويون
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r4.claim: Grammarians illustrate the principle with killing an outlaw: listeners care that he was killed, not which person killed him, so the outlaw is mentioned first.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p96/r4.anchor: وقال النحويون : إن معنى ذلك أنه قد تكون أغراض الناس في فعل ما أن يقع بإنسان بعينه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r1.claim: An indefinite adjective under negation, as in ما في الدار كريم, negates the presence of anyone who has that quality.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r1.anchor: كنت نفيت الكينونة في الدار عن كل من يكون الكرم صفة له . وحكم الإنكار أبدا حكم النفي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r2.claim: In the comparison with وجعلوا الجن شركاء لله, the stated order makes partners specific to jinn; fronting شركاء broadens the meaning to deny any partner, yielding more meaning in fewer words.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r2.anchor: كان ' الجن ' مفعولا أول و ' الشركاء ' مفعولا ثانيا . وإذا كان كذلك كان ' الشركاء ' مخصوصا غير مطلق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r3.claim: The indefinite حياة in ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة signals a desire for added future life, rather than a general love of life; definiteness would lose this nuance.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p222/r3.anchor: أن المعنى على الازدياد من الحياة ، لا الحياة من أصلها ، وذلك لا يحرص عليه إلا الحي

DAMGHANI:v1p344/r19.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r19.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r19.claim: Mafātīḥ can mean treasuries; Qarun's treasure stores were heavy for a strong band to carry.
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r19.anchor: المفاتيح الخزائن قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

DAMGHANI:v1p408/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r8.claim: Kunūz means money and wealth, as in the accounts of Pharaoh’s people, hoarders of gold and silver, and Qārūn.
DAMGHANI:v1p408/r8.anchor: الكنوز الأموال قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

DAMGHANI:v1p394/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r12.claim: Quwwa also means strength and might: God is the Strong, and Qārūn’s company are people of strength.
DAMGHANI:v1p394/r12.anchor: القوة الشدة قوله تعالى في سورة هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r1.claim: The basic sense of ثقل is heaviness, the opposite of lightness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r1.anchor: الأصل في الثقل : الرزانة . وضده : الخفة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r3.claim: In the quoted elegy, حلت means that the earth was adorned with the dead.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r3.anchor: وتعني بقولها حلت : من التحلية ، أي : زانت به موتاها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r4.claim: ثقل and ثقلة can refer to all of a group's baggage when they travel.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r4.anchor: ويقال : ارتحل القوم بثقلهم وثقلتهم : أي : بأمتعتهم كلها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r1.claim: القوة means strength and its plural is قوى.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r2.claim: مقو is used for someone without provisions, for someone whose companions and camels are strong, and for someone who has become poor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r2.anchor: ويقال للذي لا زاد معه : مقو . وللذي أصحابه وإبله أقوياء : مقو . وللذي نزل بالفقر : مقو .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r3.claim: قواء is uninhabited land; a people may be described as having gone to such land, and a house as having become empty.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r3.anchor: والقواء : الأرض التي لا أهل بها . وأقوى القوم : صاروا بالقواء . وأقوت الدار : خلت .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r4.claim: Some define poetic اقواء as raising one rhyme ending and lowering another.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r4.anchor: فقال قوم : هو أن يرفع قافية ويخفض قافية .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r5.claim: Others define poetic اقواء as omitting a metrical unit, illustrated by the cited line.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون هو أن ينقص من عروضه قوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r9.claim: A fourth Qur'anic sense is strength or intensity, as in the phrase about Korah's strong company.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p489/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن القوة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

FARRA:v2p310/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r1.claim: The keys of Qarun's treasuries weigh down a band of forty men; maftāḥ means a treasury, and their weight makes the men lean.
FARRA:v2p310/r1.anchor: نوؤها بالعصبة أن تثقلهم، والعصبة هاهنا أربعون رجلا

FARRA:v2p310/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r2.claim: With the preposition, say tanūʾu bihim or tunīʾu bihim; dropping it adds an initial alif to the verb, as in atūnī afriġ and fa-aj āʾahā al-makhāḍ, understood with an omitted bi.
FARRA:v2p310/r2.anchor: قلت: تنوء بهم وتنيء بهم، كما قال (آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا)

FARRA:v2p310/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r3.speaker: رجل من أهل العربية
FARRA:v2p310/r3.claim: Another grammarian makes the band the subject weighed down by the keys, shifting the verb to mafātiḥ; al-Farrāʾ accepts it only if supported by transmitted usage, otherwise rejecting it as a misunderstanding.

FARRA:v2p310/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r4.claim: An unnamed poet's line says the lamp adorns the eye, citing taḥlā as evidence for the alternate construction.
FARRA:v2p310/r4.anchor: إن سراجا لكريم مفخره ... تحلى به العين إذا ما تجهره

FARRA:v2p310/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r5.claim: An unnamed Arab poem uses nāʾ for an archer leaning to one side under a bow's weight.

FARRA:v2p310/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r6.claim: Mā sāʾaka wa-nāʾaka means what troubles and burdens you; alif is suppressed by parallelism, as in hanāʾan wa-marāʾan and amraʾan.
FARRA:v2p310/r6.anchor: ما ساءك وناءك من ذلك، ومعناه ما ساءك وأناءك، إلا أنه ألقى الألف لأنه متبع لساءك، كما قالت العرب:

FARRA:v2p310/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p310/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p310/r7.claim: The same suppression appears in akaltu ṭaʿāman fa-hannaʾanī wa-marraʾanī, whose unpaired form is amraʾanī.
FARRA:v2p310/r7.anchor: فهنأني ومرأني، ومعناه، إذا أفردت: وأمرأني، فحذفت منه الألف

FARRA:v2p311/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r1.speaker: ذكروا
FARRA:v2p311/r1.claim: They report that Moses told Qarun not to exult because Qarun belonged to Moses' people, despite following another religion.
FARRA:v2p311/r1.anchor: ذكروا أن موسى الذي قال له ذلك لأنه من قومه وإن كان على غير دينه

FARRA:v2p311/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p311/r2.claim: The plural people can be represented by a single man, just as 3:173 says “the people told them”; there the informant was one man from Ashjaʿ.
FARRA:v2p311/r2.anchor: وجمعه هاهنا وهو واحد كقول الله (الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم)

FARRA:v2p311/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p311/r3.claim: Fāriḥīn would also be correct: fāriḥ describes people who will rejoice, while fariḥ describes those rejoicing now, like ṭāmiʿ/ṭamiʿ and sālis/salis.
FARRA:v2p311/r3.anchor: ولو قيل: الفارحين كان صوابا، كأن الفارحين: الذين يفرحون فيما يستقبلون

FARRA:v2p311/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p311/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p311/r4.claim: A Banū Dubayr poet uses sālis; ʿaḍāris means cold and derives from ʿaḍras, “cold,” showing the paired forms sālis and salis.
FARRA:v2p311/r4.anchor: ممكورة غرثى الوشاح السالس ... تضحك عن ذي أشر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r1.claim: Mafātiḥ burden the group by their weight; nāʾa means to lean under a burden, while anāʾa means to make someone lean.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r1.anchor: {ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة} أي تميل بها العصبة -إذا حملتها- من ثقلها. يقال: ناءت بالعصبة، أي مالت بها. وأناءت العصبة: أمالتها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ interprets mafātiḥ as the treasure itself; Ibn Qutayba adds that the word can mean the place where treasures are stored.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير أبي صالح: {ما إن مفاتحه} يعني: الكنز نفسه وقد تكون "المفاتح": مكان الخزائن.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r3.claim: In 24:61, mafātiḥ means the stored goods someone owns; in 6:59, the phrase refers, in his view, to God's treasuries.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r3.anchor: قال في موضع آخر: {أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه} (1) أي ما ملكتموه: من المخزون. وقال: {وعنده مفاتح الغيب} (2) نرى: أنها خزائنه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r4.claim: A ʿuṣbah is a group numbering from ten to forty.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r4.anchor: و"العصبة": ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r5.claim: The prohibition means do not exult arrogantly or grow proud; ordinary happiness is not blameworthy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r5.anchor:
{لا تفرح} لا تأشر، ولا تبطر. قال الشاعر:
ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني ... ولا جازع من صرفه المتحول (3)
أي لست بأشر. فأما السرور فليس بمكروه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r6.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r6.claim: The poet uses mafarrāḥ for one who is arrogant, not simply happy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p334#9/r6.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني ... ولا جازع من صرفه المتحول (3) أي لست بأشر.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r1.claim: Farah first means joy or gladness, as in people rejoicing in a favorable wind at sea.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r2.claim: Farah can also mean satisfaction, since satisfaction follows from gladness; the cited groups are content with what they have.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r2.anchor: والفرح: الرضا، لأنه عن المسرة يكون، قال الله تعالى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r3.claim: Farah can mean arrogant exultation or insolence, an excess of joy; this is the sense in the verse about those whom God does not love.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p268/r3.anchor: والفرح: البطر والأشر، لأن ذلك عن إفراط السرور

MAJAZ:v2p110/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p110/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p110/r4.claim: Mafātiḥ means the keys to Qarun’s treasuries. The wording reverses the burden: the strong band is burdened by the keys. Arabic makes similar reversals, as poetry says the haunch bears the camel and lances suffer from men.
MAJAZ:v2p110/r4.anchor: «ما إن مفاتحه لتنوأ بالعصبة أولي القوة» (76) أي مفاتح خزائته، ومجازه: ما إن العصبة ذوى القوة لتنوء بمفاتح نعمه

MAJAZ:v2p111/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p111/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p111/r1.claim: Lā tafraḥ means do not behave arrogantly or exultantly. Hudbah uses it for excessive joy; Ibn Aḥmar’s line means not exposing one’s nakedness to people.
MAJAZ:v2p111/r1.anchor: «لا تفرح» (76) أي لا تأشر ولا تمرح، قال هدبة: ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرنى

NAHHAS:v3p242/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p242/r1.claim: Qārūn is a foreign proper name and is indeclinable; foreign names on the fāʿūl pattern that do not take al are declined as indefinite, while suitable masculine names with al, such as Ṭāwūs and Rāqūd, are declinable.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r1.anchor: إن قارون لم ينصرف لأنه اسم أعجمي وما كان على فاعول أعجميا لا يحسن فيه الألف واللام لم ينصرف

NAHHAS:v3p242/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p242/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq says Qārūn would be declinable if it were Arabic, derived from qarantu al-shayʾ.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق ولو كان قارون من العربية من قرنت الشيء لانصرف

NAHHAS:v3p242/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p242/r3.claim: An with its subject forms the relative complement of mā.

NAHHAS:v3p242/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r4.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p242/r4.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān rejects the Kufans' claim that an cannot form the complement of a relative pronoun, pointing to this Qur'anic construction.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r4.anchor: وسمعت علي بن سليمان يقول ما أقبح ما يقول الكوفيون في الصلاة أنه لا يجوز

NAHHAS:v3p242/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p242/r5.claim: Mafātiḥ is the plural of maftaḥ; whoever uses miftāḥ instead has the plural mafātīḥ.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r5.anchor: وهو جمع مفتح ومن قال مفتاح قال مفاتيح

NAHHAS:v3p242/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p242/r6.claim: The best explanation is that the keys make the group lean under their weight, as in expressions where one causes another to go or come.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r6.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أن المعنى لتنيء العصبة أي تميلهم من ثقلها

NAHHAS:v3p242/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p242/r7.claim: In the paired idiom mā sāʾahu wa-nāʾahu, nāʾahu is a follow-on to sāʾahu; the expected form would be anāʾahu, as in hanāʾanī wa-marāʾanī and mā qaddama wa-mā ḥadatha.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r7.anchor: فأما قولهم له عندي ما ساءه وناءه فهو اتباع كان يجب أن يقال وأناءه

NAHHAS:v3p242/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r8.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p242/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Moses alone addressed Qārūn, using a plural expression, as in the report that people spoke to the believers when the speaker was one man, Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r8.anchor: تأوله الفراء على أن موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم هو الذي قاله له وحده فجمع ومثله

NAHHAS:v3p242/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r9.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p242/r9.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān rejects al-Farrāʾ's singular-speaker analysis as defeating the clarity of the statement; Nuʿaym and those who followed him were the speakers.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r9.anchor: وسمعت علي بن سليمان يقول غير هذا وينكر ما قال الفراء لأنه بطلان البيان

NAHHAS:v3p242/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p242/r10.claim: Do not exult in wealth, since such joy results in failing to give wealth its due.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r10.anchor: تأوله أبو إسحاق على أن المعنى لا تفرح بالمال لأن الفرح لا يؤدي فيه الحق

NAHHAS:v3p242/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p242/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes farḥīn as people currently in joy from fāriḥīn as people who will rejoice later, comparing ṭamiʿ and ṭāmiʿ and mayyit and māʾit.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r11.anchor: فرق الفراء بين الفرحين والفارحين وزعم أن الفرحين الذين هم في حال الفرح

NAHHAS:v3p242/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p242/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p242/r12.claim: The distinction al-Farrāʾ draws is contradicted by 69:21, which says mayyit rather than māʾit for those who are dead.
NAHHAS:v3p242/r12.anchor: وبذلك على خلاف ما قال قول الله جل وعز ﴿ إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون ﴾ ولم يقل مائت

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r1.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; its relative clause includes in and what follows, explaining the kasra on in.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r1.anchor: " ما " موصولة بمعنى الذي، صلتها " إن " وما في حيزها

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r2.speaker: الأخفش الصغير
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash the Younger transmits that the Kufans prohibit a relative clause from beginning with in and consider it objectionable, despite its Qurʾānic occurrence.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r2.anchor: ونقل الأخفش الصغير عن الكوفيين منع الوصل ب " إن "

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r3.claim: One parse makes bāʾ causative like hamza, without inversion: the keys make the strong group stagger under their burden.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r3.anchor: أن الباء للتعدية كالهمزة، ولا قلب في الكلام. والمعنى: لتنيء المفاتيح العصبة الأقوياء

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r4.claim: Nāʾa bi-shayʾ means to bear it with difficulty; Abū Zayd glosses nāʾtu bi-l-ʿamal as rising to undertake the work, supported by the cited poems.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r4.anchor: ومعنى ناء بكذا: نهض به بثقل

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r5.claim: Abū Zayd explains nāʾtu bi-l-ʿamal as “I rose to carry out the work,” and poetry attests nāʾa with a load.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r5.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: " نؤت بالعمل أي: نهضت "

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets nāʾa as making the load heavy and causing the carrier to lean; this yields the sense that the keys weigh down the group.

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd proposes inversion: the group is the subject that bears the keys, as in saying a she-camel was presented to a watering trough.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r7.anchor: والثاني: أن في الكلام قلبا، والأصل: لتنوء العصبة بالمفاتح، أي: لتنهض بها. قاله أبو عبيد

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r8.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r8.claim: Budayl ibn Maysara reads yanūʾu with masculine agreement because he supplies the omitted noun ḥamluhā or thiqluhā as the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r8.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة " لينوء " بالياء

SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also suggests the pronoun in mafātiḥuhu refers to Qārūn, with mafātiḥ acquiring masculine agreement from its genitive complement.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76/r9.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في " مفاتحه " لقارون، فاكتسب المضاف من المضاف إليه التذكير كقولهم: " ذهبت أهل اليمامة " قاله الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes إذ dependent on تنوء.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون معمولا لتنوء. قاله الزمخشري:

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes إذ depend on بغى; al-Shaykh rejects this because the meaning is not restricted to that time.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r2.anchor: أو ل " بغى " قاله ابن عطية. وردهما الشيخ:/ بأن المعنى ليس على التقييد بهذا الوقت.

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects attaching إذ to آتيناه because the gift did not occur then.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r3.anchor: بأن الإتياء لم يكن ذلك الوقت

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa makes إذ depend on an omitted verb, estimated as بغى عليهم.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r4.anchor: أو لمحذوف فقدره أبو البقاء: بغى عليهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r5.claim: Al-Samin says Abu al-Baqa's estimate بغى عليهم faces Ibn Atiyya's objection.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبغي أن يرد بما رد به قول ابن عطية

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r6.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari estimates اذكر; al-Shaykh estimates أظهر الفرح.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r6.anchor: وقدره الطبري: اذكر، وقدره الشيخ: أظهر الفرح

SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r7.claim: Al-Samin says al-Shaykh's estimate of showing joy fits.
SAMIN-DURR:28:76#2/r7.anchor: وقدره الشيخ: أظهر الفرح وهو مناسب.

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r5.claim: Qarun is a foreign proper name and indeclinable; even an Arabic faʿul derivation would remain indeclinable, explaining no tanwin.

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r6.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r6.claim: Reports call Qarun Moses' cousin and a Torah scholar; he opposed Moses and sought to discredit him.

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r7.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r7.claim: Qarun, then richest man, hired a notorious woman to falsely accuse Moses of soliciting her, promising marriage and payment.
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r7.anchor: يأمرها أن تصير إليه، وهو في ملأ من أصحابه

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r8.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r8.claim: The woman repented and exposed Qarun; he was stunned, and God gave Moses authority over him and ordered earth to obey him.

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.claim: Moses ordered earth to swallow Qarun and his house in stages, from knees to navel to neck, until both sank.

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r1.speaker: رواية
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r1.claim: A report describes Qarun's keys as finger-sized leather pieces carried by seventy or sixty mules.
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r1.anchor: روي في التفسير أن مفاتحه كانت من جلود على مقادر الإصبع

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes مفاتحه to mean his storehouses or treasuries.

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r3.claim: The group is variously said to number seventy, forty, fifteen to forty, or three to ten.
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r3.anchor: وقيل إن العصبة ههنا سبعون رجلا، وقيل أربعون

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r4.claim: عصبة is a common-purpose group whose members follow and support one another.
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r4.anchor: والعصبة في اللغة الجماعة الذين أمرهم واحد

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r5.claim: The likelier reading is keys meaning treasuries of wealth carried on seventy or forty mules; tiny leather keys could not be so burdensome.
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r5.anchor: أن مفاتحه خزائنه، وأنها خزائن المال

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r6.claim: The phrase means the keys or treasuries weighed heavily on the group.

ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r7.claim: Abu Zayd says نؤت بالحمل means I rose carrying a load, while ناء بي الحمل means the load weighed me down.
ZAJJAJ:v4p154/r7.anchor: قال أبو زيد: يقال نؤت بالحمل أنوء به نوءا

ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r1.claim: The sentence structure shows that even a follower of a great apostle can sin through pride and self-exaltation, exemplifying the preceding passage's false imagery.
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r1.anchor: a person who had been a follower of one of the greatest of God's apostles was not above the possibility of sinning under

ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r2.claim: Asad rejects the conventional identification of Qarun with biblical Korah as unwarranted; the account teaches a moral lesson rather than recounting history.
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r2.anchor: The conventional "identification" of Qarun with the Korah of the Old Testament

ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r3.claim: Asad says Qarun's moral role explains why the Qur'an juxtaposes him with Pharaoh, the arch-sinner.
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n84/r3.anchor: the juxtaposition, elsewhere in the Qur'an (29:39 and 40:24), of Qarun with Pharaoh, the arch-sinner

ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r1.claim: Usbah means a group of ten or more, up to forty; metonymically it conveys the great weight of Qarun's treasure-chests.
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r1.anchor: The term 'usbah denotes a company of ten or more (up to forty) persons

ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r2.claim: Mafatih can mean keys or what is locked away; the context requires the latter sense, treasure-chests.
ASAD-NOTES:28:76#n85/r2.anchor: The noun mafatih is a plural of both miftah or miftah ("key") and maftah

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p562/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p562/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p562/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses latanūʾu bi-l-ʿuṣba as weighing heavily and cites Imruʾ al-Qays's line about a woman walking under the weight of her hips.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p562/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: لتثقل. واستثهد بقول امرئ القيس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r1.claim: The verb is unique in form and root in the Qurʾān. The cited lexicons distinguish nāʾtu bi-l-ḥaml, rising while carrying a heavy load, from nāʾanī al-ḥaml, when the load weighs down and overcomes the carrier.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r1.anchor: السؤال عن: (تنوء) وحيدة فى القرآن، صيغة ومادة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r2.speaker: السجستاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r2.claim: Al-Sijistānī records reciprocal phrasing in which the burden is said to weigh down Zayd just as Zayd bears the burden, and uses the verse as an example.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r2.anchor: وقالوا ناء بزيد الحمل إذا ناء زيد بالحمل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the verse as a transferred or inverted attribution: the company actually bears the keys, though the wording makes the keys the subject of nāʾa.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r3.anchor: وأبو عبيدة أورد الكلمة فى مجاز ما يُحوَّل الفاعل منه إلى المفعول أو إلى غير المفعول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba reads the clause as the company rising with the keys, burdened; Ibn al-Anbārī transmits al-Farrāʾ's alternative that the keys weigh down the company.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r4.anchor: فى تأويل المشكل لابن قتيبة: (لَتَنُوءُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ) أي تنهض بها مثقلة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r5.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the keys weigh down and tilt the company; he analyzes it as latunīʾu al-ʿuṣba, with the bāʾ removed when the tāʾ is opened, like other causative constructions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r5.anchor: قول الفراء - فى معاني القرآن، آية القصص: معناه ما إن مفاتحه لتنىِء العصبة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r6.speaker: الجوهري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r6.claim: Al-Jawharī says nāʾa can mean rising with effort or falling, making it a word of opposites.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r6.anchor: وقال الجوهرى: ناء ينوء نوءًا، نهض بجهد ومشقة وناء: سقط. وهو من الأضداد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r7.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r7.claim: Ibn Fāris derives the hamzated root from rising: anyone who rises while carrying a weight has nāʾa; the same form can describe a burden weighing someone down.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p563/r7.anchor: قال ابن فارس فى مادة نوى: وبالهمز: كلمة تدل على النهوض

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r1.claim: The excerpt continues a grammatical debate: one analysis treats the wording as an inversion like a rump weighing down its bearer, while some Kufans reject that explanation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r1.anchor: ذلك نحو: تنوء بها عجيزتها، وإنما توء هى بهاكما ينوء البعير بحمله. وبعض الكوفيين ينكره

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r2.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the keys weigh down and tilt the company: saying the company raises the keys would not itself show abundance, whereas the burden's weight conveys Qarun's vast treasure and follows the early gloss.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r3.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls al-Farrāʾ's reading best: the keys make the company lean under their weight, expressed by a causative construction.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r3.anchor: وقال القرطبى: أحسن ما قيل فيه: إن المعنى لتنىء العصبة أي تميلهم بثقلها، فلما انفتحت التاء دخلت الباء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān judges the bāʾ causative, meaning the keys make the company heavy; he attributes this analysis to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, and al-Farrāʾ, and says al-Naḥḥās chose it.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib relates the expression to the setting or inclination of a star: a load makes a person heavy and tilts him, until he falls.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r5.anchor: ناء به الحمل أثقله وأماله، وناء فلان أثقل فسقط

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r6.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says nāʾa bi-l-ḥaml means to rise carrying a weight, while nāʾa bihi al-ḥaml means the burden exhausts and tilts its bearer; the Qurʾānic wording stresses a load so great that even strong men tire under it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p564/r6.anchor: والذى يظهر لنا من إمعان النظر فى أقوالهم، أن: ناء بالحمل بمعنى نهض به مثقلا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r1.claim: Bint explains that al-Jāḥiẓ's comparison with spontaneous everyday speech answered those who claimed that isolated Qurʾānic phrases fit poetic meter, not Quraysh's charge that the Qurʾān was poetry.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r1.anchor: والجاحظ لا يسوق هذا الكلام، ردًّا على وصف قريش للقرآن بالشعر وإنما يرد على من التقطوا بعض آيات قرآنية زعموا أنها في وزن الشعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r2.claim: She rejects the comparison with servants, commoners, and sellers of eggplant as inadequate to defend the Qurʾān's supreme discourse from the charge of poetry.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r2.anchor: لكن يوهنه عندي، هذا التنظير بكلام العامة والسوقة، من الحاشية، والغلمان وباعة الباذنجان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r3.claim: Bint rejects al-Bāqillānī's suggestions that Quraysh meant some Qurʾānic passages matched poetic meters: they would not mistake a few lines for poetry, but recognized the Qurʾān's eloquent spell; al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said Arabs would reject the poet label and settle on sorcery that divides families.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p51/r3.anchor: ما قصدوا إلى أن فيه بعض فقرات موزونة وزن الشعر، ولا خطر لهم على بال أن يتعلقوا بآيات فيه على وزن بيت أو بيتين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r3.claim: Qur'anic inimitability has linguistic, scientific, historical, psychological, educational, and legal dimensions that continue to be discovered; no person or group in one era can exhaust them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r3.anchor: فالإعجاز القرآنيّ متعدِّدُ النواحي، متشعب الاتجاهات، ولا يزال الناس يكتشفون من مظاهر إعجازه الشيء الكثير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r4.claim: Different specialists can show how a single expression's artistry works from their disciplines, while a linguist identifies its exact word choice, order, and emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p8/r4.anchor: ويأتيك العالم في الطب ليقول من وجهة نظر الطب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.claim: Qārūn’s exemplary fate admonishes people seduced by worldly riches who forget God and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.anchor: people who were lured by the riches of this world and had forgotte n God and the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r2.claim: Abū Lahab occupies Qārūn’s role in Muḥammad’s community: his wealth made a trial for himself and others, and the example is meant to open such people’s eyes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r2.anchor: the same status as Q ārūn. He, too, was very proud of his wealth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r1.claim: Qārūn is identified in the Torah as Korah, mentioned in Numbers chapter 19.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r1.anchor: has been mentioned in the Torah in chapter 19 of the Book of Numbers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r2.claim: Korah was a Levite and Moses’ and Aaron’s cousin, jealous of their political and religious leadership and arguing that others had equal right to lead.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r2.anchor: the tribe to which Moses (sws) and Aaron (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r3.claim: Korah challenged Moses’ and Aaron’s superiority and conspired with members of the family to rebel against Moses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r4.speaker: The Torah
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r4.claim: The Torah recounts Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, with Reubenites Dathan, Abiram and another associate, rising against Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p569/r4.anchor: The Torah records: Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r1.speaker: The Torah
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r1.claim: The Torah says 250 Israelite community leaders joined the revolt, declaring the whole community holy and questioning Moses’ and Aaron’s authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r1.anchor: With them were 250 Israelite men, well-k nown community leaders who had been appointed members of the council.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r2.claim: Qārūn’s tyranny in the Qur’an refers to his rebellion against Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r2.anchor: It is this rebellion of his which

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r3.claim: The treasure and its keys indicate affluence, which fueled Qārūn’s rebellion and arrogance because he resented Moses’ and Aaron’s leadership.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r3.anchor: They actually point to the reason that made him rebellious and arrogant: since he was a very rich person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r4.claim: The keys are literal heavy latches: treasures were buried behind huge iron doors bolted with rods, requiring strong men to lift or fasten them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r4.anchor: A group of powerful men would be needed to lift or bolt the latch.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r5.claim: The heavy keys signify wealth just as heavy food cauldrons signify generosity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r5.anchor: Just as heavy cauldrons of food signify generosity, the existence of such keys is a sign of wealth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r6.claim: The wise among Qārūn’s people politely warned him not to be arrogant before God, who granted his wealth and dislikes the haughty, reminding him that such people are seized by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r6.anchor: when Korah adopted this attitude of rebelliousness, the wise among his nation tried to persuade him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r7.claim: Although “his people” is a general term, it refers here to the nation’s learned men; most supported Moses, while only a few with vested interests joined Qārūn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p570/r7.anchor: the majority of the nation was with Moses

NASHR:v1p449/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p449/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p449/r1.claim: The author rejects al-Dānī’s and al-Shāṭibī’s claim that لتنوء is written with an alif for hamza: its hamza is ḍamma, so its image would be wāw and is omitted by the usual rule.
NASHR:v1p449/r1.anchor: وذكر الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني (لتنوء بالعصبة) في القصص مما صورت الهمزة فيه ألفا

NASHR:v1p449/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p449/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p449/r2.claim: The following alif is extra after the plural wāw, by analogy with other words; the author says this may also explain أن تبوء بإثمي.
NASHR:v1p449/r2.anchor: والصواب أن صورة الهمزة منها محذوف على القياس، وهذه الألف وقعت زائدة كما كتبت في (يعبؤا)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī says a ʿuṣba is a group of fifteen to forty people.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال العصبة ما بين الخمس عشرة إلى الأربعين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says Qarun’s keys were made of camel hides.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال كانت من جلود الإبل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid also reports that the keys were made of camel hides.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال كانت مفاتيحه من جلود الإبل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r4.claim: Ibn Sīrīn relates that ʿUmar considered making dirhams from camel hides, but abandoned the idea when told it would exhaust the camels.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن سيرين أن عمر بن الخطاب أراد أن يضرب من جلود الإبل دراهم فقالوا إذا يفنى الإبل فتركها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
