ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r5.claim: Mujāhid gives the group’s size as fifteen men.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p92#3/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال العصبة خمسة عشر رجلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#507/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#507/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#507/r5.claim: In Qārūn’s story, the إن clause is the relative clause of ما; Sībawayh paraphrases the construction with an inserted oath, ما والله إن شره خير من جيد ما معك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#507/r5.anchor: فإن صلة لما كأنك قلت ما والله إن شره خير من جيد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r1.claim: Qārūn is a foreign proper name and is diptote for proper-name status and foreign origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r1.anchor: قارون اسم اعجمي منع الصرف للعلمية والعجمة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r2.claim: Qārūn was from the Israelites; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r2.anchor: كان من قوم موسى أي من بني اسرائيل كما هو الظاهر وحكى ابن عطية الاجماع عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jurayj, Qatāda, and Ibrāhīm report Qārūn was Moses's cousin, with lineage traced through Qahath and Levi to Jacob.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r3.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وابن جريج وقتادة وابراهيم أنه ابن عم موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r4.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r4.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān transmits from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that Qārūn was Moses's maternal cousin, also reported from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r4.anchor: وفي مجمع البيان عن عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه ابن خالة موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says Qārūn was Moses's paternal uncle on the lineage he describes.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r5.anchor: وحكي عن محمد بن إسحاق أنه عم موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r6.claim: Qārūn was called al-Munawwar for beauty and was Israel's foremost Torah memorizer and reciter, but became a hypocrite like the Samaritan.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r6.anchor: وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته وكان أحفظ بني اسرائيل للتوراة وأقرأهم لكنه نافق كما نافق السامري

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r7.claim: A report says Qārūn resented Moses's prophethood and Aaron's priestly role after the sea crossing, since sacrifice went to Aaron; he asked why he had no similar standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r7.anchor: لما جاوز بهم موسى عليه السلام البحر وصارت الرسالة والحبورة لهرون يقرب القربان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r8.claim: Moses says the arrangement was God's doing; Qārūn demands a sign, but dismisses Aaron's sprouting staff as magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r8.anchor: قال موسى عليه السلام هذا صنع الله تعالى قال والله تعالى لا أصدقك حتى تأتي بآية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r9.claim: Baghy means seeking superiority and control, arrogance, or oppression and demanding what was not one's right.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r9.anchor: فطلب الفضل عليهم وأن يكونوا تحت أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r10.claim: One report says he lengthened clothes by a span; another says Pharaoh appointed him over Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p109#4/r10.anchor: قيل : وذلك حين ملكه فرعون على بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r1.claim: Qārūn envied Moses and Aaron and wanted their blessings removed; the fa may explain his wrongdoing or mark consequence, since kinship can prompt oppression.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r1.anchor: وقيل حسدهم وطلب زوال نعمهم وذلك ما ذكر منه في حق موسى وهرون عليهما السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r2.claim: The treasures are stored wealth, metaphorically treated as buried treasure if kanz is restricted to buried wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r2.anchor: أي الاموال المدخرة فهو مجاز بجعل المدخر كالمدفون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r3.claim: One view says the wealth was called treasure because Qārūn paid no zakāt despite Moses ordering him to, causing their enmity.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r3.anchor: وحكي في البحر أنه سميت أمواله كنوزا لأنها لم تؤد منها الزكاة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r4.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r4.claim: A report from ʿAṭāʾ says God gave Qārūn a buried treasure from Joseph's hoards.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r4.anchor: وكان كما روي عن عطاء قد أظفره الله تعالى بكنز عظيم من كنوز يوسف عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r5.claim: Mafātiḥ means keys to chests, with an omitted genitive or close association; it is plural of maftaḥ, an opening instrument.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r5.anchor: أي مفاتح صناديقه فهو على تقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r6.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says treasuries; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says vessels or containers, likewise reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r6.anchor: وقال السدي : أي خزائنه وفي معناه قول الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r7.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r7.claim: If mafātiḥ means treasuries, its singular is a place noun; al-Aʿmash's mafātīḥu reading supports the key interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r7.anchor: وقياس واحدة على هذا المفتح بالفتح لأنه اسم مكان ويؤيد ما تقدم قراءة الأعمش مفاتيحه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r8.claim: ما is relative and the second object of آتينا; mafātiḥ is the noun of إنّ, and its clause is both predicate and relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r8.anchor: والجملة صلة ما والعائد الضمير المجرور

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r9.claim: The Kūfans prohibit an إنّ-initial relative clause; al-Naḥḥās quotes al-Akhfash rejecting their restriction by citing this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r9.anchor: ومنع الكوفيون جواز كون الجملة المصدرة بان صلة للموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r10.claim: If the objection is lack of precedent, the verse is not unambiguous because ما may be an indefinite noun with an adjectival clause; if it is syntactic linkage, the verse rebuts it for either clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r11.claim: Nāʾa bihi means a load weighs someone down until it tilts him; the ba is causative, as in ذهبت به.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r11.anchor: فالباء للتعدية كما في ذهبت به

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r12.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿuṣbah means a large group without a fixed number, though lexicographers offer several ranges.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r12.anchor: والعصبة الجماعة الكثيرة من غير تعيين لعدد خاص على ماذكره الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r13.claim: Reported sizes include ten to fifteen (Mujāhid), fifteen to forty (al-Kalbī), three to ten, ten to forty (Qatāda), forty (Ibn ʿAbbās), and seventy (Abū Ṣāliḥ).

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r14.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r14.claim: Abū Zayd derives the verb from rising while carrying a load and cites a poem about a camel's hindquarters rising before it tires.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r14.anchor: وقال أبو زيد : تنوء من نوت بالحمل إذا نهضت به قال الشاعر : تنوء بأخراها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah and others see inversion, with the group carrying keys; another reading says the keys rise with the group lifting them.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r15.anchor: وفي الآية على هذا قلب عند أبي عبيدة ومن تبعه والأصل تنوء بها أي تنهض

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r16.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r16.claim: Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Farrāʾ, and al-Naḥḥās prefer the straightforward transitive reading; similar sense is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and al-Suddī.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r16.anchor: والأولى ما قدمناه أولا وهو منقول عن الخليل وسيبويه والفراء واختاره النحاس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r17.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r17.claim: Budayl reads the verb with masculine yāʾ, لينوء, prompting an explanation for its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r17.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة ( لينوء ) بالياء التحتية وخرج ذلك أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r18.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r18.claim: Abū Ḥayyān supplies an omitted masculine noun such as load or amount of the keys; Ibn Jinnī treats that amount as one unit and cites rajaz.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r18.anchor: أي ما إن حمل مفاتحه أو مقدارها أو نحو ذلك وقال ابن جني : ذهب بالتذكير إلى ذلك القدر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r19.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r19.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains masculine agreement by construing mafātiḥ as treasuries; al-Kashf calls this weak because it loses emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r19.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : وجهه أن يفسر المفاتح بالخزائن ويعطيها حكم ما أضيفت اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r20.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī says Budayl read mafātiḥ in the singular, so masculine agreement needs no reinterpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r20.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو الداني أن بديل بن ميسرة قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r21.speaker: خيثمة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r21.claim: Khaythamah reports sixty decorated mules carrying keys, one key per treasure; another version gives seventy mules and leather keys, one per storehouse.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p110/r21.anchor: فروي عن خيثمة أنها كانت وقر ستين بغلا أغر محجلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r1.claim: Al-Baḥr excludes extravagant key stories as false or nearly so; Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for treasuries carried by forty men, with a reported four hundred thousand keys, ten thousand per man.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r1.anchor: وفي البحر ذكروا من كثرة مفاتحه ما هو كذب أو يقارب الكذب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r2.claim: Abū Muslim takes keys as knowledge, like the keys of the unseen in 6:59; al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r2.anchor: وأبعد أبو مسلم في تفسير الآية فقال : المراد من المفاتح العلم والاحاطة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches إذ قال to تنوء, though the burdening is not limited to that time.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري : هو متعلق بتنوء وضعف بأن اثقال المفاتح

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches it to بغى, subject to the same objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : ببغي وضعف بنحو ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ attaches it to آتينا, also facing the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : بآتينا ويجوز أن يكون ظرفا لمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r6.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r6.claim: Al-Ḥawfī treats it as governed by an omitted اذكر; another proposal attaches it to the following قال إنما أوتيته.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers an implicit phrase that Qārūn displayed pride in his gifts when his people admonished him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r7.anchor: ورجح تعلقه بمحذوف والتقدير أظهر التفاخر والفرح بما أوتي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r8.claim: 'Do not rejoice' means do not become arrogant; worldly joy for its own sake is blameworthy because of love for the world and forgetting its pleasures pass.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r8.anchor: لا تبطر والفرح بالدنيا لذاتها مذموم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r9.speaker: أبو الطيب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r9.claim: Abū al-Ṭayyib says greatest grief comes amid joy whose owner knows it will leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r9.anchor: كما قال أبو الطيب : أشد الغم عندي في سرور تيقن عنه صاحبه انتقالا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r10.speaker: ابن شمس الخلافة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r10.claim: Ibn Shams al-Khilāfah says transient hardship is better than transient pleasure.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r10.anchor: وقال ابن شمس الخلافة : وإذا نظرت فان بؤسا زائلا للمرء خير من نعيم زائل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r11.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r11.claim: Arab poets praise restraint at good fortune: one rejects exulting in fortune or despairing at its turns; another likewise praises moderation.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p111/r11.anchor: والعرب تمدح بترك الفرح عند اقبال الخير قال الشاعر : ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r1.claim: Worldly joy is not blameworthy when one rejoices in worldly things as a means toward an afterlife purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r1.anchor: لأن الفرح بها لكونها وسيلة إلى أمر من أمور الآخرة غير مذموم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r2.claim: The verse decisively establishes worldly joy is religiously censured; many theologians take God's love as an act meaning He does not favor such people, but hates, humiliates, and distances them.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r2.anchor: فهو دليل إني على كون الفرح بالدنيا مذموما شرعا وإنما قلنا إن الفرح بها لذاتها مذموم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r3.claim: Some say God's withholding love alone suffices as deterrence apart from hatred and punishment; al-Ālūsī approves.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن في نفي محبته تعالى إياهم تنبيها على أن عدم محبته تعالى كاف في الزجر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: In له صوت صوت حمار, the repeated noun is accusative by an implied action meaning يصوت; it is not an adjective or appositive to صوت.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.anchor: فإنما انتصب هذا لأنك مررت به فى حال تصويت

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: With an explicit verb such as يصوت, the following accusative can give the sound’s model or be a circumstantial comparison; an implicit verb can also govern it.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.anchor: فإذا قلت مررت به فإذا هو يصوت صوت الحمار فعلى الفعل غير

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: An indefinite sound noun can be construed as a simile with مثل understood; a definite noun cannot be a circumstantial accusative or modify an indefinite noun in the same way.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.anchor: فإذا أخرجت مثل قام المصدر النكرة مقام مثل لأنه مثله نكرة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: Al-Khalīl allows صوت الحمار to describe the indefinite صوت as a simile; Sībawayh calls the analogous construction رجل أخو زيد weak and restricted to poetic necessity.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنه يجوز له صوت صوت الحمار

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: Al-Nābigha’s repeated صريف exemplifies a sound noun after له; lines by Ruʾbah, al-ʿAjjāj, and Abū Kabīr show related accusatives explained through implied verbal action.

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: Sībawayh says the echo suffix follows the final vowel: wāw after ḍamma, yāʾ after kasra, alif after fatḥa; a final consonant cluster is broken by moving the consonant.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: فالزيادة تتبع الحرف الذي هو قبلها

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: The suffix marks a challenging echo that can reject the speaker’s position, express surprise, or deny that a reported event occurred.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: فتقول أزيدنيه غير راد عليه متعجبا

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: Attach the suffix once at the end of the entire echoed utterance, including a coordinated phrase or an adjective.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: قلت أزيدا وعمرنيه تجعل العلامة في منتهى الكلام

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: A following vocative such as يا فتى is outside the reported utterance and prevents the suffix from attaching, as other endings are dropped in that connection.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: وإن قلت أزيدا يا فتى تركت

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: Some Arabs insert إن between the name and suffix to make the marker clearer, since the hāʾ and yāʾ are otherwise faint.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: واعلم أن من العرب من يجعل

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: رجل من أهل البادية
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: Sībawayh reports a Bedouin answering أنا إنيه when asked whether he would go out once the steppe became lush, illustrating denial of the questioner's assumption.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: وسمعنا رجلا من أهل البادية قيل له

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: The speaker may echo the actual words or append the marker to wording that conveys the intended correction; the marker may also be omitted.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: الزيادة ما لفظ به وتحكيه مبادرة له

SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.claim: Do not use the echo suffix when asking for confirmation or guidance rather than rejecting the reported statement.
SIBAWAYH:إذاأنكرتأنتثبترأيهعلىماذكرأوتنك.anchor: إذا قال ضربت زيدا فإنك لا تلحق الزيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r1.claim: With fatḥa, أن has four uses: it can nominalize a clause, mean أي, be redundant, or be a lightened form of heavy أن.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r2.claim: إن can mark a conditional clause or introduce a statement in an oath context, as in the cited Qur'anic examples.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r2.anchor: فتكون للمجازاة وتكون أن يبتدأ ما بعدها في معنى اليمين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r3.speaker: رجل من أهل المدينة موثوق به
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r3.claim: A trusted Medinan informant reports hearing an Arab say إن زيد لذاهب; Sībawayh identifies this lightened إن with the form in the cited verse.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r3.anchor: عن رجل من أهل المدينة موثوق به

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r4.claim: In إن الكافرون إلا في غرور, إن means ما, giving the sense “the disbelievers are only in delusion.”

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r5.claim: The construction ما إن زيد ذاهب has an independent initial clause; Sībawayh cites Furwa ibn Maysik's ما إن طبنا as poetic evidence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأنإن)#509/r5.anchor: وقال فروة بن مسيك # % وما إن طبنا جبن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r1.claim: Baghawī says Qarūn was Moses’ cousin and gives their shared lineage through Qāhith and Yaṣhar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r1.anchor: كان ابن عمه؛ لأنه قارون بن يصهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq instead says Qarūn was Moses’ paternal uncle, Amram’s brother, and both were sons of Yaṣhar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r2.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان قارون عم موسى، كان أخا عمران، وهما ابنا يصهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r3.claim: Qarūn was the most learned Israelite in Torah, but became a hypocrite like al-Sāmirī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r3.anchor: ولم يكن في بني إسرائيل أقرأ للتوراة من قارون، ولكنه نافق كما نافق السامري

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r4.claim: One account says Qarūn was Pharaoh’s agent over the Israelites and oppressed them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r4.anchor: قيل: كان عاملا لفرعون على بني إسرائيل، فكان يبغي عليهم ويظلمهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r5.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r5.claim: Qatāda says Qarūn transgressed against them through his wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: بغى عليهم بكثرة المال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r6.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Qarūn transgressed through associating partners with God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r7.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r7.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab says Qarūn transgressed by lengthening his garment by a handspan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r7.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: زاد في طول ثيابه شبرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar quotes the Prophet saying that God will not look on Resurrection Day at one who drags his garment out of pride.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r8.anchor: وروينا عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r9.claim: Another explanation says Qarūn transgressed through pride and arrogance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r10.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r10.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and others take mafātiḥ as the keys used to open doors.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r11.claim: Another view takes mafātiḥ as the treasuries, as in 6:59.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r12.claim: The keys were so heavy they burdened and tilted the strong group carrying them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r12.anchor: أي: لتثقلهم، وتميل بهم إذا حملوها لثقلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls the wording inverted: the group is weighed down by the keys; nāʾa means to rise under a heavy burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r13.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: هذا من المقلوب، تقديره: ما إن العصبة لتنوء بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r14.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r14.claim: Mujāhid defines the group as ten to fifteen people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r14.anchor: قال مجاهد: ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r15.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, gives the range as three to ten.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r15.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r16.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r16.claim: Qatāda defines the group as ten to forty people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r16.anchor: وقال قتادة: ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r17.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r17.claim: One view says the group consisted of forty men; another says seventy.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that forty of the strongest men carried Qarūn’s keys.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r18.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان يحمل مفاتحه أربعون رجلا أقوى ما يكون من الرجال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r19.speaker: خيثمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r19.claim: Khaythama says he found in the Gospel that Qarūn’s treasury keys loaded sixty mules, each key no longer than a finger and each opening a treasure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p220/r19.anchor: وقال جرير عن منصور عن خيثمة، قال: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r1.speaker: ويقال
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r1.claim: One account says Qarūn carried the keys everywhere; after iron became too heavy, he tried wood, then cowhide, and the keys went with him on forty mules.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r1.anchor: ويقال: كان قارون أينما ذهب يحمل معه مفاتيح كنوزه، وكانت من حديد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r2.claim: The command not to rejoice means not to become arrogant, insolent, or frolicsome.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r2.anchor: لا تبطر ولا تأشر ولا تمرح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r3.claim: The disfavored rejoicers are arrogant people who do not thank God for what He has given them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221/r3.anchor: الأشرين البطرين الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r3.claim: Qarun was Moses' cousin, son of Yaṣhar b. Qāhith b. Levi, and was among those who believed in Moses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r3.anchor: كان ابن عمه يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوي وكان ممن آمن به

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r4.claim: His transgression meant seeking superiority over his people and wanting them under his command, behaving arrogantly, or oppressing them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r4.anchor: فطلب الفضل عليهم وأن يكونوا تحت أمره، أو تكبر عليهم أو ظلمهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r5.claim: One report says this occurred when Pharaoh put Qarun in charge of the Israelites.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r5.anchor: قيل وذلك حين ملكه فرعون على بني إسرائيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r6.claim: A report says Qarun envied Moses and Aaron, complaining that Moses had prophecy and Aaron priesthood while he had nothing; Moses replied that this was God's arrangement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r6.anchor: لما روي أنه قال لموسى عليه السلام: لك الرسالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r7.anchor: من الأموال المدخرة. { ما إن مفاتحه } مفاتيح صناديقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r8.claim: مفاتحه means the keys to his chests, from the singular مفتح with kasra, the tool used to open; alternatively it means his treasuries, from مفتح.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r8.anchor: مفاتيح صناديقه جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به، وقيل خزائنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r9.claim: The keys weigh heavily on a strong band of people; تنوء means to bear a load that bends or inclines someone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r9.anchor: والجملة صلة وهو ثاني مفعولي آتى، ونائبه الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r10.claim: A reading has لينوء with yāʾ, giving the genitive complement the syntactic status of its governing noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r10.anchor: وقرىء «لينوء» بالياء على إعطاء المضاف حكم المضاف إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r11.claim: The time clause إذ قال له قومه is governed by تنوء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r11.anchor: { إذ قال له قومه } منصوب ب «تنوء»

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r12.claim: لا تفرح means do not become arrogant in worldly joy; it is blameworthy because worldly pleasure departs, and knowing it must end brings grief. The verse links this to 57:23.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r12.anchor: لا تبطر والفرح بالدنيا مذموم مطلقا لأنه نتيجة حبها والرضا بها والذهول عن ذهابها

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r13.claim: God does not love those exulting in worldly ornament; such joy blocks love of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:75-76/r13.anchor: وعلل النهي ها هنا بكونه مانعا من محبة الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.claim: After the partners’ helplessness in the Hereafter, the text shows God’s rule in this world by destroying arrogant people who cannot save one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.anchor: ولما دل على عجزهم في تلك الدار , وعلمهم أن المتصرف في جميع الأقدار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r2.claim: The general warning about towns ruined for their prosperity is applied to Qarun as a particular example.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r2.anchor: تطبيقا لعموم { وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r3.claim: Qarun’s destruction warns those who accuse the Prophet of magic and shows that prophets separate from the wretched even when they are close kin.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r3.anchor: تخويفا لمن كذب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , لا سيما من نسبه غلى السحر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r4.claim: God destroyed Qarun and his companions with an unprecedented punishment, though they were Israelites and among Moses’ closest people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r4.anchor: عذب قارون ومن كان معه بعذاب لم يسبقهم فيه أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.claim: Those who boast in gifts must recognize God’s right in what the messengers and scriptures teach; worldly possessions cannot save those who rely on them as if they secured lasting happiness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.anchor: أن الحق لله في كل ما دعت إليه رسله , ونطقت به كتبه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.claim: Their worldly dependence resembles the spider that takes a house, a comparison found in the following sūra.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.anchor: كما يأتي في التي بعده كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r7.claim: Moses witnessed Qarun’s rejection and accusation of magic but did not pray against him, since arrogance removed him from the promise to aid the oppressed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r7.anchor: حين كذبه ونسبه إلى السحر وتكبر عليه , فلم يسأل الله تعالى فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r8.claim: Qarun’s punishment resembles Pharaoh’s in concealing them from sight: Pharaoh was submerged in liquid, while Qarun was buried in solid earth, demonstrating God’s power.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r8.anchor: من جنس ما عذب به فرعون في الصورة من حيث إنه تغييب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r9.claim: Moses selected a witness from each Israelite tribe; the account continues in the next segment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r9.anchor: من كل سبط من أسباط بني إسرائيل شهيدا من عصبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r1.claim: Qarun is called Qorach in the Torah.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r1.anchor: { إن قارون } ويسمى في التوراة قورح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r2.claim: Qarun was one of the believers in Moses and belonged to the people promised divine favor after oppression.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r2.anchor: أنه كان من الذين آمنوا به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by Abu Hayyan and others, says Qarun was Moses’ cousin.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r4.claim: Qarun transgresses by despising his people because of wealth, cutting his bonds with them and joining Pharaoh’s party; this moves him from favor and trust into ruin and betrayal.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r4.anchor: تجاوز الحد في احتقارهم بما خولناه فيه من هذا الحطام المتلاشي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r5.claim: The preposition ʿalā signals overbearing and marks Qarun’s willful departure from proper conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r5.anchor: المقتضية للاستعلاء تنبيها على خروجها عن أصلها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r6.claim: Kunūz are buried and stored wealth, in addition to visible property ready to spend on needs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r6.anchor: الأموال المدفونة المدخرة , فضلا عن الظاهرة التي هي بصدد الإنفاق منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r7.claim: The treasure keys are so heavy that a strong, mutually supporting group strains under them; the layered wording conveys wealth beyond anyone of Qarun’s rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r7.anchor: وفي المبالغة بالتعبير بالكنوز والمفاتيح والنوء والعصبة الموصوفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r8.claim: The keys open the locks behind the doors of the places where Qarun’s treasure was stored.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r8.anchor: مفتاح الأغلاق التي هو مدفون فيما وراء أبوابها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r9.claim: Tanūʾ means to tilt or strain with effort under a heavy burden.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r10.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r10.claim: Al-Razi explains that nuʾ is a star setting from view, and gives both senses of carrying a load: rising under its weight and being tilted by it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r10.anchor: قال الرازي : والنوء : الكوكب مال عن العين عند الغروب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r11.claim: The next phrase identifies the time when Qarun’s people spoke and introduces the cause of his transgression.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r11.anchor: ولما ذكر بغيه , ذكر وقته , والوقت قد يكون واسعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r12.claim: Moses’ tribal witnesses were told to bring proof about the priesthood; Aaron’s staff blossomed while theirs did not, showing that God decides priesthood and all affairs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p517/r12.anchor: وقال لهم : هاتوا برهانكم فيها , فعلموا بإبراق عصا هاورن عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r1.claim: Although the verse attributes the counsel to Qarun’s whole people, only some spoke; either the rest agreed or only the righteous count as people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r1.anchor: وساغت نسبة القول للكل وإن كان القائل البعض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r2.claim: The warning targets joy in perishable wealth that settles into the heart and burns into arrogance and insolence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r2.anchor: لا تسر سرورا يحفر في قلبك فيتغلغل فيه فيحرقك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r3.claim: Rejoicing in transient possessions shows reliance on them and forgetfulness of the afterlife; it reflects ignorance and poor judgment, leading to arrogance and ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r3.anchor: فإن الفرح بالعرض الزائل يدل على الركون إليه , وذلك يدل على نسيان الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r4.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r4.claim: Al-Razi says rejoicing in what is not worth rejoicing over brings grief that never ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r4.anchor: قال الرزاي : ومن فرح بغير مفروح به استجلب حزنا لا انقضاء له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r5.claim: God’s perfection is what merits joy; people deeply rejoicing in what perishes reveal low aspirations, and God does not treat them as beloved.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r5.anchor: الذي له صفات الكمال فلا شيء أجل منه , فبه ينبغي أن يفرح

DURR-FULL:v6p436/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Qarun was Moses's cousin, studied until he amassed knowledge, then envied Moses and rebelled; he rejected the alms command and plotted to have a woman falsely accuse Moses.
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} قال: كان ابن عمه وكان يبتغي العلم حتى جمع علما

DURR-FULL:v6p436/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r2.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas's account Moses says God commanded worship without partners, kinship, and stoning a married adulterer; the woman later recanted her paid accusation and testified Moses was innocent and God's messenger.
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} قال: كان ابن عمه

DURR-FULL:v6p436/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r3.speaker: الله تعالى
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r3.claim: God grants Moses control over the earth; Moses sinks Qarun's followers in stages despite their cries, and God reproaches him, saying He would have answered had they called Him.
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r3.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه: ما يبكيك قد سلطناك على الأرض فمرها فتطيعك

DURR-FULL:v6p436/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas connects Qarun's fate to the verse saying God caused the earth to swallow him and his house, sinking him to the lowest earth.
DURR-FULL:v6p436/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وذلك قوله تعالى {فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض} وخسف به إلى الأرض السفلى

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r1.claim: Ibrahim says Qarun was Moses's cousin.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم رضي الله عنه قال: كان قارون ابن عم موسى

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives Qarun and Moses's lineage as cousins through their fathers, with alternate forms Fahith or Qahith and an Arabic form ʿImran for ʿArmum.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} قال: كان ابن عمه أخي أبي قارون بن مصر بن فاهث

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r3.claim: Qatada says Qarun was Moses's paternal cousin, crossed the sea with Israel, was called al-Nur for his beautiful Torah recitation, then hypocritically rebelled like al-Samiri and was destroyed.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله قال: كان قارون ابن عم موسى أخي أبيه وكان قطع البحر مع بني إسرائيل وكان يسمى النور

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r4.claim: Qatada says Qarun transgressed because of his great wealth and children.

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r5.claim: Qatada glosses bagha as rising over or lording it over them.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فبغى عليهم} قال: فعلا عليهم

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r6.claim: Shahr b. Hawshab says Qarun's transgression was adding a span to the length of his clothes.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r6.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم} قال: زاد عليهم في طول ثيابه شبرا

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r7.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r7.claim: ʿAta says Qarun found one of Joseph's hoards.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r7.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه في قوله {وآتيناه من الكنوز} قال: أصاب كنزا من كنوز يوسف

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r8.speaker: الوليد بن زوران
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r8.claim: Al-Walid b. Zawran also says Qarun found one of Joseph's hoards.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r8.anchor: عن الوليد بن زوران رضي الله عنه في قوله {وآتيناه من الكنوز} قال: أصاب كنزا من كنوز يوسف

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r9.speaker: الوليد بن زوران
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r9.claim: Al-Walid b. Zawran alternatively says Qarun knew alchemy.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r9.anchor: عن الوليد بن زوران رضي الله عنه في قوله {وآتيناه من الكنوز} قال: كان قارون يعلم الكيمياء

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r10.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r10.claim: Salman reports the Prophet saying Qarun's estate had a silver floor and a gold foundation.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r10.anchor: عن سلمان رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت أرض دار قارون من فضة وأساسها من ذهب

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r11.speaker: خيثمة
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r11.claim: Khaythama says he found in the Gospel that Qarun's keys were carried by sixty fine camels, each key no larger than a finger.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r11.anchor: عن خيثمة رضي الله عنه قال: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون كانت وقر ستين بغلا غرا محجلة

DURR-FULL:v6p437/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r12.speaker: خيثمة
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r12.claim: In another report Khaythama says the keys were made of hide, each opened a separate storehouse, and seventy camels carried them when Qarun rode.
DURR-FULL:v6p437/r12.anchor: عن خيثمة رضي الله عنه قال: كانت مفاتيح كنوز قارون من جلود كل مفتاح على خزانة على حدة

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r1.claim: Mujahid says Qarun's treasure keys were made from camel hides.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: كانت المفاتيح من جلود الإبل

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says even a group of strong men could not lift the keys.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {لتنوء بالعصبة} يقول: لا يرفعها العصبة من الرجال {أولي القوة}

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains to Nafiʿ b. al-Azraq that تنوء means to weigh heavily; he confirms Arab usage with Imruʾ al-Qays’s line using ينوء for bearing a load.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {لتنوء بالعصبة} قال: لتثقل

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r4.claim: Mujahid defines a ʿuṣbah as ten to fifteen men and says the strong group numbered fifteen.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال العصبة ما بين العشرة إلى الخمسة عشر و {أولي القوة} خمسة عشر

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r5.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi gives the ʿuṣbah a range of fifteen to forty men.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r5.anchor: عن الكلبي قال {بالعصبة} ما بين الخمس عشرة إلى الأربعين

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the ʿuṣbah as forty men.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال {بالعصبة} أربعون رجلا

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r7.claim: Qatada reports the ʿuṣbah as more than ten and up to forty men.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: كنا نحدث أن {بالعصبة} ما فوق العشرة إلى الأربعين

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r8.speaker: أبو صالح مولى أم هانىء
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r8.claim: Abu Salih says the ʿuṣbah numbered seventy men.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح مولى أم هانىء قال {بالعصبة} سبعون رجلا

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r9.speaker: أبو صالح مولى أم هانىء
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r9.claim: Abu Salih adds that Qarun's treasury was carried on forty mules.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r9.anchor: قال: وكانت خزانته تحمل على أربعين بغلا

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r10.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r10.claim: Al-Suddi identifies Qarun's advisers as believers from his people, who warned him not to exult lest he become insolent.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r10.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح} قال: هم المؤمنون منهم قالوا: يا قارون لا تفرح بما أوليت فتبطر

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses the condemned exultation as giddiness, arrogance, insolence, and failure to thank God for His gifts.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} قال: المرحين الأشرين البطرين الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r12.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet saying that God loves every sorrowful heart.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r12.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله يحب كل قلب حزين

DURR-FULL:v6p438/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r13.claim: A report from Abu Dharr urges visiting graves and washing the dead to remember the Hereafter, saying grief places one in God's shade; al-Hakim authenticated it, while al-Bayhaqi called its text munkar.
DURR-FULL:v6p438/r13.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زر القبور تذكر بها الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r1.claim: Mujahid says the condemned joy here means transgression (baghy).
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} قال: الفرح هنا البغي

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the condemned joy as insolent pride (baṭar).
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r2.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} قال: إن الله لا يحب بطرا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Qārūn was a cousin of Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ان قارون كان من قوم موسى قال : كان ابن عمه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r2.claim: Qatāda says Qārūn was Moses’s paternal cousin and crossed the sea with the Children of Israel.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال : وكان قارون ابن عم موسى اخي أبيه وكان قطع البحر مع بني اسرائيل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r3.claim: Qatāda says Qārūn was called al-Munawwar for his beautiful voice reciting the Torah.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قال : وكان قارون ابن عم موسى اخي أبيه وكان قطع البحر مع بني اسرائيل وكان يسمى المنور من حسن صوته بالتوراة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r4.claim: Qatāda says Qārūn became a hypocrite like al-Sāmirī and was destroyed for transgression; his wealth and children drove his oppression, as the next verse says.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r4.anchor: ولكن عدو الله نافق كما نافق السامري فاهلكه الله لبغيه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل وإبراهيم النخعي وسماك بن حرب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r5.claim: Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and Simāk ibn Ḥarb are also reported to say Qārūn was Moses’s cousin.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r5.anchor: وروي ، عن عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل وابراهيم النخعي ، وسماك بن حرب انهم قالوا كان ابن عم موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that people tried to frame Moses for adultery by bribing a woman to accuse him; she instead testified to his innocence and prophethood. God then told Moses that the earth would obey him, so he could command it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3005/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان موسى يقول لبني اسرائيل ان الله عز وجل يامركم بكذا وكذا حتى دخل عليكم في اموالكم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets Qārūn’s transgression as unbelief in God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : فبغى عليهم قال : الكفر بالله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r2.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r2.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab says Qārūn transgressed by lengthening his garment by a span.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r2.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب ان قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم قال : زاد في طول ثيابه شبرا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r3.claim: Qatāda links Qārūn’s hypocrisy and destruction to his transgression, caused by his abundant wealth and children; he cites the following verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r3.anchor: عن قتادة يعني قوله : فبغى عليهم ولكن عدو الله نافق كما نافق السامري فاهلكه الله ببغيه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses his transgression as acting superior over his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : فبغى عليهم قال : فعلا عليهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Qārūn found one of Joseph’s hidden treasures.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r5.anchor: عن عثمان بن عطاء ، عن أبيه في قوله : واتيناه من الكنوز قال : اصاب كنزا من كنوز يوسف

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r6.speaker: الوليد بن زروان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r6.claim: Al-Walīd ibn Zarwān says Qārūn practiced alchemy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r6.anchor: عن الوليد ابن زروان في قوله : واتيناه من الكنوز قال : كان قارون يعمل الكيميا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r7.speaker: خيثمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r7.claim: Khaythama says the leather keys were finger-sized, each opened a separate storehouse, and sixty gray, white-footed camels carried them when Qārūn rode.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r7.anchor: عن الاعمش ، عن خيثمة قال : كانت مفاتيح كنوز قارون من جلود ، كل مفتاح مثل الاصبع

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r8.speaker: خيثمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r8.claim: A second report from Khaythama says leather keys were carried by forty gray, white-footed camels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3006/r8.anchor: عن الاعمش ، عن خيثمة ما ان مفاتحه قال : كانت المفاتيح من جلود يحملها اربعون بغلا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the keys were made of camel hide.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ان مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة اولي القوة كانت المفاتيح من جلود الابل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r2.claim: Abū Razīn glosses the keys as the storehouses; al-Suddī is also reported to give this gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r2.anchor: سالت أبا رزين ، عن قوله : ما ان مفاتحه قال : خزائنه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r3.claim: Al-Suddī is reported to gloss the keys as the storehouses, like Abū Razīn.

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the keys as the containers or receptacles.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ما ان مفاتحه قال : اوعيته

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r5.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r5.claim: Abū Razīn says even the contents secured by one key would suffice the people of Kufa; the verse means his treasures.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r5.anchor: عن أبي رزين في قوله : ما ان مفاتحه قال : ان كان مفتاح واحد لكافي اهل الكوفة ، انما يعني كنوزه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح والسدي وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, al-Suddī, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd gloss تنوء as weighing heavily.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : لتنوء بالعصبة يقول : تثقل . وروي ، عن أبي صالح - والسدي وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas offers a different gloss for تنوء: to pass by or over the group.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r7.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس قوله : لتنوء بالعصبة قال : لتمر بالعصبة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r8.speaker: أبو صالح مولى أم هانئ
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r8.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of Umm Hāniʾ, says the group numbered seventy men.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح مولى أم هانئ في قول الله عز وجل : ما ان مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة قال : العصبة سبعون رجلا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r9.speaker: الحكم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r9.claim: Al-Ḥakam says the group numbered forty men.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r9.anchor: عن الحجاج بن ارطاة ، عن الحكم لتنوء بالعصبة قال : العصبة اربعون رجلا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r10.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says Qārūn’s storehouse was carried on forty mules.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3007/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله : لتنوء بالعصبة قال : كانت خزانته تحمل على اربعين بغلا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح وقتادة والضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk are also reported to say Qārūn’s storehouse was carried on forty mules.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r1.anchor: وروي ، عن ابن عباس وابي صالح وقتادة والضحاك مثل ذلك . الوجه الثالث :

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r2.claim: Al-Suddī defines the group as between ten and forty people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r2.anchor: عن السدي ما ان مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة والعصبة ما بين العشرة إلى الاربعين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r3.claim: Mujāhid defines the group as ten to fifteen people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ما ان مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة ما بين العشرة إلى الخمسة عشرة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd defines the group as three to nine people, a small band.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r4.anchor: ثنا عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قوله : لتنوء بالعصبة اولي القوة قال : العصبة ما بين ثلاثة إلى تسعة وهم النفر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says a group numbers six or seven.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قلت : كم العصبة ؟ قال : ست أو سبع

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the strong people numbered fifteen.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : اولي القوة قال : خمسة عشرة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r7.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the people who advised Qārūn as believers among his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r7.anchor: عن السدي اذ قال له قومه لا تفرح قال : هؤلاء المؤمنون منهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says they warned Qārūn not to become insolent because of what he had received.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r8.anchor: به ، عن السدي اذ قال له قومه لا تفرح قال : هؤلاء المؤمنون منهم قالوا : يا قارون بما اوتيت فتبطر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r9.claim: Qatāda glosses لا تفرح as do not praise or boast about yourself.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r9.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اذ قال له قومه لا تفرح اي : لا تمدح

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r10.claim: Mujāhid describes the disfavored exultant as self-praising, insolent, arrogant, and ungrateful for God’s gifts.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3008/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ان الله لا يحب الفرحين المتمدحين الاشرين البطرين الذين لا يشكرون الله فيما اعطاهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r1.claim: Mujāhid says joy in this context means transgression.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : لا تفرح ان الله لا يحب الفرحين قال : الفرح هاهنا البغي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the word as المرحين, and Qatāda is reported to give the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ان الله لا يحب الفرحين يقول : المرحين . وروي ، عن قتادة مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says God does not love rejoicing that is boastful and insolent.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3009/r3.anchor: عن السدي قوله : ان الله لا يحب الفرحين قال : ان الله لا يحب الفرح بطرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r1.claim: Quraysh’s wealthy leaders resisted Muhammad and disparaged poor followers, claiming revelation should come to a wealthy notable; the Qur’an repeatedly rebukes this status-by-wealth assumption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r1.anchor: من دواعي تصلبهم في إعراضهم عن دعوته اعتزازهم بأموالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi reports from Ibn Masʿud and others that Quraysh leaders demanded Muhammad dismiss Khabbab, Bilal, ʿAmmar, and Suhayb so they might follow him; revelation answered that he must not drive away those who call on God. No grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r2.anchor: روى الواحدي عن ابن مسعود وغيره بأسانيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r3.claim: The Qarun example follows the reminder that worldly possessions are only the adornment of this life and their owners will be brought before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r3.anchor: فيما تقدم من الآيات قريبا قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r4.claim: Qarun’s wealth and arrogance exemplify Meccan figures: Abu Lahab and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith in kinship and abuse, al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil in abusing Khabbab, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira in boasting of wealth and dependents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r4.anchor: وأن مثل قارون صالح لأن يكون مثلا لأبي لهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r5.claim: The story opens as an example for Meccan leaders such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Jahl, and attaches to the preceding account of worldly goods and resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p174/r5.anchor: لذكر قصة ضربت مثلا لحال بعض كفار مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r1.claim: The Qarun story also connects with the close of the Pharaoh-soldiers narrative, which ends with the reminder that Muhammad was not at the Mount when God called.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r1.anchor: ولهذه القصة اتصال بانتهاء قصة جند فرعون المنتهية عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r2.claim: Qarun is an Arabized form of Hebrew Qorah, altered for easier pronunciation and molded on Arabic names such as Talut and Jalut; its letters are not derived from q-r-n.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r3.claim: Qorah was Moses’ cousin: the source gives their Levi-family genealogies and identifies Izhar as Amram’s brother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r3.anchor: فهو قورح بن يصهار بن قهات بن لاوى بن يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r4.speaker: سفر العدد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r4.claim: Numbers 16 says Korah joined 250 Israelite leaders against Moses and Aaron over the Aaronide priesthood, was swallowed by the earth with his followers, and lost his wealth near Jericho; exegetes also say Pharaoh made him Israel’s chief in Egypt and he amassed riches.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r4.anchor: في الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r5.claim: The Qur’anic account explains Qarun’s envy: Moses’ mission and departure with Israel removed Qarun from power over his people, so he resented Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r5.anchor: لأن موسى لما جاء بالرسالة وخرج ببني إسرائيل زال تأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r6.claim: Storytellers’ elaborate accounts of Qarun’s luxury and magnificence lack Qur’anic or other proof; exegetes repeated them except Ibn ʿAtiyya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r6.anchor: وقد أكثر القصاص من وصف بذخة قارون وعظمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r7.claim: The opening إن may emphasize the central lesson about the disastrous end of people deceived by wealth, who fail to thank God, disdain religion, and reject His laws; Qarun’s ancestry itself was not in doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p175/r7.anchor: فمصب التأكيد هو ما بعد قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r1.claim: Alternatively, إن draws attention to the whole lesson: Qarun’s belonging to Moses’ people and becoming his enemy is especially striking, even more than Pharaoh’s case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r1.anchor: لمجرد الاهتمام بالخبر ومناط الاهتمام هو مجموع ما تضمنته القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r2.claim: Saying Moses’ people rather than Israelites hints at Qarun’s special kinship connection to Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r2.anchor: من الإيماء إلى أن لقارون اتصالا خاصا بموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r3.claim: The clause is parenthetical between Qarun’s identity and the grant of treasure; fa marks immediate sequence, highlighting how quickly he grew insolent toward his kin after receiving favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r3.anchor: وجملة { فبغى عليهم } معترضة بين جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r4.claim: Baghy is aggression; aggression against a community means slighting its rights, beginning with violation of its law. Oppressing one’s kin is especially painful, as Tarafa’s verse says.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r5.claim: The wording about Qarun’s people prepares an analogy with the harm Muhammad suffered from his own idolatrous relatives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r5.anchor: تمهيد للكناية بهذا الخبر عن إرادة التنظير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r6.claim: The sentence happens to scan as a hemistich in al-Khafif meter; Qur’anic rhetorical circumstances can call for wording whose rhythm coincides with a poetic meter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r6.anchor: فإن هذه الجملة جاءت على ميزان مصراع من بحر الخفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r7.claim: Basran grammarians allow إن to begin the relative clause of ما; Kufans disallow it and instead parse ما as an indefinite noun described by the following clause, citing lack of Arabic usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r7.anchor: عند نحاة البصرة الذين لا يمنعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r8.claim: Mafātiḥ is the plural of maftaḥ, the instrument for opening, also called miftāḥ; another plural is mafātīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p176/r8.anchor: وهو آلة الفتح ، ويسمى المفتاح أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r1.claim: Treasures are stored money kept in a box or vault; a store could hold a standard sum, with a key for each container.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r1.anchor: جمع كنز وهو مختزن المال من صندوق أو خزانة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r2.speaker: أبو رزين لقيط بن عامر العقيلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r2.claim: The Companion Abu Razin said that one key would suffice for Kufa, meaning one treasure could have a single key; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r2.anchor: وعن أبي رزين لقيط بن عامر العقيلي أحد الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r3.claim: Many keys imply many vaults and thus great wealth, a two-step metonymy; he also cites a line about a timid dog and thin calf as indirect expression.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r4.claim: Tanūʾ means to weigh heavily; the keys are so heavy that they burden even the strong group carrying them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r4.anchor: باء الملابسة أن تثقل مع العصبة الذين يحملونها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r5.claim: The ba is associative, not causal as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s line; the author also rejects al-Zamakhshari’s example in which a load burdens its bearer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r5.anchor: وليست هذه الباء باء السببية كالتي في قول امرىء القيس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r6.claim: The author rejects Abu ʿUbayda’s claim that the verse uses reversed syntax.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r6.anchor: فلا يقبله من كان له قلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r7.claim: ʿUṣba means a group; Mujahid’s nearest estimate is ten to fifteen people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r7.anchor: وأقرب الأقوال في مقدارها قول مجاهد أنه من عشرة إلى خمسة عشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r8.claim: Qarun accumulated his wealth in Egypt and went out with it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177/r8.anchor: وكان اكتسب الأموال في مصر وخرج بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r1.claim: إذ is syntactically governed by بغى عليهم, but it marks the narrative setting rather than the time of the transgression; some exegetes attach it to an implicit أذكر.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r1.anchor: ظرف منصوب بفعل ( بغى عليهم ) والمقصود من هذا الظرف القصة وليس القصد به توقيت البغي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r2.claim: قومه can mean a group of Qarun’s people, namely those who admonished him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالقوم بعضهم إما جماعة منهم وهم أهل الموعظة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it can refer to Moses, called the people because his words set an example for them, as though they had spoken them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r3.anchor: وإما موسى عليه السلام أطلق عليه اسم القوم لأن أقواله قدوة للقوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r4.claim: Farah can mean joy, as in Yunus 10:22, or excessive elation, arrogance, and conceit, as in the usage at 13:26.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r4.anchor: والفرح يطلق على السرور كما في قوله تعالى { وفرحوا بها } في يونس ( 22 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r5.claim: The prohibited joy is excessive attachment to worldly pleasures that turns one from good works, competition in virtue, spiritual perfection, and religious manners; 28:77 makes this contextual sense explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r5.anchor: والفرح المنهي عنه هو المفرط منه ، أي الذي تمحض للتعلق بمتاع الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r6.claim: Unqualified joy suggests a settled disposition of conceit and arrogance; the intensive form and causal clause condemn extreme absorption in pleasure, which entails neglect of serious duties.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r6.anchor: وأحسب أن الفرح إذا لم يعلق به شيء دل على أنه صار سجية الموصوف فصار مرادا به العجب والبطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r7.claim: The intensive form in لا يحب الفرحين means those excessive in joy; its causal force makes the prohibition a warning against turning from serious obligations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r7.anchor: وقد أشير إلى بيان المقصود تعضيدا لدلالة المقام بقوله { إن الله لا يحب الفرحين } ، أي المفرطين في الفرح فإن صيغة ( فعل ) صيغة مبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r1.claim: Qārūn is a foreign name and therefore diptote.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r1.anchor: قارون اسم أعجمي فلذلك لم ينصرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Qārūn was Moses’ paternal uncle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r2.anchor: فقال ابن إسحاق هو عمه، وقال ابن جريج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r3.speaker: ابن جريج وإبراهيم النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī say he was Moses’ paternal cousin, the more famous view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وإبراهيم النخعي هو ابن عمه لحا، وهذا أشهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r4.claim: Another view makes Qārūn the son of Moses’ maternal aunt.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r5.claim: All agree Qārūn was an Israelite believer who excelled in Torah; pride later led him to transgress and disdain Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r5.anchor: وهو بإجماع رجل من بني إسرائيل كان ممن آمن بموسى وحفظ التوراة وكان من أقرأ الناس لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Qārūn hired a beautiful courtesan to accuse Moses publicly; she repented, exposed him, and God cleared Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r6.anchor: فيما قال ابن عباس بأنه عمد إلى امرأة مومسة ذات جمال وقال لها أنا أحسن إليك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r7.claim: Another account says the woman first accused Moses, then confessed Qārūn had prompted her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r7.anchor: وقيل بل قالت المرأة ذلك عن موسى فلما بلغه الخبر وقف المرأة بمحضر ملإ من بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r8.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab says Qārūn lengthened his clothes by a handspan beyond others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r8.anchor: وكان من بغيه أنه زاد في ثيابه شبرا على ثياب الناس، قاله شهر بن حوشب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r9.claim: Qārūn’s wealth was called treasures because he withheld zakāt, beginning his hostility toward Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r9.anchor: وكان من أعظم الناس مالا وسميت أمواله «كنوزا» إذ كان ممتنعا من أداء الزكاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r10.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r10.claim: The apparent meaning is keys; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says mafātiḥ can mean storehouses or large vessels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p297#3/r10.anchor: قاله الضحاك لأن المفتح في كلام العرب الخزانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r1.speaker: خيثمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r1.claim: Khaythama says the Gospel describes Qārūn’s keys as camel-hide, half a handspan long, each weighing a camel or mule load.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r1.anchor: فروي عن خيثمة أنه قال: نجد في الإنجيل مكتوبا أن مفاتيح قارون كانت من جلود الإبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r2.claim: The author rejects similar reports as weak and implausible: identifying keys is unclear and their number could be counted easily.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r2.anchor: وروي غير هذا مما يقرب منه ذلك كله ضعيف والنظر يشهد بفساد هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r3.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r3.anchor: وكان يلزم على هذا المعنى أن تكون «مفاتيح» بياء وهي قراءة الأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r4.claim: The keys were likely iron and numerous due to scattered treasuries; alternatively mafātiḥ means the treasuries.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r4.anchor: والذي يشبه إنما هو أن تكون «المفاتيح» من الحديد ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the treasuries were carried on forty mules.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r5.anchor: قال أبو صالح كانت خزائنه تحمل على أربعين بغلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r6.claim: Tanūʾu means to rise or strain under weight; a poem uses it of weak ewes weighed down by feathers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r6.anchor: وأما قوله «تنوء» فمعناه تنهض بتحامل واشتداد ومن ذلك قول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r7.claim: Another poem uses nāʾa of a shoulder inclining under strain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r8.claim: The better construction is that the band is weighed down by the keys, an Arabic reversal used by many interpreters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r8.anchor: والوجه أن يقال إن العصبة تنوء بالمفاتح المثقلة لها وكذلك قال كثير من المتأولين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r9.claim: A poem about giving one’s life and wealth exemplifies the reversal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r10.claim: Khudāsh ibn Zuhayr’s verse is not evidence because it reads straightforwardly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r10.anchor: وهذا البيت لا حجة فيه إذ يتجه على وجهه فتأمله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r11.claim: A war poem is cited as another example of syntactic reversal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r11.anchor: ومن ذلك قول الآخر: فما كنت في الحرب العوان مغمزا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r12.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r12.claim: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl reconstruct “the band would be weighed down,” using a preposition to make the verb transitive; Arabs say a load burdens a camel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r12.anchor: وقال سيبويه والخليل التقدير «لتنيء العصبة» فجعل بدل ذلك تعدية الفعل بحرف الجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r13.claim: The verb may be metaphorically predicated of the keys, which rise with strain when carried.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يسند «تنوء» إلى المفاتح مجازا لأنها تنهض بتحامل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the band numbered three.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r14.anchor: واختلف الناس في «العصبة» كم هي فقال ابن عباس ثلاثة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r15.claim: Qatāda gives ten to forty people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r15.anchor: وقال قتادة من العشرة إلى الأربعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r16.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r16.claim: Mujāhid says fifteen porters; other views give eleven, like Joseph’s brothers, or forty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r16.anchor: وقال مجاهد خمسة عشر حملا، وقيل أحد عشر حملا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
