IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r17.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r17.claim: Budayl reads linūʾu with yāʾ; Abū al-Fatḥ explains the plural subject, while al-Dānī reports singular miftāḥuhu, making that explanation unnecessary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r17.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة «لينوء» بالياء ووجهها أبو الفتح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r18.claim: “When his people said to him” attaches to “he transgressed.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r18.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إذ قال له قومه، متعلق بقوله فبغى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r19.claim: His people warn against transgressive delight: indulgence, self-abandonment, arrogance, and conceit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r19.anchor: ونهوه عن الفرح المطغي الذي هو انهماك وانحلال نفس وأشر وإعجاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r20.claim: “God does not love” here does not describe an act tied to will; it means He does not manifest blessing or mercy toward them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r20.anchor: ولا يجب في هذا الموضع صفة فعل لأنه أمر قد وقع فمحال أن يرجع إلى الإرادة وإنما هو لا يظهر عليهم بركته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r1.claim: Qarun was from Moses' own clan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس وعبد الله بن الحارث وإبراهيم وابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r2.claim: One view makes Qarun Moses' cousin; it is reported by Said ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas and also held by Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, Ibrahim, and Ibn Jurayj.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه كان ابن عمه رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس وبه قال عبد الله بن الحارث وإبراهيم وابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r3.claim: A second view makes him the son of Moses' maternal aunt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r3.anchor: والثاني ابن خالته رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Qarun was Moses' paternal uncle.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r4.anchor: والثالث انه كان عم موسى قاله ابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qarun is a foreign indeclinable name; if Arabic فاعول from قرنت, it would decline.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج قارون اسم أعجمي لا ينصرف ولو كان فاعولا من العربية من قرنت الشئ لا نصرف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun paid a woman to accuse Moses; when Moses made her swear, she disclosed the plot.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r6.anchor: أحدها أنه جعل لبغي جعلا على أن تقذف موسى بنفسها ففعلت فاستحلفها موسى على ما قالت فأخبرته بقصتها فكان هذا بغيه قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says Qarun transgressed by disbelief in God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه بغى بالكفر بالله تعالى قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r8.claim: Qatada says his transgression was arrogance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r9.speaker: عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r9.claim: Ata al-Khurasani and Shahr ibn Hawshab say he lengthened his clothes by a span.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r9.anchor: والرابع أنه زاد في طول ثيابه شبرا قاله عطاء الخراساني وشهر بن حوشب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r10.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits that Qarun served Pharaoh and oppressed the Israelites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r10.anchor: والخامس أنه كان يخدم فرعون فتعدى على بني إسرائيل وظلمهم حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r11.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r11.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the مفاتح were keys opening the treasury doors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r11.anchor: أحدهما أنها مفاتيح الخزائن التي تفتح بها الأبواب قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r12.speaker: الأعمش عن خيثمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r12.claim: Al-A'mash reports from Khaythama that Qarun's leather keys, each finger-sized, loaded sixty mules.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r12.anchor: وروي الأعمش عن خيثمة قال كانت مفاتيح قارون وقر ستين بغلا وكانت من جلود كل مفتاح مثل الإصبع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r13.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r13.claim: Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, and al-Dahhak say مفاتح means the treasuries themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r13.anchor: والثاني أنها خزائنه قاله السدي وأبو صالح والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r14.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers ‘treasuries of wealth’; Ibn Qutayba agrees.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r14.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا الأشبه أن تكون مفاتحه خزائن ماله وإلى نحو هذا ذهب ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r15.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r15.claim: Abu Salih says Qarun's treasuries were carried on forty mules.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p239/r15.anchor: قال أبو صالح كانت خزائنه تحمل على أربعين بغلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r1.claim: The keys weighed down the group and made them lean.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r2.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r2.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn Qutayba, al-Zajjaj and others take the keys as subject: they burden the group; the prefixed ba changes the construction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r2.anchor: ومعنى الكلام لتنئ العصبة فلما دخلت الباء في العصبة انفتحت التاء كما تقول هذا يذهب بالأبصار وهذا يذهب الأبصار وهذا اختيار الفراء وابن قتيبة والزجاج في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash call it inversion: the group bears the keys' weight, like the cited example of an old woman weighed down by her hips.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم هذا من المقلوب وتقديره ما إن العصبة لتنوء بمفاتحه كما يقال إنها لتنوء بها عجيزتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r4.claim: The poem فديت بنفسه witnesses the inversion, meaning ‘I ransomed him with my self and wealth.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r4.anchor: وأنشدوا فديت بنفسه نفسي ومالي وما آلوك إلا ما أطيق أي فديت بنفسي وبمالي نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says he explained عصبة earlier in Surat Yusuf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r5.anchor: وقد بينا معنى العصبة في سورة يوسف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r6.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r6.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that عصبة means forty men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r6.anchor: أحدها أربعون رجلا رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r7.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that it means three to ten people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r7.anchor: والثاني ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r8.claim: Mujahid says it means fifteen people.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r9.claim: Qatada says it means more than ten up to forty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r9.anchor: والرابع فوق العشرة إلى الأربعين قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r10.claim: Abu Salih says it means seventy men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r10.anchor: والخامس سبعون رجلا قاله أبو صالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives the range as fifteen to forty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r11.anchor: والسادس ما بين الخمسة عشر إلى الأربعين حكاه الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r12.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says believers from Qarun's people addressed him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r12.anchor: أحدهما أنهم المؤمنون من قومه قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r13.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r13.anchor: والثاني أنه قول موسى له حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r14.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r14.claim: Ibn Qutayba says do not exult arrogantly or be insolent; the cited poem uses فرح for arrogance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r14.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المعنى لا تأشر ولا تبطر قال الشاعر ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r15.claim: Arrogance is blameworthy, but simple happiness is not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r15.anchor: أي لست بأشر فأما السرور فليس بمكروه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r16.speaker: أبو رجاء وأبو حيوة وعاصم الجحدري وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r16.claim: These readers read الفارحين with an alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p240/r16.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء وأبو حيوة وعاصم الجحدري وابن أبي عبلة الفارحين بألف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، إبراهيم النخعي، عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل، سماك بن حرب، قتادة، مالك بن دينار، ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the listed authorities say Qarun was Moses's cousin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: {إن قارون كان من قوم موسى} ، قال: كان ابن عمه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies Qarun as Qarun son of Yashhar son of Qahith, and Moses as Moses son of Imran son of Qahith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: هو قارون بن يصهر بن قاهث، وموسى بن عمران بن قاهث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Qarun was Moses's uncle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r3.anchor: وزعم محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: أن قارون كان عم موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir says most scholars held that Qarun was Moses's cousin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r4.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وأكثر أهل العلم على أنه كان ابن عمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r5.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r5.claim: Qatada says Qarun was called al-Munawwar for his beautiful Torah recitation, then became a hypocrite like al-Samiri and was destroyed by arrogance over his wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة بن دعامة: كنا نحدث أنه كان ابن عم موسى، وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صوته بالتوراة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r6.claim: Shahr says Qarun lengthened his clothes by a span to elevate himself above his people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253/r6.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: زاد في ثيابه شبرا طولا ترفعا على قومه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r1.claim: The treasures were so abundant that their keys would weigh heavily on a group of strong people carrying them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r1.anchor: أي: ليثقل حملها الفئام من الناس لكثرتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r2.speaker: الأعمش عن خيثمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r2.claim: Khaythama says the keys were leather, each finger-sized and assigned to a separate storehouse; sixty marked gray mules carried them when Qarun rode.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r2.anchor: قال الأعمش، عن خيثمة: كانت مفاتيح كنوز قارون من جلود، كل مفتاح مثل الأصبع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r3.claim: Qarun's people advised him not to become arrogant and overbearing because of his wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r3.anchor: فقالوا على سبيل النصح والإرشاد: لا تفرح بما أنت فيه، يعنون: لا تبطر بما أنت فيه من الأموال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the joy condemned here as being frivolous and boastful.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the condemned joy as insolent arrogance and ingratitude for God's gifts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني الأشرين البطرين، الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r3.claim: Baghy is seeking superiority without right; its root is seeking, which is why unjust rulers are called transgressors.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r3.anchor: البغي: طلب العلو بغير حق، وأصله من الطلب؛ ولذلك يقال لولاة الجور: بغاة.

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r4.claim: Kanz originally means gathering; in custom it is wealth hidden underground, and in law it is wealth whose zakat has not been paid.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r4.anchor: الكنز: معروف، وأصله: الجمع، ويقال لكل مجتمع من لحم أو غيره: مكتنز

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r5.claim: The legal meaning of kanz as wealth not tithed is established by the law.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r5.anchor: وفي الشرع: اسم لمال لم تؤد زكاته، جاء الشرع بذلك.

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r6.claim: A miftāḥ opens locks; its plurals include mafātīḥ and mafātiḥ.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r6.anchor: والمفتاح: ما يفتح به الأغلاق، يقال: مفتاح ومفاتيح ومفاتح.

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r7.claim: Nawʾ first means rising under a heavy load; it also names the stars’ rising and setting.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r7.anchor: النوء: نهوض الإنسان بالحمل إذا نهض به مع ثقله ينوء نوءا

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r8.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi describes 28 known stars, one setting in the west at dawn every thirteen nights as its opposite rises, completing a yearly cycle.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r8.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: الأنواء ثمانية وعشرون نجما معروفة يسقط في كل ثلاث عشرة ليلة نجم في المغرب

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says people speak of a nawʾ only when rain accompanies the star’s setting and rising.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: لا يكون نوء حتى يكون معه مطر

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r10.claim: Attributing rain to a star is unbelief; saying God sent it when a star rose is neither error nor unbelief.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r10.anchor: لأنهم أضافوا المطر إلى النجم فكفروا، ولو قالوا: أمطرنا الله عند طلوع نجم كذا لم يكن خطأ

JISHUMI:v8p5527/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r11.speaker: رسول الله
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r11.claim: The Prophet strongly condemned attributing rain to stars as a pre-Islamic practice.
JISHUMI:v8p5527/r11.anchor: وقد شدد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في ذلك وذكر أنه من أمور الجاهلية

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r1.claim: ʿUṣba is a group without a singular of the same form; ʿuṣāba is similar, and some say ten to forty or derive it from binding.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r1.anchor: والعصبة: الجماعة لا واحد له من لفظه، وكذلك العصابة، وقيل: هو من العشرة إلى الأربعين

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r10.claim: The story is linked to Moses’ promised history at the start of the surah.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r10.anchor: قيل: هو من نبأ موسى الذي وعد تلاوته في أول السورة، قصة قارون معه.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r11.claim: Qarun’s story confirms the preceding teaching that worldly possessions are fleeting and what is with God is better and more lasting.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r11.anchor: وقيل: لما قال: (فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى) أكد ذلك بحديث قارون.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r13.claim: One account makes Qarun an Israelite by lineage; another says he descended from Levi son of Jacob.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r13.anchor: قيل: كان من بني إسرائيل نسبا، وقيل: كان من ولد لاوي بن يعقوب

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies Qarun as Moses’ cousin.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r14.anchor: وقيل: كان ابن عم موسى، عن ابن جريج.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r15.speaker: ابن إسحاق
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r15.claim: Ibn Isḥaq says Qarun was Moses’ maternal and paternal nephew.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r15.anchor: وقيل: كان ابن أخيه لأمه وأبيه، عن ابن إسحاق.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r16.claim: Another view says Qarun belonged to Moses’ people and had believed in him and accepted his religion.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r16.anchor: وقيل: كان من قومه ممن آمن به وقبل دينه.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r17.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r17.claim: Qatada says Qarun was called al-Munawwar because of his handsome appearance.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r17.anchor: وقيل: كان يقال له: المنور؛ لحسن صورته، عن قتادة.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r18.claim: A further account says Qarun was Israel’s best Torah reader, handsomest, and richest, then became a hypocrite like the Samaritan.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r18.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن في بني إسرائيل أقرأ للتوراة منه ولا أجمل ولا أغنى، ثم نافق كما نافق السامري

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r19.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r19.claim: Abu ʿAli says Qarun scorned and acted arrogantly toward his people; Jishumi calls this the best explanation.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r19.anchor: فقيل: كان بغيه أنه يستخف بهم، ويتكبر، عليهم، عن أبي علي، وهو أحسن ما قيل فيه.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r20.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r20.claim: Qatada says Qarun flaunted his many treasures, which Jishumi equates with Abu ʿAli’s explanation.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r20.anchor: وقيل: استطال عليهم بكثرة كنوزه، عن قتادة، وهذا مثل قول أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r21.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r21.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says Qarun was Pharaoh’s official over Israel and oppressed them.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r21.anchor: وقيل: كان عاملا لفرعون على بني إسرائيل، فكان يبغي عليهم، ويظلمهم، عن سعيد بن المسيب.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r22.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Qarun was king over Israel while they were in Egypt.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r22.anchor: وقيل: كان ملكا عليهم لما كانوا بمصر، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r23.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r23.claim: One story says Qarun paid a notorious prostitute to accuse Moses of soliciting her; God restrained her tongue and she exonerated him.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r23.anchor: وقيل: قصد إلى امرأة بغية مشهورة بذلك، وضمن مالا على أن تقصد موسى في مجلسه

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r24.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r24.claim: Another version says she repented and publicly confessed Qarun paid her to accuse Moses, who was innocent.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r24.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل تابت وجاءت وقارون وبنو إسرائيل حول موسى فقالت: إن قارون ضمن لي مالا

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r25.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r25.claim: Other views identify Qarun’s transgression as unbelief and hypocrisy, or pursuing entertainment and corruption.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r25.anchor: وقيل: بغيه: كفره ونفاقه. وقيل: بغيه أنه كان يشتغل باللهو والفساد.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r26.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r26.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani says Qarun lengthened his garments by a handspan.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r26.anchor: وقيل: زاد عليهم في الثياب شبرا، عن عطاء الخراساني.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r27.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r27.claim: Another account says Qarun refused Moses’ zakat assessment after the amount became enormous.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r27.anchor: وقيل: طالبه موسى بالزكاة وبلغ مبلغا عظيما، فمنعه وتعدى، فذلك بغيه.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r28.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r28.claim: One view says Moses removed Qarun from overseeing offerings and gave the role to his brother, provoking Qarun’s rebellion.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r28.anchor: وقيل: كان موسى جعل إليه القربان، فعزله وجعل ذلك إلى أخيه فغضب وبغى.

JISHUMI:v8p5528/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r29.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r29.claim: God gave Qarun stored wealth so vast that its door keys weighed on a strong band of people.
JISHUMI:v8p5528/r29.anchor: وآتيناه من الكنوز أعطيناه من الأموال المدخرة ما إن مفاتحه جمع مفتح، وهو المفتاح الذي تفتح به الأبواب.

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r12.claim: Qarun’s kinship with Moses’ people did not benefit him without faith.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r12.anchor: الآية تدل على أن قارون كان من قوم موسى، وأن القرابة لا تنفع من غير إيمان.

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r13.claim: Baghy is a blameworthy legal term for rebelling against the imam; law specializes the root sense of seeking what is not rightfully sought.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r13.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فبغى عليهم) أن البغي اسم ذم في الشرع؛ ولذلك يقال للخارج على الإمام: باغ

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r14.claim: The verse indicates that Qarun had great wealth.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r14.anchor: وتدل أن قارون كان أوتي مالا كثيرا

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r15.claim: Jishumi infers that Qarun’s wealth was lawful because God says He gave it to him.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r15.anchor: وتدل أنه كان حلالا أضافه إلى نفسه فقال: (وآتيناه من الكنوز).

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r16.claim: Vast lawful wealth could come from pre-Islamic treasures, inheritance, trade or farming by a large household, earnings, or spoils; Pharaoh’s appointment of Qarun over Israel may have enabled business, and sources could combine.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r16.anchor: قلنا: لذلك وجوه: منها: أن يظفر بكنوز من أهل الجاهلية. ومنها: أن يرث. ومنها: أن يكون له حشمه

JISHUMI:v8p5533/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r17.claim: Worldly rejoicing through vanity and arrogance is blameworthy; one should rejoice in what leads to Paradise.
JISHUMI:v8p5533/r17.anchor: وتدل على أن الفرح بالدنيا على سبيل البطر والتكبر قبيح، وأن الواجب الفرح بما يؤديه إلى الجنة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r1.claim: Qārūn is a foreign name like Hārūn, indeclinable because it is foreign and a proper name; as a native faʿūl from q-r-n, it would decline.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r1.anchor: قارون } اسم أعجمي مثل هرون ، ولم ينصرف للعجمة والتعريف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r2.claim: One explanation takes Qārūn’s being from Moses’ people to mean that he believed in Moses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r2.anchor: وقيل : معنى كونه من قومه أنه آمن به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r3.claim: Another account makes Qārūn an Israelite, son of Moses’ paternal uncle, and gives his ancestry through Levi; another says Moses was his nephew.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r3.anchor: وقيل : كان إسرائيليا ابن عم موسى : هو قارون بن يصهر بن قاهث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r4.claim: Qārūn was called al-Munawwar for his beauty and was said to be Israel’s best reader of the Torah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r4.anchor: وقيل : كان موسى ابن أخيه ، وكان يسمى المنور لحسن صورته ، وكان أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r5.claim: He became a hypocrite like al-Sāmirī and resented that Moses had prophethood and Aaron the altar and offering; he complained that he had no role.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r5.anchor: ولكنه نافق كما نافق السامري وقال : إذا كانت النبوة لموسى عليه السلام ، والمذبح والقربان إلى هرون فمالي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r6.claim: A report says that after the sea crossing, Moses assigned Aaron the religious leadership and priestly offering, which made Qārūn resent and envy them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r6.anchor: وروي : أنه لما جاوز بهم موسى البحر وصارت الرسالة والحبورة لهرون يقرب القربان ويكون رأسا فيهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r7.claim: Qārūn challenged Moses to show a sign, and Moses said the arrangement was God’s doing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r7.anchor: وجد قارون في نفسه وحسدهما ، فقال لموسى : الأمر لكما ولست على شيء ، إلى متى أصبر ؟ قال موسى : هذا صنع الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r8.claim: In the reported sign, Israelite leaders placed their guarded staffs in the revelation tent; Aaron’s almond staff alone sprouted green leaves, but Qārūn called it magic.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r8.anchor: فأمر رؤساء بني إسرائيل أن يجيء كل واحد بعصاه ، فحزمها وألقاها في القبة التي كان الوحي ينزل عليه فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r9.claim: Baghy means injustice; one report says Pharaoh appointed Qārūn over Israel and he oppressed them, while other reports call it pride and ostentation over wealth and children, or lengthening clothes by a span.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r9.anchor: فبغى عليهم } من البغي وهو الظلم . قيل : ملكه فرعون على بني إسرائيل فظلمهم . وقيل : من البغي وهو الكبر والبذخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r10.claim: Mafātiḥ can be the plural of maftaḥ, with kasra, meaning keys; it is also explained as treasuries, whose singular is maftaḥ with fatḥa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r10.anchor: المفاتح : جمع مفتح بالكسر : وهو ما يفتح به . وقيل هي الخزائن ، وقياس واحدها : مفتح بالفتح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r11.claim: The idiom nāʾa bihi al-ḥiml means a load weighed someone down until it made him lean; ʿuṣba and ʿiṣāba mean a large group and iʿṣawṣabū means gathered together.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r11.anchor: ويقال : ناء به الحمل ، إذا أثقله حتى أماله . والعصبة : الجماعة الكثيرة والعصابة : مثلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r12.claim: A report says sixty mules carried the treasury keys, one per treasury, each no larger than a finger and made of leather.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r12.anchor: وقيل : كانت تحمل مفاتيح خزائنه ستون بغلا ، لكل خزانة مفتاح ، ولا يزيد المفتاح على إصبع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r13.speaker: أبو رزين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r13.claim: Abū Razīn says one key would suffice for Kufa, underscoring the extraordinary scale of the keys.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r13.anchor: قال أبو رزين : يكفي الكوفة مفتاح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r14.claim: The description amplifies the burden through treasures, keys, weighing down, a large band, and strong people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r14.anchor: وقد بولغ في ذكر ذلك بلفظ : الكنوز ، والمفاتح ، والنوء ، والعصبة ، وأولى القوة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r15.speaker: دليل بن ميسرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r15.claim: Dalīl ibn Muyassara reads the verb with yāʾ, construing mafātiḥ as treasuries and giving it agreement with what it is attached to.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r15.anchor: وقرأ بدليل بن ميسرة : لينوء بالياء . ووجهه أن يفسر المفاتح بالخزائن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r16.claim: The adverb إذ is in the accusative as a complement of تنوء.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r16.anchor: ومحل إذ منصوب بتنوء { لا تفرح } كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r17.claim: The prohibition echoes the warning not to exult in what God has given, cited from 57:23.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p434/r17.anchor: لا تفرح } كقوله : { ولا تفرحوا بما ءاتاكم } ( الحديد : 23 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r1.claim: The poem’s مفراح describes rejoicing when fortune delights someone; only one settled in worldly life rejoices, while the afterlife-minded know they will soon leave it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r1.anchor: ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني … وذلك أنه لا يفرح بالدنيا إلا من رضي بها واطمأن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r2.claim: A second anonymous couplet captures the grief hidden in joy when its owner knows that separation is near.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r2.anchor: ما أحسن ما قال القائل : أشد الغم عندي في سرور … تيقن عنه صاحبه انتقالا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun was Moses's cousin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان ابن عمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r2.claim: Qatada specifies that Qarun was the son of Moses's paternal uncle and crossed the sea with the Israelites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r2.anchor: قاله قتادة : ابن عم موسى أخي أبيه وكان قطع البحر مع بني إسرائيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r3.claim: Qatada says Qarun was called al-Munawwar for his beautiful voice reciting the Torah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r3.anchor: وكان يسمى : المنور , من حسن صوته بالتوراة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r4.claim: Mawardi calls Qarun an enemy of God who feigned faith like al-Samiri.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r4.anchor: ولكن عدو الله نافق كما نافق السامري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says Qarun's transgression was disbelief in God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r5.anchor: أحدها : بغيه عليهم أنه كفر بالله , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r6.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says Qarun's transgression was lengthening his garment by a span.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه زاد في طول ثيابه شبرا , قاله شهر بن حوشب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r7.claim: Qatada says Qarun's transgression was his superiority over them through abundant wealth and children.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r7.anchor: الثالث : أنه علا عليهم بكثرة ماله وولده , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that, after Moses ordered an adulterer stoned, Qarun paid a prostitute to falsely accuse Moses of adultery; she then confessed Qarun's scheme and affirmed Moses's innocence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r8.anchor: حين أمر الله موسى برجم الزاني فعمد قارون إلى امرأة بغي فأعطاها مالا وحملها على أن ادعت عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r9.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r9.claim: Al-Suddi names the prostitute Shajarta and says Qarun promised her two thousand dirhams.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r9.anchor: قال السدي : وكان اسم البغي شجرتا وبذلك لها قارون ألفي درهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says Qarun had been Pharaoh's slave, then exceeded bounds by oppressing the Israelites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r10.anchor: الخامس : أنه كان غلاما لفرعون فتعدى على بني إسرائيل وظلمهم , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r11.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r11.claim: Ibn Bahr says Qarun's transgression was attributing God's treasure to his own knowledge and contrivance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r11.anchor: السادس : أنه نسب ما آتاه الله من الكنوز إلى نفسه بعلمه وحيلته , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r12.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r12.claim: Ata says Qarun found one of Joseph's treasures.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أصاب كنزا من كنوز يوسف عليه السلام , قاله عطاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r13.speaker: الوليد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r13.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان يعمل الكيمياء ، قاله الوليد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r14.speaker: السدي وأبو رزين
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r14.claim: Al-Suddi and Abu Razin gloss the keys as Qarun's storehouses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r14.anchor: أحدها : خزائنه , قاله السدي وأبو رزين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r15.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the keys as Qarun's containers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r16.claim: Another view takes them as the keys to his storehouses, made of hides and carried by forty mules.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r16.anchor: الثالث : مفاتيح خزائنه وكانت من جلود يحملها أربعون بغلا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r17.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r17.claim: Ibn Bahr takes the keys as Qarun's comprehensive knowledge of the treasures, citing God's possession of the keys of the unseen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r17.anchor: الرابع : أن مفاتيح الكنوز إحاطة علمه بها , حكاه ابن بحر لقول الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r18.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو صالح والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi say the keys weighed heavily on the group.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r18.anchor: أحدها : لتثقل العصبة , قاله ابن عباس وأبو صالح والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r19.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r19.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas reads the phrase as making the group lean or move away, deriving it from al-nay, distance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p264/r19.anchor: الثاني : لتميل بالعصبة , قاله الربيع بن أنس مأخوذ من النأي وهو البعد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r1.claim: The cited line uses nayūn to convey distance or separation, supporting the explanation of al-nay as distance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r1.anchor: ينأون عنا وما تنأى مودتهم … والقلب فيهم رهين حيثما كانوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the wording as inverted: the group bears the keys, rather than the keys weighing on the group.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r2.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيدة أن هذا من المقلوب تأويله : إن العصبة لتنوء بالمفاتح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r3.claim: An ʿuṣba is a group whose members support one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r3.anchor: والعصبة الجماعة الذين يتعصب بعضهم لبعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r4.claim: Abu Salih says the group numbered seventy men.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r4.anchor: أحدها : سبعون رجلا , قاله أبو صالح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r5.speaker: الحكم وقتادة والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r5.claim: Al-Hakam, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say the group numbered forty men.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r5.anchor: الثاني : أربعون رجلا , قاله الحكم وقتادة والضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r6.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the group numbered between ten and forty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r6.anchor: الثالث : ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r7.claim: Mujahid says the group numbered between ten and fifteen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r7.anchor: الرابع : ما بين العشرة إلى الخمسة عشر , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r8.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r8.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the group numbered six or seven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r8.anchor: الخامس : ستة أو سبعة . قاله ابن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r9.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says the group numbered from three to nine, the range denoted by nafar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r9.anchor: السادس : ما بين الثلاثة والتسعة وهم النفر , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r10.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say the group numbered ten, citing Joseph's brothers calling themselves an ʿuṣba.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r10.anchor: السابع : عشرة لقول إخوة يوسف ^ { ونحن عصبة } ^ [ يوسف : 8 ] قاله الكلبي ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r11.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r11.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the people of strength as people of might.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says the speakers were the believers among Qarun's people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قول المؤمنين منهم , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r13.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r13.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says Moses was the one who spoke to Qarun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r13.anchor: الثاني : قول موسى , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r14.claim: Mujahid glosses do not rejoice as do not transgress.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r14.anchor: أحدها : لا تبغ إن الله لا يحب الباغين , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r15.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r15.claim: Ibn Bahr glosses do not rejoice as do not be miserly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r15.anchor: الثاني : لا تبخل إن الله لا يحب الباخلين , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r16.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r16.claim: Al-Suddi glosses do not rejoice as do not become insolently exultant.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r16.anchor: الثالث : لا تبطر إن الله لا يحب البطرين , قاله السدي ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r17.claim: The cited poetry depicts not being carried away by joy when fortune pleases.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p266/r17.anchor: وقال الشاعر : ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني … ولا جازع من صرفه المتغلب

MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r1.claim: Mujahid defines a ʿuṣba as a group of ten to fifteen people.
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال العصبة ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر

MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r2.claim: Mujahid specifies fifteen for the people of strength.
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ لتنوء بالعصبة ﴾ قال العصبة ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر ﴿ أولي القوة ﴾ خمسة عشر

MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r3.claim: The exultant are the ostentatious, insolent, boastful people who fail to thank God for what He gave them.
MUJAHID:v2p489#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إن الله لا يحب الفرحين ﴾ يعني المتبذخين الأشرين البطرين الذين لا يشكرون الله

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r1.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and Moses’s cousin; Muqatil gives both their genealogies through Qohath and Levi.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r1.anchor: يعني من بني إسرائيل، وكان ابن عمه، قارون بن أصهر بن قوهث

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r2.claim: Qarun oppressed the Israelites because of his treasure.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r2.anchor: يقول: بغى قارون على بني إسرائيل من أجل كنزه ما له

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r3.claim: The treasures are wealth and their keys are storehouses; a company of ten to forty strong men could not carry the chests.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r3.anchor: والعصبة من عشرة أنفار إلى أربعين، فإذا كانوا أربعين

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r4.claim: Here rejoice means prance, act arrogantly, and boast over wealth; God does not love the boastful and arrogant.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r4.anchor: يقول: لا تمرح ولا تبطر ولا تفخر بما أوتيت من الأموال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r1.claim: Qārūn is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name; if it were a native faʿūl form from qarana, it would decline.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r1.anchor: لا ينصرف للعجمة والتعريف ولو كان فاعولامن قرنت الشيء لانصرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r2.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and Moses' cousin, from the line of Levi; he was called al-Munawwar for his beauty, knew the Torah better than the Israelites, but became a hypocrite like al-Samiri.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r2.anchor: كان اسرائيليا ابن عم لموسى فهو قارون بن يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوى بن يعقوب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r3.claim: Baghā means that Qarun transgressed and oppressed his people.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r4.claim: Reported explanations say Pharaoh appointed Qarun over Israel and he oppressed them; alternatively, his wealth and children made him arrogant, or he wore clothes a handspan longer than theirs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r4.anchor: قيل ملكه فرعون على بني اسرائيل فظلمهم أو من البغي الكبر تكبر عليهم بكثرة ماله وولده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r5.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun in the accusative as the object of ātaynāhu; the following inna clause is its relative clause, explaining the kasra on inna.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r5.anchor: ما بمعنى الذي في موضع نصب بآيتنا وأن واسمها وخبرها صله الذي ولهذا كسرت إن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r6.claim: Mafātiḥ can mean keys or treasuries, depending on the vowel of the singular maftaḥ; the author prefers the sense 'keys'.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r6.anchor: والمفاتح جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به أو مفتح بالفتح وهو الخزانة والأصوب أنها المقاليد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r7.claim: The keys weigh down the large group; the bā makes the verb transitive, as in the idiom for a load weighing someone down until he leans.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r7.anchor: لتثقل العصبة فالباء للتعدية يقال ناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r8.claim: The keys were carried by sixty mules, one key per treasury; each key was no larger than a finger and made of leather.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r8.anchor: وكانت تحمل مفاتيح خزائنه ستون بغلا لكل خزانة مفتاح ولا يزيد المفتاح على اصبع وكانت من جلود

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r9.claim: Ulū al-quwwa means people of strength.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r10.claim: The phrase 'when his people said' is grammatically accusative in relation to tanūʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r11.claim: The speakers were either the believers or Moses.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r11.anchor: أي المؤمنون وقيل القائل موسى عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r12.claim: The warning means not to exult arrogantly over wealth; the author compares it with the prohibition in 57:23.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r12.anchor: لا تبطر بكثرة المال كقوله ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r13.claim: Only someone content and settled in worldly life rejoices in it; a person whose heart looks to the Hereafter knows this world will soon be left behind.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r13.anchor: ولا يفرح بالدنيا إلا من رضي بها واطمأن وأما من قلبه إلى الآخرة ويعلم أنه يتركها عن قريب فلا يفرح بها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p245#6/r14.claim: Al-fariḥīn here means those who are arrogant and boastful about their wealth.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r1.claim: The story shows that Qarun possessed worldly adornment yet was not protected from punishment, like Pharaoh; it warns that the opponents are not richer or more numerous than they were.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r1.anchor: بين أن قارون أوتيها واغتر بها ولم تعصمه من عذاب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r2.speaker: النخعي وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r2.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, and others say Qarun was Moses’ paternal cousin; their genealogies meet at Qahith.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r2.anchor: قال النخعي وقتادة وغيرهما: كان ابن عم موسى لحا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Qarun was Moses’ full paternal and maternal uncle.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r3.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان عم موسى لأب وأم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r4.claim: Another view makes Qarun the son of Moses’ maternal aunt.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r5.claim: Qarun is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r6.claim: Foreign masculine names on the fāʿūl pattern without a suitable definite article are indeclinable when definite but declinable when indefinite.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r6.anchor: وما كان على وزن فاعول أعجميا لا يحسن فيه الألف واللام لم ينصرف في المعرفة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qarun would decline if derived from qarantu al-shayʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: ولو كان قارون من قرنت الشيء لانصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r8.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says Qarun’s transgression was letting his garment trail an extra span.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r8.anchor: بغيه أنه زاد في طول ثوبه شبرا قاله شهر ابن حوشب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r9.claim: A prophetic report warns that God will not look at one who trails his garment out of arrogance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث: " لا ينظر الله إلى من جر إزاره بطرا "

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies Qarun’s transgression as disbelief in God.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r10.anchor: وقيل: بغيه كفره بالله عز وجل قاله الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r11.claim: Qatada says Qarun wronged his people by despising them because of his abundant wealth and children.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r11.anchor: استخفافه بهم بكثرة ماله وولده قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r12.speaker: ابن بحر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r12.claim: Ibn Bahr says Qarun’s transgression was attributing God-given treasures to his own knowledge and ingenuity.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r12.anchor: نسبته ما أتاه لله من الكنوز إلى نفسه بعلمه وحيلته قاله ابن بحر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r13.claim: A reported story says Qarun resented Moses’ leadership and Aaron’s priestly role, demanded a sign, then dismissed Aaron’s staff sprouting leaves as magic.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r13.anchor: فقال لموسى: الأمر لكما وليس لي شيء إلى متى أصبر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r14.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Qarun paid a prostitute to accuse Moses of adultery; she confessed that Qarun had bribed her and Moses was innocent.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77/r14.anchor: قال سابع: روي عن ابن عباس قال: لما أمر الله تعالى برجم الزاني

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r6.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the prostitute was named Sabarta and Qarun paid her two thousand dirhams.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r6.anchor: قال السدي: وكان اسم البغي سبرتا، وبذل لها قارون ألفي درهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r7.claim: Qatada says Qarun crossed the sea with Moses, was called al-Munawwar for his handsome Torah description, but became a hypocrite like al-Samiri.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r7.anchor: قتادة: وكان قطع البحر مع موسى وكان يسمى المنور من حسن صورته في التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r8.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r8.claim: ʿAtaʾ says Qarun obtained many of Joseph’s treasures.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r8.anchor: قال عطاء: أصاب كثيرا من كنوز يوسف عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r9.speaker: الوليد بن مروان
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r9.claim: Al-Walid ibn Marwan says Qarun practiced alchemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r9.anchor: وقال الوليد بن مروان: إنه كان يعمل الكيمياء

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r10.claim: The particle inna and its subject and predicate are within the relative clause of mā; mā is the object of ataynā.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r10.anchor: واسمها وخبرها في صلة { ما } و { ما } مفعولة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r11.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas reports that ʿAli ibn Sulayman rejects the Kufans’ claim that inna and its governed phrase cannot form a relative clause, since the Qur’an has this construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r11.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول ما أقبح ما يقول الكوفيون في الصلات

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r12.claim: Mafātih is the plural of miftah, a key; if the singular is miftāḥ its plural is mafātīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r12.anchor: وهو جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r13.claim: If mafātih means storehouses, its singular is maftaḥ with fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r13.anchor: ومن قال هي الخزائن فواحدها مفتح بالفتح

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r14.claim: The best explanation is that the keys make the group lean under their weight; the wording shifts the preposition so the group appears to strain upward.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r14.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أن المعنى لتنيء العصبة أي تميلهم بثقلها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r15.claim: Nāʾa means to rise while bearing a heavy load.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#2/r15.anchor: يقال: ناء ينوء نوءا إذا نهض بثقل

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayda reverses the construction: the group strains under the keys’ weight.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: قوله { لتنوء بالعصبة } مقلوب، والمعنى لتنوء بها العصبة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r2.claim: Abu Zayd says nāʾtu bi-l-ḥiml means that I rose carrying the load.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r2.anchor: أبو زيد: نؤت بالحمل إذا نهضت

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r3.claim: The poet’s line illustrates nāʾa as rising with difficulty under weight.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r3.anchor: تنوء بأخراها فلأيا قيامها وتمشي الهويني عن قريب فتبهر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r4.claim: Abu Zayd cites a verse about a servant who stops when he bears a load, illustrating the usage nāʾa bi-l-ḥiml.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r4.anchor: إنا وجدنا خلفا بئس الخلف عبدا إذا ما ناء بالحمل وقف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r5.claim: An additional usage, anāʾanī, means “made me heavy”.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r5.anchor: وأناءني إذا أثقلني عن أبي زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r6.claim: Another derivation connects the word to naʾy, distance; the cited poem uses yanʾawna for keeping away.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو مأخوذ من النأي وهو البعد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r7.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r7.claim: Badil ibn Maysara reads linūʾu with yāʾ, construing the singular understood referent as the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة: { لينوء } بالياء أي لينوء الواحد منها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r8.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r8.claim: Ruʾba says his plural pronouns intentionally refer at once to the lines, their colors, and the combined image.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas defines ʿuṣba as three men.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r9.anchor: الأول: ثلاثة رجال قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to define it as three to ten people.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r10.anchor: وعنه أيضا من الثلاثة إلى العشرة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r11.claim: Mujahid gives the range fifteen to twenty for ʿuṣba.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: العصبة هنا ما بين العشرين إلى خمسة عشر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r12.claim: Mujahid is also reported to define it as ten to fifteen.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r12.anchor: وعنه أيضا: ما بين العشرة إلى الخمسة عشر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r13.claim: A further report from Mujahid gives the range five to ten.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r13.anchor: وعنه أيضا: من عشرة إلى خمسة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r14.speaker: أبو صالح والحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r14.claim: Abu Salih, al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba, Qatada, and al-Dahhak define the group as forty men.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r14.anchor: وقال أبو صالح والحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة والضحاك: أربعون رجلا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r15.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r15.claim: Al-Suddi defines ʿuṣba as ten to forty; Qatada is also reported to give this range.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r15.anchor: السدي ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين. وقاله قتادة أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r16.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r16.claim: ʿIkrima says some define the group as forty and others as seventy.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r16.anchor: وقال عكرمة: منهم من يقول أربعون، ومنهم من يقول سبعون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r17.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r17.claim: Al-Mawardi reports Abu Salih’s definition of ʿuṣba as seventy men.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r17.anchor: إن العصبة سبعون رجلا ذكره الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r18.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r18.claim: Another view defines the group as sixty men.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r19.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r19.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the group numbers six or seven.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r19.anchor: وقال سعيد ابن جبير: ست أو سبع

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r20.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r20.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd defines ʿuṣba as three to nine, equivalent to nafar.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r20.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: ما بين الثلاثة والتسعة وهو النفر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r21.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r21.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say ʿuṣba means ten, citing Joseph’s brothers’ self-description.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#3/r21.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عشرة لقول إخوة يوسف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r1.speaker: خيثمة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r1.claim: Khaithama says the Gospel described Qarun’s keys on sixty richly marked white camels; each key was finger-sized and opened a treasure sufficient for Basra.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r1.anchor: وقال خيثمة: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون وقر ستين بغلا غراء محجلة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r2.claim: Mujahid says the keys were made of camel hide.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: كانت المفاتيح من جلود الإبل

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r3.claim: Another report says the keys were made of cowhide to make them lighter.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: من جلود البقر لتخف عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r4.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r4.claim: Al-Qushayri says seventy mules carried Qarun’s keys when he rode.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the number of mules carrying the keys as forty.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: على أربعين بغلا. وهو قول الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says mafātih here means Qarun’s containers.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r7.claim: Abu Salih says mafātih means the treasure stores themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r7.anchor: وكذا قال أبو صالح: إن المراد بالمفاتح الخزائن

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r8.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the people who admonished Qarun as believing Israelites.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r8.anchor: أي المؤمنون من بني إسرائيل قاله السدي

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r9.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam identifies Qarun’s “people” here as Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r9.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام: القوم هنا موسى

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r10.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the plural qawm can refer to one person, as in the verse about “the people” who spoke, meaning Nuʿaym ibn Masʿud.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: وهو جمع أريد به واحد كقوله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r11.claim: Here lā tafraḥ means do not exult arrogantly or act insolently.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r12.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r12.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain al-fariḥīn as the arrogant.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r13.claim: A poem uses mufrāḥ for one who is not excessively elated when fortune favors him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r13.anchor: ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني ولا ضارع في صرفه المتقلب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r14.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qarun is told not to rejoice in wealth because such joy does not lead him to fulfill its due.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r14.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى لا تفرح بالمال فإن الفرح بالمال لا يؤدي حقه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r15.speaker: مبشر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r15.claim: Mubashir ibn ʿAbd Allah interprets lā tafraḥ as “do not corrupt”.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r15.anchor: قال مبشر بن عبد الله: لا تفرح لا تفسد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r16.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r16.claim: Abu ʿAmr says afraḥahu al-dayn means debt weighed him down, citing a poem about burdensome deposits.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r16.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: أفرحه الدين أثقله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r17.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r17.claim: Al-Zajjaj says al-fariḥīn and al-fāriḥīn mean the same thing.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r18.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r18.claim: Al-Farraʾ distinguishes the forms: al-fariḥīn are presently joyful, while al-fāriḥīn will rejoice later.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r18.anchor: وفرق بينهما الفراء فقال: معنى الفرحين الذين هم في حال فرح

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r19.claim: The Qur’anic phrase “you are dying and they are dying” contradicts al-Farraʾ’s analogy between mayyit and māʾit.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r19.anchor: ويدل على خلاف ما قال قول الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r20.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r20.claim: Mujahid also interprets lā tafraḥ as “do not transgress,” and al-fariḥīn as aggressors.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r20.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: معنى { لا تفرح } لا تبغ

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r21.speaker: ابن بحر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r21.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the warning as “do not be miserly,” since God does not love misers.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r21.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: لا تبخل إن الله لا يحب الباخلين
